On a success, you gain the ability to use one of the following Metamagic options as a sorcerer for the next minute, requiring no sorcery points. The type of Metamagic you gain access to depends on the type of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, and once you use it, you can't use it again until you inhale {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} again.
Red suude allows you to use the {@optfeature Distant Spell|PHB} Metamagic option.

item.name: Tinkertop Boltblaster 1000
entries: This strange contraption of gears, wires, and lacquered wood has a handle with a metal grip and crank. Its stock bears a flamboyant maker's mark that reads: "Made in Hupperdook," a city in {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount}. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon, you can immediately make another attack with this weapon after resolving the critical hit. When you roll a 1 on an attack roll made with this weapon, you must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} piercing damage as some of its gears and wires spring loose.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When the Titanstone Knuckles reach an awakened state, they gain the following properties:

items: Your Strength score becomes 24.

You can use an action to cast the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell from the gauntlets on yourself (enlarge only), with a duration of 10 minutes. This property of the gauntlets can't be used again until you finish a long rest.

item.name: Titanstone Knuckles (Dormant)
entries: Carved from the heartstone of a slain earth primordial, these gauntlets bestow immeasurable might to their wearer. In recent times, they were wielded by the legendary barbarian {@creature Grog Strongjaw|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, who continues to use them as he seeks worthy challengers across Tal'Dorei and Exandria.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While the Titanstone Knuckles are in a dormant state, your Strength score becomes 22 while you wear these gauntlets. Additionally, your weapon attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When the Titanstone Knuckles reach an exalted state, they gain the following properties:

items: Your Strength score becomes 26.
While you are under the effect of the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell cast by the gauntlets, you have resistance to cold, fire, lightning, and thunder damage.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When Whisper reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +2. Additionally, when you hit with an attack using this dagger, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} psychic damage.
The DC to resist being {@condition frightened} from a critical hit increases to 15.

item.name: Whisper (Dormant)
entries: Forged with a mercurial metal accidentally drawn from the Realms Beyond, this dagger shimmers with an unsettling sourceless light. It was once wielded by {@creature Champion of Ravens|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Vax'ildan, a legendary champion of the Matron of Ravens}. Two raven feathers are linked to its pommel as a memento of its former bearer.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While Whisper is in a dormant state, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Additionally, when you score a critical hit with this dagger, the target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. On a success, the target is immune to this effect for 24 hours.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When Whisper reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +3, and the extra psychic damage it deals increases to {@dice 1d8}.
The DC to resist being {@condition frightened} from a critical hit increases to 17.

When this dagger is used to make a ranged attack, you can choose to transform into shadow and merge with the blade as part of the action used to attack, teleporting to another location. If the attack hits, you appear in an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of the target. If the attack misses, you appear where the GM determines the dagger lands (typically within {@dice 1d6 × 5} feet of the target). In either case, you appear with the dagger in your hand.

item.name: Whitestone
entries: The sheer amount of leftover arcane power within the whitestone of the {@book Alabaster Sierra|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Alabaster Sierras} mountains is incredibly receptive to enchantment. Magic items that incorporate at least an ounce of whitestone into their construction require only one-quarter the creation time of other magic items. Some alchemists in {@book Emon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship} have discovered that dissolving whitestone with specific acids can leave behind pure {@item residuum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, which can substitute for expensive spell components when such materials are not readily available.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When the Wraps of Dyamak reach an awakened state, they gain the following properties:

items: The bonus to attack and damage rolls with your unarmed strike increases to +2.

You can cast the {@spell misty step} spell from the wraps as a bonus action, vanishing in a cloud of crimson mist. This property of the wraps can't be used again until you finish a short or long rest, or until you score a critical hit with an unarmed strike against a hostile creature.

item.name: Wraps of Dyamak (Dormant)
entries: Created and wielded by the ancient warrior-monk Dyamak, these thick strips of enchanted cloth are stained to appear dark crimson with blood of unknown origin. The current resting place of the wraps is unknown.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: When the Wraps of Dyamak are in a dormant state, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with your unarmed strike while wearing them.
In addition, when you finish a short or long rest, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your total number of ki points.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When the Wraps of Dyamak reach an exalted state, they gain the following properties:

items: The bonus to attack and damage rolls with your unarmed strike increases to +3.

When you hit with an unarmed strike, you can choose to make the attack a ravenous strike. The target takes an extra {@damage 6d6} necrotic damage, and you regain hit points equal to the amount of necrotic damage dealt. This property of the wraps can't be used again until you finish a long rest, or until you score a critical hit with an unarmed strike against a hostile creature.

item.name: Writing Kit
entries: Includes:

items: a {@item pouch|PHB|small pouch}
a quill
{@item Ink (1-ounce bottle)|PHB|ink}
{@item Parchment (one sheet)|PHB|folded parchment}
a penknife

item.name: Zeal
entries: Distilled from the ichor of demons, {@item zeal|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} was originally used by Tal'Dorei's ancient berserkers to grant them incredible strength and courage before battles. These days, it's most commonly used by criminal bruisers before a brawl. Most modern warriors stay well away from {@item zeal|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, due both to its addictive nature and to the mental and physical degeneration it can cause over long periods of time. When prepared properly, {@item zeal|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} is a purple, ashy-tasting gel that typically costs 150 gp per dose.

After slathering {@item zeal|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} across your exposed skin as an action, you must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you become {@condition paralyzed} for {@dice 1d4} rounds as your muscles lock up. On a success, your weapon attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d6} damage for the next minute. After this effect ends, you gain one level of {@condition exhaustion}.

feat.name: Acuity
entries: A drive for perfection may be futile, but not fruitless. The precision you act with grants you an advantage over your opponents:

items: Your critical hit range increases by 1 for attack rolls. Apply this after any features that may improve your critical hit range.

feat.name: Spell Sniper
entries: You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled.
Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.
Your ranged spell attacks for leveled spells gain a +2 to their attack rolls.

You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll. Choose the cantrip from the {@filter bard|spells|level=0|class=bard|spell attack=m;r;o}, {@filter cleric|spells|level=0|class=cleric|spell attack=m;r;o}, {@filter druid|spells|level=0|class=druid|spell attack=m;r;o}, {@filter sorcerer|spells|level=0|class=sorcerer|spell attack=m;r;o}, {@filter warlock|spells|level=0|class=warlock|spell attack=m;r;o}, or {@filter wizard|spells|level=0|class=wizard|spell attack=m;r;o} spell list. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the spell list you chose from: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

feat.name: Charger
entries: When you use an action to Dash, you can make one melee weapon attack or shove a creature as part of the same action.

If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before making this attack, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).

feat.name: Wakeful
entries: A life of diligence allows you to do more. Less time asleep allows for more time to accomplish your goals. Long rests take half as long to finish (to a minimum of 4 hours) as well as short rests.

feat.name: Versatile Weapons Master
entries: You have become a master of adaptation by training with handling and grips of weapons. While you wield a Versatile weapon with two hands or with one hand and nothing in the other, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain +1 AC.
You can make an attack with the Versatile weapon as a bonus action.

feat.name: Parlor Trickster
entries: You don't need a university's worth of magic, just a little to ease your life and impress others doing it. You learn to use four Cantrips that dont deal damage. The spellcasting modifier for them is your choice of Charisma, Intelligence or Wisdom

feat.name: Master of Armaments
entries: You are a master of weapons. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can choose any of the kinds of Mastery weapons you’re using and replace the Mastery property of each with another Mastery property.

The chosen kind of weapon must qualify for the new property. For example, you could replace the Longsword’s Sap property with the Push property. These property changes apply only for you, not for others, and the changes end for you when you finish your next Long Rest.
You may refer to the {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} table for the qualifications of each weapon type.

feat.name: Weapon Master
entries: You have learnt to hone on certain qualities of weapons, yielding new abilities. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can use the Mastery property of two kinds of Simple or Martial melee weapons of your choice, such as Greatswords and Shortswords. At the end of a Long Rest, you may change one of those weapon choices.

feat.name: Weapon Enthusiast
entries: You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits:

items: You become proficient in the use of 4 Exotic Weapons of your choice.

feat.name: Heavy Armor Master
entries: You feel encumbered no more when donning heavy armour. It has become a second skin to you, granting you the following benefits:

items: While you are wearing heavy armour, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from attacks is reduced by your proficiency bonus.

feat.name: Thrown Weapon Expert
entries: You've specialized in the casting of weapons and can now throw them in quick succession.

items: You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.
When you use your action to make a melee attack, you can use you bonus action to make a thrown weapon attack with a light weapon.
When you use your action to make a thrown weapon attack, you can use your bonus action to make another thrown weapon attack.
Long range does not impose disadvantage on thrown weapon attacks.

feat.name: Skirmisher
entries: You've gotten pretty good at surviving in sticky situations and wedging yourself out of them.

items: You can disengage using a bonus action
Your Movement increases by 5 feet
While wielding ranged weapons that don't possess the Heavy property you get +1 AC.

feat.name: Athlete
entries: You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Athletics} skill. If you already have proficiency, you gain expertise instead.
When you are {@condition prone}, you can stand up without using any additional movement.
Your movement speed cannot be reduced by non-magical means, including non-magical difficult terrain
You gain a climbing and a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10 feet.

feat.name: Bountiful Luck

choose.entry: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries: Your people have extraordinary luck, which you have learned to mystically lend to your companions when you see them falter. You're not sure how you do it; you just wish it, and it happens. Surely a sign of fortune's favor!

When an ally you can see within 60 feet of you rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to let the ally reroll the die. The ally must use the new roll.
When you use this ability, you can't use your Lucky racial trait before the start of your next turn.

feat.name: Dragon Hide
entries: You manifest scales and claws reminiscent of your draconic ancestors. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your scales harden. While you aren't wearing armor, you can calculate your AC as 13 + your Dexterity or Constitution (your choice) modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

You grow retractable claws from the tips of your fingers. Extending or retracting the claws requires no action. The claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal slashing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier, instead of the normal bludgeoning damage for an unarmed strike.

You can make a single claw attack as a bonus action if you have taken the attack action on your turn. Additionally, you gain a bonus to the claws damage equal to your proficiency bonus when attacking a creature who has been affected by a breath weapon within the last round.

feat.name: Gift of the Chromatic Dragon
entries: You've manifested some of the power of chromatic dragons, granting you the following benefits:

items.name: Chromatic Infusion
entries: As a bonus action, you can touch a {@filter simple or martial weapon|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=martial weapon;simple weapon} and infuse it with one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. For the next minute, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type when it hits. After you use this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

items.name: Reactive Resistance
entries: When you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to that instance of damage. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Gift of the Gem Dragon
entries: You've manifested some of the power of gem dragons, granting you the following benefits:

items.name: Telekinetic Reprisal
entries: When you take damage from a creature that is within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to emanate telekinetic energy. The creature that dealt damage to you must make a Strength saving throw (DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 2d8} force damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed. Additionally, you gain temporary hitpoints equal to the damage dealt. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Gift of the Metallic Dragon
entries: You've manifested some of the power of metallic dragons, granting you the following benefits:

items.name: Draconic Healing
entries: You learn the {@spell cure wounds} spell. You can cast this spell without expending a spell slot. Once you cast this spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast this spell using spell slots you have. The spell's spellcasting ability is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma when you cast it with this feat (choose when you gain the feat).

items.name: Protective Wings
entries: You can manifest protective wings that can shield you or others. When you or another creature you can see within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to manifest spectral wings from your back for a moment. You grant a bonus to the target's AC equal to your proficiency bonus against that attack roll. If it causes the attack to miss, you may make a single weapon attack as part of the same reaction. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Drow High Magic
entries: You learn more of the magic typical of dark elves. You learn the {@spell detect magic} spell and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot. You also learn {@spell levitate} and {@spell dispel magic}, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast those two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spell's spellcasting ability is Charisma.

feat.name: Durable
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Defy Death
entries: You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws.

entries.name: Speedy Recovery
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice, roll the die, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll.

feat.name: Dwarven Fortitude
entries: You have the blood of dwarf heroes flowing through your veins. You gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever you take the {@action Dodge} action in combat, you can spend one Hit Die to heal yourself. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1). Additionally, you can make a single weapon attack as a bonus action whenever you take the {@action Dodge} action.

feat.name: Fade Away
entries: Your people are clever, with a knack for illusion magic. You have learned a magical trick for fading away when you suffer harm. You gain the following benefits:

items: Immediately after you take damage, you can use a reaction to magically become {@condition invisible} until the end of your next turn or until you attack, deal damage, or force someone to make a saving throw. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Fey Teleportation
entries: Your study of high elven lore has unlocked fey power that few other elves possess, except your eladrin cousins. Drawing on your fey ancestry, you can momentarily stride through the Feywild to shorten your path from one place to another. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn to speak, read, and write {@language Sylvan}.

You learn the {@spell misty step} spell and one other {@filter 1st-level spell|spells|level=1|class=wizard} of your choice. the {@filter 1st-level spell|spells|level=1|class=wizard} must be from the Wizard spell list. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability when you cast these spells.

feat.name: Flames of Phlegethos
entries: You learn to call on hellfire to serve your commands. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll fire damage for a spell you cast, you can reroll any roll of 1 on the fire damage dice, but you must use the new roll, even if it is another 1.

Whenever you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can cause flames to wreathe you until the end of your next turn. The flames don't harm you or your possessions, and they shed bright light out to 30 feet and dim light for an additional 30 feet. While the flames are present, any creature that moves within 5 feet of you or hits you with a melee attack takes {@damage 1d8} fire damage.

feat.name: Grappler
entries: You've developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close-quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on grapple checks
You do not suffer a penalty to your movement speed when dragging a creature whose size is equal to or smaller than yours.

If the grappled creature is pushed away from your grapple through forced movement (such as through a {@spell thunderwave} spell, you can use your reaction to hold on to the creature. To do so, make another grapple check. You maintain your hold on the creature on a successful check.

You can attempt to grapple a creature whose size is two levels larger than you. When you do so, you make your grapple check with disadvantage. If you successfully grapple the creature, it's speed is reduced by an amount equal to your strength or dex score (your choice, rounded up), and you are dragged with the creature when it moves.

feat.name: Heavily Armored
entries: You have trained to master the use of heavy armor, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and shields.
You can treat your strength score as if it were higher by 5 (up to a maximum of 25) for the purposes of heavy armor requirements, as well as when calculating your carry capacity.
You can don and doff heavy armor as an action.

feat.name: Inspiring Leader
entries: You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Wisdom/Charisma modifier, and is inspired. Until they take a short or long rest, they can choose to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. A creature can't gain temporary hit points or be inspired from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.

feat.name: Pyromancer
entries: You've gained the  ability to channel the purest form of the element. You gain the following beneits:

items: When you gain this feat, you gain resistance to fire damage.

Any fire damage you deal ignites creatures, giving them the {@hazard burning|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. Additionally, the burning condition deals {@dice 2d4} damage, and has disadvantage on saving throws against any of your spells that deal fire damage.

When you deal fire damage with a spell to a creature is immune to the chosen damage type, you can choose to temporarily suppress the immunity, treating it as resistance until the start of your next turn. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Cryomancer
entries: You've gained the  ability to channel the purest form of the element. You gain the following beneits:

items: When you gain this feat, you gain resistance to cold damage.

When you deal cold damage to a creature, they are frozen until the start of your next turn. A frozen creature has its movement speed reduced by 10 feet, and takes an additional {@dice 1d6} cold damage whenever it takes bludgeoning, slashing or piercing damage. If you land a critical hit with the spell, or the creature fails the saving throw by 5 or more, their movement speed is reduced to 0 instead. The creature loses the frozen condition if they take fire damage.

When you deal cold damage with a spell to a creature is immune to the chosen damage type, you can choose to temporarily suppress the immunity, treating it as resistance until the start of your next turn. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Acetomancer
entries: You've gained the  ability to channel the purest form of the element. You gain the following beneits:

items: When you gain this feat, you gain resistance to acid damage.

When you deal acid damage to a creature, they gain a stack of corrosion. A creature cannot gain more than 1 stack of corrosion on a round. A corroded creature has its Armor Class reduced by 1 for each stack of corrosion it has. The stacks last for 1 minute, or until the creature uses an action to scrape the acid off of itself.

When you deal acid damage with a spell to a creature is immune to the chosen damage type, you can choose to temporarily suppress the immunity, treating it as resistance until the start of your next turn. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Thunemancer
entries: You've gained the  ability to channel the purest form of the element. You gain the following beneits:

items: When you gain this feat, you gain resistance to Thunder damage.

When you deal thunder damage to a creature, they are Unsettled until the start of your next turn. An Unsettled creature has disadvantage on checks that require hearing, and cannot benefit on advantage on its attack rolls and ability checks.

When you deal thunder damage with a spell to a creature is immune to the chosen damage type, you can choose to temporarily suppress the immunity, treating it as resistance until the start of your next turn. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Fulmimancer
entries: You've gained the  ability to channel the purest form of the element. You gain the following beneits:

items: When you gain this feat, you gain resistance to Lightning damage.

When you deal lightning damage to a creature, they are Jolted. A Jolted creature cannot take reactions, and only gains half the benefit from abilities that increase the creature's movement speed (such as the {@action dash} action).

When you deal lightning damage with a spell to a creature is immune to the chosen damage type, you can choose to temporarily suppress the immunity, treating it as resistance until the start of your next turn. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a long rest.

feat.name: Ritual Caster
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ritual Spells
entries: Choose a number of level 1 spells equal to your Proficiency Bonus that have the {@filter Ritual tag|spells|level=1|components & miscellaneous=ritual}. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them with any spell slots you have. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat. Whenever your Proficiency Bonus increases thereafter, you can add an additional level 1 spell with the Ritual tag to the spells always prepared with this feature.

entries.name: Quick Ritual
entries: With this benefit, you can cast a Ritual spell that you have prepared using its regular casting time rather than the extended time for a Ritual. Doing so doesn't require a spell slot. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can do so a number of times equal to the modifier of the attribute increased when you pick this feat.

feat.name: Mystic Empowerment
entries: You have trained to more efficiently channel magical energy into your spell. You gain the following benefits.

items: You gain two focus charges when you take this feat, regaining one charge on a short rest and both charges on a long rest. You can spend focus charges in the following ways:

items.name: Destructive Focus
entries: When you cast a spell that deals damage, you can spend a focus charge to increase its damage die type in the following way: (d4->d6, d6->d8, d8->d10, d10->d12, d12->3d4).

items.name: Rejuvenating Focus
entries: When you cast a spell that recovers hit-points, you can expend a focus charge to roll the maximum amount on the healing die for no more than two of the creatures healed.

items.name: Exact Focus
entries: When you miss an attack roll with a spell, you can expend a focus charge to add a bonus to the attack roll equal to your proficiency bonus.

items.name: Stalwart Focus
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, you can spend a focus charge to give yourself a bonus equal to your proficiency bonus on concentration checks for that spell.

items.name: Potent Focus
entries: When you cast a leveled spell, you can spend a focus charge to cast the spell as if the spell slot expended was of one higher level.

feat.name: Festering Condition
entries: Conditions you inflict grow more and more potent the longer a creature is affected by them. The condition festers after the creature has been affected by the original condition for one turn, applying a more debilitating condition for the duration of the original condition, and is lost whenever the original condition ends. The condition festers as shown in the table below:

feat.name: Lightly Armored
entries: You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with light armor.
your speed increases by 10 feet when wearing light armor.
Opportunity against you are made at disadvantage.

feat.name: Linguist
entries: You have studied languages and codes, gaining the following benefits:

items: You learn four languages of your choice.

You can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.

You have a +5 bonus to checks when trying to decipher codes. Additionally, you can make out the general meaning of messages when reading languages you don't understand, as long as you know a language that uses the same script.

feat.name: Mage Slayer
entries: You have practiced techniques useful in melee combat against spellcasters, gaining the following benefits:

items: When a creature within your reach casts a spell, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature. If you hit, the creature must make a constitution saving throw as if it were concentrating on the spell. If it fails, the spell is lost and the creature's action is wasted.

When you damage a creature that is {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on saving throws it makes to maintain its {@status concentration} until the end of your next turn.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creatures whom you have dealt damage to within your last turn.

feat.name: Magic Initiate
entries: Choose a class: {@filter bard|spells|level=0;1|class=bard}, {@filter cleric|spells|level=0;1|class=cleric}, {@filter druid|spells|level=0;1|class=druid}, {@filter sorcerer|spells|level=0;1|class=sorcerer}, {@filter warlock|spells|level=0;1|class=warlock}, or {@filter wizard|spells|level=0;1|class=wizard}. You learn two cantrips of your choice from that class's spell list.

In addition, choose one 1st-level spell to learn from that same list. Using this feat, you can cast the spell once at its lowest level, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again.  You can also cast the spell using spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

Your spellcasting ability for these spells depends on the class you chose: Charisma for {@filter bard|spells|level=0;1|class=bard}, {@filter sorcerer|spells|level=0;1|class=sorcerer}, or {@filter warlock|spells|level=0;1|class=warlock}; Wisdom for {@filter cleric|spells|level=0;1|class=cleric} or {@filter druid|spells|level=0;1|class=druid}; or Intelligence for {@filter wizard|spells|level=0;1|class=wizard}.

feat.name: Martial Adept
entries: You have martial training that allows you to perform special combat maneuvers. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn two {@filter maneuvers|optionalfeatures|feature type=MV:B} of your choice from among those available to the {@class fighter|phb|Battle Master|Battle Master|phb|2-0} archetype in the fighter class. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

You gain two superiority dice, which are a {@dice d6} (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

feat.name: Medium Armor Master
entries: You have practiced moving in medium armor to gain the following benefits:

items: Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks.
When you wear medium armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.

feat.name: Observant
entries: Quick to notice details of your environment, you gain the following benefits:

items: If you can see a creature's mouth while it is speaking a language you understand, you can interpret what it's saying by reading its lips.
You have a +5 bonus to Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and passive Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) scores.
you have advantage on checks you make to identify traps, hidden doors, and other hidden compartments.

feat.name: Orcish Fury
entries: Your fury burns tirelessly. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you hit with an attack using a {@filter simple or martial weapon|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=martial weapon;simple weapon}, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice an additional time and add it as extra damage of the weapon's damage type. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses on a short or long rest.
Your Relentless Endurance trait can now be used once per short rest.

feat.name: Prodigy
entries: You have a knack for learning new things. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain one {@table skills|phb|skill proficiency} of your choice, one {@filter tool proficiency|items|type=tool;artisan's tools} of your choice, and fluency in one language of your choice.

Choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. The skill you choose must be one that isn't already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.

feat.name: Savage Attacker
entries: when you hit a target with an unarmed strike or a weapon attack, you can roll damage for it twice and use either total.

feat.name: Ambusher
entries: You have learnt the ways of assassination and covertness, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks and Initiative rolls.
You can use the {@action Hide} action as a bonus action.
You do not break stealth when you make an attack with a silent weapon, as long as you move after you make the attack and before you end your turn.
You deal an additional {@damage 1d8} damage when you land an attack on a creature who hasn't taken a turn in combat.

feat.name: Second Chance
entries: Fortune favors you when someone tries to strike you. You gain the following benefits:

items: When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force that creature to attack another creature or waste the attack. You can use this ability twice, regaining its use when you roll initiative at the start of combat or finish a short or long rest.

feat.name: Cartomancer
entries: You have learned to channel your magic through a deck of cards. You can use a card deck as your spellcasting focus, and you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Card Tricks
entries: You learn the {@spell Prestidigitation} cantrip and can use it to create illusions that duplicate the effects of stage magic. When you use {@spell Prestidigitation} in this way, you can conceal the verbal and somatic components of the spell as ordinary conversation and card handling.

items.name: Hidden Ace
entries: When you finish a long rest, you can choose one spell from your class's spell list and imbue that spell into a card. The chosen spell must have a casting time of 1 action, and it must be a level for which you have spell slots (maximum of level 5). The card remains imbued with this spell for 8 hours. While the card is imbued with the spell, you can use a bonus action to flourish the card and cast the spell within. The card then immediately loses its magic.

feat.name: Sharpshooter
entries: You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits:

items: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.
Your ranged weapon attacks ignore {@quickref Cover||3||half cover} and {@quickref Cover||3||three-quarters cover}.
Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

feat.name: Great Weapon Master
entries: You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits:

items: On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action.
Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

feat.name: Martial Artist
entries: You have trained yourself in martial arts. You gain the following benefits

items: You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes, and they deal {@dice 1d6} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier damage on a hit (Your choice). If you aren't wielding any weapons or a {@item shield|phb} when you make the attack roll, the {@dice 1d6} becomes a {@dice 1d8}.
You gain 2 Ki points, which replenish whenever you finish a short or long rest.
You gain the following abilites which are fueled by your Ki points:

items.name: Flurry of Blows:
entries: You can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.

items.name: Patient Defense:
entries: You can expend 1 Ki Point to take both the {@action Disengage|XPHB} and the {@action Dodge|XPHB} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Step of the Wind
entries: You can expend 1 Ki Point to take both the {@action Disengage|XPHB} and {@action Dash|XPHB} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

feat.name: Skill Expert
entries: You have honed your proficiency with particular skills, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in two {@table skills|phb|skills} or {@filter tool proficiency|items|type=tool;artisan's tools} of your choice.

Choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. The skill you choose must be one that isn't already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.

feat.name: Skilled
entries: You gain proficiency in any combination of four {@table skills|phb} or {@filter tools|items|type=tools;artisan's tools;instrument;gaming set;vehicle (land);vehicle (water)} of your choice.

feat.name: Skulker
entries: You are expert at slinking through shadows. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding.
When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.
you gain {@sense darkvision} up to a range of 120 feet. If you already have darkvision from another source, its range is increased by 60 feet.
Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks relying on sight.

feat.name: Squat Nimbleness
entries: You are uncommonly nimble for your race. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your walking speed by 5 feet.
You have  advantage on saving throws against being {@condition prone}, and can get up from being prone by expending only 5 feet of movement.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Acrobatics} or {@skill Athletics} skill (your choice).
You have advantage on any Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check you make to escape from being {@condition grappled}.

feat.name: Wood Elf Magic
entries: You learn the magic of the primeval woods, which are revered and protected by your people. You learn one druid cantrip of your choice. You also learn the {@spell longstrider} and {@spell pass without trace} spells, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast these two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for all three spells.

feat.name: Actor
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Impersonation
entries: While you're disguised as a real or fictional person, you have Advantage on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks to convince others that you are that person.

entries.name: Mimicry
entries: You can mimic the sounds of other creatures, including speech. A creature that hears the mimicry must succeed on a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check to determine the effect is faked (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and Proficiency Bonus).

feat.name: Chef
entries: Time spent mastering the culinary arts has paid off, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item cook's utensils|phb} if you don't already have it.

As part of a short rest, you can cook special food, provided you have ingredients and {@item cook's utensils|phb} on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 + your proficiency bonus. At the end of the short rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points regains an extra {@dice 1d8} hit points.

With one hour of work or when you finish a long rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your proficiency bonus. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats to gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

feat.name: Lucky
entries: You have inexplicable luck that seems to kick in at just the right moment.

You have 3 luck points. Whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can spend one luck point to roll an additional {@dice d20}. You can choose to spend one of your luck points after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You choose which of the {@dice d20}s is used for the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

You can also spend one luck point when an attack roll is made against you. Roll a {@dice d20}, and then choose whether the attack uses the attacker's roll or yours. If more than one creature spends a luck point to influence the outcome of a roll, the points cancel each other out; no additional dice are rolled.
You regain your expended luck points when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Revenant Blade
entries: You are descended from a master of the {@item double-bladed scimitar|ERLW}, and some of that mastery has passed on to you. You gain the following benefits:

items: While you are holding a double-bladed scimitar with two hands, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.
A double-bladed scimitar has the finesse property when you wield it.

feat.name: Telepathic
entries: You awaken the ability to mentally connect with others, granting you the following benefits:

items: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Your telepathic utterances are in a language you know, and the creature understands you only if it knows that language.

You can cast the {@spell detect thoughts} spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. Your spellcasting ability for the spell is the ability increased by this feat. If you have spell slots of 2nd level or higher, you can cast this spell with them.

feat.name: Aberrant Precision
entries: Your unique training method gives you accuracy only matched by the greatest of elves. You have uncanny aim with attacks that rely on precision rather than brute force. You gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever you have advantage on an attack roll using Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can reroll one of the dice once.

feat.name: Keen Mind
entries: You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision. You gain the following benefits:

items: You always know which way is north.
You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.
You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

Choose one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, or {@skill Religion|XPHB}. If you lack proficiency in the chosen skill, you gain proficiency in it, and if you already have proficiency in it, you gain Expertise in it.

feat.name: Dungeon Delver
entries: Alert to the hidden traps and secret doors found in many dungeons, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks made to detect the presence of secret doors.
You have evasion against damage from traps.
Traveling at a fast pace doesn't impose the normal -5 penalty on your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score.

feat.name: Eldritch Adept
entries: Studying occult lore, you learn one {@filter Eldritch Invocation|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=EI} option of your choice from the warlock class. Your spellcasting ability for the invocation is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (choose when you select this feat). If the invocation has a prerequisite of any kind, you can choose that invocation only if you're a warlock who meets the prerequisite.
Whenever you gain a level, you can replace the invocation with another one from the warlock class.

feat.name: Metamagic Adept
entries: You've learned how to exert your will on your spells to alter how they function:

items: You learn two {@filter Metamagic|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=MM} options of your choice from the sorcerer class. You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless the option says otherwise. Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one of these Metamagic options with another one from the sorcerer class.

You gain 2 sorcery points to spend on Metamagic (these points are added to any sorcery points you have from another source but can be used only on Metamagic). You regain all spent sorcery points when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Mystic conflux

choose.entry: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries: Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can attune to up to four magic items at once.
you can cast the {@spell identify} spell without expending a spell slot or material components. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

feat.name: Spelldriver

choose.entry: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries: Through intense focus, training, and dedication, you've harnessed the techniques of rapid spellcasting.

When you use your bonus action to cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also use your action to cast another spell of 1st level or higher. However, if you cast two or more spells in a single turn, only one of them can be 3rd level or higher.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Casting Multiple Spells
entries: Normally, when you cast a spell as a bonus action, you can't use your action to also cast a spell that turn unless that spell is a cantrip—{@note see {@book PHB p202|PHB|10|Bonus Action}.} The Spelldriver feat removes that restriction, but the focus necessary to channel multiple spells in the same round still limits the overall power of those spells.

feat.name: Elemental Adept
entries: When you gain this feat, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.

Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll a 1 or a 2 on a damage die for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can reroll the damage dice and must use the new roll.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.

feat.name: Cruel
entries: The challenges and struggles you've faced throughout your life have led you to delight in inflicting pain and anguish upon others. You gain a number of cruelty dice equal to your proficiency bonus. Your cruelty dice are {@dice d6|d6s}. You can roll only one cruelty die per turn, and a cruelty die is spent when you roll it.
You can roll a cruelty die under any of the following circumstances, with the indicated result:

items: When you deal damage to a creature, spend one cruelty die to deal extra damage to the creature equal to the roll.
When you score a critical hit, spend one cruelty die to gain temporary hit points equal to the roll.
When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check, spend one cruelty die and add the roll to your check.

entries: You regain all spent cruelty dice when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Flash Recall
entries: You've developed the ability to instantly recall an unprepared spell in moments of sudden necessity.

As a bonus action, you prepare a spell of 1st level or higher from your spellbook (if you're a {@class wizard}) or from your class spell list (if you're not a {@class wizard}). This spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it replaces another spell of an equal or higher level that you had previously prepared.
Once you use this feat to recall a spell, you can't do so again until you complete a short or long rest.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Prepared Spells
entries: The Flash Recall feat requires you to be a spellcaster who prepares spells. This includes classes such as {@class cleric||clerics}, {@class druid||druids}, and {@class paladin||paladins}, who prepare spells each day from their class list, and {@class wizard||wizards}, who prepare spells from a spellbook. Classes such as {@class bard||bards} and {@class sorcerer||sorcerers}, who inherently know their spells rather than preparing them, can't benefit from this feat.

feat.name: Mystic Conflux
entries: You possess an intuitive understanding of the way magic ebbs and flows within enchanted items. Such items attune easily to you, and you are able to sound out their secrets. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can attune to up to four magic items at once.
You can cast the {@spell identify} spell without expending a spell slot or material components. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

feat.name: Remarkable Recovery
entries: Your body has the ability to recover quickly from terrible injuries, and is unusually receptive to healing magic. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you are successfully stabilized while dying, you regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
Whenever you regain hit points as a result of a spell, potion, or class feature (but not this feat), you regain additional hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

feat.name: Spelldriver
entries: Through intense focus, training, and dedication, you've harnessed the techniques of rapid spellcasting.

When you use your bonus action to cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also use your action to cast another spell of 1st level or higher. However, if you cast two or more spells in a single turn, only one of them can be 3rd level or higher.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Casting Multiple Spells
entries: Normally, when you cast a spell as a bonus action, you can't use your action to also cast a spell that turn unless that spell is a cantrip—{@note see {@book PHB p202|PHB|10|Bonus Action}.} The Spelldriver feat removes that restriction, but the focus necessary to channel multiple spells in the same round still limits the overall power of those spells.

feat.name: Thrown Arms Master
entries: You've honed your ability to lob weaponry into the fray, including weapons not meant for ranged combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: Simple and martial melee weapons without the thrown property have the {@itemProperty T|PHB|thrown} property for you. One-handed weapons have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, while two-handed weapons have a normal range of 15 feet and a long range of 30 feet.
Weapons that already have the {@itemProperty T|PHB|thrown} property increase their short range by 20 feet and their long range by 40 feet for you.

When you miss with a thrown weapon attack using a light weapon, the weapon returns to your grasp like a boomerang at the end of your turn, unless something prevents it from returning. You can catch and stow as many weapons as you threw in this way.

feat.name: Vital Sacrifice
entries: You've learned secrets of hemocraft that grant you esoteric power at the price of your own life force. As a bonus action, you can choose to take {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage to gain a blood boon. Your blood boon lasts for 1 hour or until expended.
You can expend this blood boon to gain one of the following benefits:

items: When you make an attack roll, you roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the total.
When you hit with an attack or spell, you deal an additional {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage.
When you cause a creature to make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, roll a {@dice d4} and reduce their save by the amount rolled.

entries: The damage you take to gain a blood boon can't be reduced in any way.

reward.name: Boon of High Magic
entries: You gain an additional spell slot that recovers on a long rest. The level of the spell slot is equal to the highest level spell slot that you can use.

reward.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
entries: You add your proficiency bonus to your damage rolls with unarmed strikes and weapons that you are proficient with.

You add a bonus equal to your proficiency bonus to any saving throw you force on a creature through a weapon attack (weapon masteries, battlemaster maneuvers, rogue cunning strike, paladin spell smites, etc.).

reward.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blink Steps
entries: Immediately after you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action or the {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

reward.name: Boon of Energy resistance
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Energy Resistances
entries: You gain Resistance to two of the following damage types of your choice: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your choices.

entries.name: Energy Redirection
entries: When you take damage of one of the types chosen for the Energy Resistances benefit, you can take a Reaction to direct damage of the same type toward another creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that isn't behind Total Cover. If you do so, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take damage equal to {@dice 2d12} plus your Constitution modifier.

reward.name: Boon of Fate
entries: When another creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an ability check, an attack roll, or a saving throw, you can roll a {@dice 2d4} and apply the result as a bonus or penalty to the roll. Once you use this boon, you can't use it again until you roll initiative or finish a short rest or long rest.

reward.name: Boon of the Fire Soul
entries: You have immunity to fire damage. You can also cast {@spell burning hands} as a level 2 spell (DC 18 or your spell save dc) and {@spell scorching ray} (+10 or your spell attack roll) at will, without using a spell slot or any components.

reward.name: Boon of Fortitude
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fortified Health
entries: Your Hit Point maximum increases by 40. In addition, whenever you regain Hit Points, you can regain additional Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier. Once you've regained these additional Hit Points, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

reward.name: Boon of Immortality
entries: You stop aging. You are immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition, to diseases, as well as any effect that would age you, and you can't die from old age.

You have advantage on death saving throws. Additionally, you are instantly stabilised when you drop to 0 hitpoints. You can choose to keep rolling death saves as normal, coming back to life with 1 hitpoint when you roll a natural 20.

reward.name: Boon of Invincibility
entries: When you take damage from any source, you can reduce that damage to 0. Once you use this boon, you can't use it again until you finish a short rest.

reward.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
entries: You can bypass the damage resistances of any creature.

reward.name: Boon of Magic Resistance
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Once per long rest, when you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can choose to succeed instead.

reward.name: Boon of Peerless Aim
entries: When you miss with an unarmed strike or a weapon attack, you can choose to hit instead. Once you use this boon, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

reward.name: Boon of Perfect Health
entries: When you roll hit dice in order to regain hitpoints, you heal an amount equal to the roll + twice your constitution modifier, and you have advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.

reward.name: Boon of Planar Travel
entries: When you gain this boon, choose a plane of existence other than the Material Plane. You can now use an action to cast the {@spell plane shift} spell (no spell slot or components required), targeting yourself only, and travel to the chosen plane, or from that plane back to the Material Plane. Once you use this boon, you can't use it again until you finish a short rest.

reward.name: Boon of Quick Casting
entries: Choose one of your spells of 1st through 3rd level that has a casting time of 1 action. That spell's casting time is now 1 bonus action for you.

reward.name: Boon of Recovery
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Last Stand
entries: When you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead and regain a number of Hit Points equal to half your Hit Point maximum. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Recover Vitality
entries: You have a pool of ten d10s. As a Bonus Action, you can expend dice from the pool, roll those dice, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll's total. You regain all the expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

reward.name: Boon of Resilience
entries: You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

reward.name: Boon of Skill
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: All-Around Adept
entries: You gain proficiency in all skills.

entries.name: Expertise
entries: Choose one skill in which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in that skill.

reward.name: Boon of Speed
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Escape Artist
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action, which also ends the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition on you.

entries.name: Quickness
entries: Your Speed increases by 30 feet.

reward.name: Boon of Spell Mastery
entries: Choose one 1st or 2nd-level sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell that you can cast. You can now cast that spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot.

reward.name: Boon of Spell Recall
entries: You can cast any spell from your class spell list of level 6 or lower without expending a spell slot. Once you do so, you can't use this boon again until you finish a short or long rest.

reward.name: Boon of the Stormborn
entries: You have immunity to lightning and thunder damage. You can also cast {@spell thunderwave} (DC 18 or your spell save DC) as a level 2 spell and {@spell chromatic orb} (lightning only, +10 or your spell attack modifier) as a level 2 spell at will, without using a spell slot or any components.

reward.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Merge with Shadows
entries: While within Dim Light or Darkness, you can give yourself the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition as a Bonus Action. The condition ends on you immediately after you take an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction.

entries.name: Shadowy Form
entries: While within Dim Light or Darkness, you have Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Radiant.

reward.name: Boon of Truesight
entries: You have {@sense truesight} out to a range of 60 feet.

reward.name: Boon of Undetectability
entries: You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, and you can't be detected or targeted by {@filter divination|spells|school=D} magic, including scrying sensors.

dDRKult: (a) a {@item rapier|tct} or (b) a {@item shortsword|tct}
(a) an {@item arcane focus|tct} or (b) a {@item component pouch|tct}
(a) an {@item entertainer's pack|tct} or (b) a {@item scholar's pack|tct}
Two {@item dagger|tct|daggers}

fluff.name: The Mesmer
entries: In the heart of a bustling city, a cloaked figure dances through the shadows, their footsteps silent against the cobblestone. With a flick of their wrist, illusions spring to life, weaving a tapestry of deception that leaves onlookers in awe and adversaries in confusion.

Amidst the chaos of battle, a serene warrior stands untouched, their enemies bewildered as their strikes meet only mirages. With a gentle whisper, the Mesmer bends the perception of friend and foe alike, shaping the battlefield with an artist’s precision and a tactician’s cunning.

Mesmers are masters of illusion, manipulation, and mental magic, blurring the lines between reality and fantasy. While some spellcasters rely on brute force or elemental power, a Mesmer’s strength lies in subtlety and finesse, influencing the world around them with delicate, yet potent, manipulations of the mind.

entries.name: The Art of Illusion
entries: To a Mesmer, reality is but a canvas for their artistry. They craft illusions with such detail and depth that even the most discerning eye can be fooled. These illusions can protect allies, ensnare enemies, or simply beguile the senses. The most skilled Mesmers can make their illusions so convincing they can inflict physical harm, blurring the lines between the mental and the material.

entries.name: Mental Dominion
entries: Mesmers wield control over minds with unparalleled grace, manipulating memories, emotions, and perceptions. They can soothe the weary, inspire the despondent, or sow chaos among their enemies. This mental dominion extends to themselves, allowing Mesmers to maintain clarity in the face of confusion and resist attempts to ensnare their own minds.

entries.name: Creating a Mesmer
entries: When creating a Mesmer, consider how they discovered their unique talents. Were they born with an innate ability to perceive the fabric of reality differently, or did they learn their skills from a mentor, honing their craft through study and practice? Think about how your character uses their abilities - do they perform in grand theaters, deceive their way through political intrigue, or employ their skills in service of a greater cause?

Consider also your character’s attitude towards their powers. Do they view their illusions as an art form, a weapon, or a tool for change? How do they feel about the ethical implications of manipulating perception and memory?

entries.name: Quick Build
entries: You can quickly build a Mesmer by following these suggestions. First, Intelligence should be your highest ability score, followed by Charisma or Dexterity. Second, choose the {@spell minor illusion}, {@spell charm person}, and {@spell disguise self} cantrips to start embodying the Mesmer's capabilities in manipulating both mind and senses.

tools: One set of Artisan's Tools of your choice

(a) {@item light crossbow|phb} and {@item crossbow bolts (20)|phb|20 bolts} or (b) Two {@item dagger|phb|daggers}
One set of tools of your choice
{@item leather armor|phb} and {@item scholar's pack|phb}

(a) A dungeoneer's pack or (b) an entertainer's pack
(a) {@item dart|tct|20 darts} or (b) {@item dagger|tct|2 daggers}

fluff.name: Flickwrist
entries: A crowd gathers near the counter, eyes rapt with amazement as a man in rakish clothing bides their excitement by taking a swig of his flagon. He pauses a little. Then in a quick burst of motion, makes an elegant movement of his arm, Spinning his wrist and splays his fingers into a bystanders face as flames explode from his palm engulfing the woman's head in yellow fire. The panic from the crowd wanes when the woman gets up with not a single singed hair. He grins wide at the looks of astonishment and the excited murmurs.

A captain watches with stern disappointment as she guides the hands of her nervous subordinates as they repeatedly attempt to motion a swift and complex set of movements. Try as they might, they just appear to be flailing their arms fruitlessly. Just as she begins to contemplate retiring the training session. Her despair lifts a little when, in the distance, she spots a bolt of fire impacting a training dummy leaving smolders.

A man in strange foreign garb channels his rage into movement, controlled and serene. To his adventuring opponents he appears to be dancing but before he stops on a pose, a barrage of fire, lightning and ice seemingly erupt from his every limb, laying an elemental assault upon the inexperienced travelers.

It is quite rare to find one proficient in the arcane. Though it may come from a myriad sources, the gift of magic remains to be rare in most. Perhaps one toiled away in a tower, meditating on the many theories and equation he found in their books. Or perhaps one derives her power from her connection to nature or a deity. And then there are some who are merely born with arcane potential. Rarer still are those few who may perform grand arcane feats requiring great magic potential. Knowing this, one might be discouraged ever attempting to gain any semblance of arcane power for it would seem to be that magic is only harnessed by the extraordinary. Seemingly defiant of that notion, A Flickwrist is considered to be one who utilizes the lesser magics present within all in the form of their spelldance. Growing slowly in arcane ability but making up for it in utilizing it.

entries.name: Ex Laboris Arte
entries: Though some magic exists in everyone, to materialize and control it takes much practice. A Flickwrist translates their spells into movements that draw upon that innate power. It can be drawn from within through a basic grasp of the spell and controlled and swift gyrations. The translation of spell into movement, though easy for the mind, is difficult for the body to grasp. Adepts may come to realise that they are essentially speaking through motions but only masters are fluent enough to effectively express poetry through their motions as they reach a point where it is as if their body becomes capable of thinking for itself.

A Flickwrist will realize that it is not the spells that they are trying to master but their body. The energy present within is just the medium to that end. Through great dedication to their art they may achieve that and will be able to turn even this little speck of magic into a force wild and destructive in its capability.

entries.name: Ex Omnis Magia
entries: Flickwrists and Spelldancers can come from all walks of life. Perhaps they once saw their friend grow weeds from a wall with a mere wave of a hand. Or maybe one's mother had them tutored by a renowned spelldancer. Their curiosity is slowly replaced with a deep  passion for the art and the creation of something new. Their life thus revolves around the seeking of new inspirations for their craft or perhaps in the quest for its perfection.

When they set out for adventure they may do so seeking other spelldancers from foreign lands to observe their methods. Or perhaps they seek the chaos of battle where they may put their body to the test, seeing if it can act out of sheer instinct. Some may see nature itself as their muse and travel to distant, lurid lands to observe their environments in all its minutia from the gait of a river to the flight of a bee.

fluff.name: Flickwrist
entries: If you ask me, I think magic is safer with wizards and the like. Don't see them messing my tavern about.
-Theev Bolidnessos, Tavernkeep
