classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level,  you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM uses the optional Feats, you can instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Unparalleled Genius
entries: Upon reaching 20th level, you reach the true potential of your mind. Your Intelligence and Wisdom scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: As a Flickwrist your specialty is the learning and mastery of movement to cast Cantrips. As you progress through this class you will gain abilities that strengthen and quicken the casting of them.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 1st level, you know four cantrips of your choice from the {@filter wizard spell list|spells|level=0|class=wizard}, they count as Flickwrist cantrips. You learn additional wizard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Flickwrist table. You may replace a cantrip you know with with another from the wizard spell list when you gain a level in this class.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Flickwrist spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your wizard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. For example, if you know the 1st-level spell shield and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast shield using either slot.

entries.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
entries: At 1st level, You know three 1st-level {@filter wizard spells|spells|level=1|class=wizard} of your choice. The Spells Known column of the Flickwrist Spellcasting table shows when you learn more wizard spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the wizard spells you know with another spell of your choice from the wizard spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellasting Ability
entries: Dexterity is your spellcasting ability for casting spells. Your finesse in its casting determines the spells potency. You use your Dexterity whenever a Spell refers to your Spellcasting ability. You also use your Dexterity modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Flickwrist Cantrip you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an article of clothing or a worn accessory as a spellcasting focus.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: At 1st level, choose one of your skill proficiencies, a tool or musical instrument you're proficient with. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose one more of your proficiencies (in skills, tools or musical instruments) to gain this benefit.

classFeature.name: Choreurgic Art
entries: At the 2nd Level, You choose a school of spelldance to guide your movements. Your choice grants you different features at 6th, 10th and 14th Levels.

classFeature.name: Casting Style
entries: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of spellcasting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Casting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Elusion
entries: While you aren't wearing medium armour, heavy armour or shields, you gain a +1 to AC.

entries.name: Fluency
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged spell attacks.

entries.name: Potency
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to your spell save DCs for cantrips you cast.

entries.name: Deflection
entries: You can use your reaction to grant a creature within 5 feet of you advantage against a spells saving throw. You must have both your hands free.

entries.name: Spellbending
entries: Cantrips you cast ignore half and three-quarters cover. If there is and an unobstructed path of a length less than or equal to the range exists between you and the target behind total cover, it can be targeted by cantrips that require sight but the target has advantage on any of its saves and attack rolls against it will be at disadvantage.

entries.name: Close-Quarters Casting
entries: Being within 5 feet of an enemy does not impose disadvantage on ranged cantrips that you cast.

entries.name: Esotericism
entries: Choose 2 cantrips from the {@filter Druid|spells|level=0|class=Druid}, {@filter Cleric|spells|level=0|class=Cleric} or {@filter Bard|spells|level=0|class=Bard} spell lists and add it to the cantrips you know. They now count as Flickwrist cantrips but do not count towards your cantrips known limit.

entries.name: Stability
entries: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for a spell you cast, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.

classFeature.name: Choreurgic Masteries
entries: As you deepen your study of the Choreurgic arts, you begin to discover new intricacies to your step that change how you dance or the way you cast spells.

At the 3rd Level, you gain two Choreurgic Masteries of your choice from the list {@filter here|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=FW:CM}. They are powerful abilities that you gain throughout the course of this class as shown in the 'Masteries Known' table.
Additionally when you gain a mastery, you may replace one that you know for another that you meet the requirements for.

You may learn a mastery at the same time that you meet its requirements. If a mastery has a level requirement, you must be a Flickwrist of that level. If you change something about yourself such that you don't meet choreurgic mastery's prerequisites, the mastery and its effects are disabled until its prerequisites are met again or the mastery changed entirely.

classFeature.name: Potent Cantrip
entries: At the 3rd Level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
In additon, when a cantrip that requires a spell attack hits, you can add your Dexterity modifier to one damage roll of the attack.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Tachyurgy
entries: Beginning at 5th level, you can cast two cantrips, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action cast a spell} action on your turn.
Unless you have the Extra Attack feature, only one of those cantrips cast can involve a weapon attack.

classFeature.name: Augments

entries.name: Choreurgic Capacity & Repletion
entries: The amount of vigour slots a Flickwrist can store is his Choreurgic Capacity. When your character reaches the 5th, 11th and 17th level it goes up by one. Though Flickwrists can gain additional vigour slots at certain levels shown in the Flickwrist table.

During the course of a battle, spent vigour slots will recover at a certain rate. This rate is represented by your Choreurgic repletion. Your Character's level determines how many vigour slots he recovers.
It is 1 at 1st Level, then increases by 1 on the 5th, 11th and 17th level.
When you enter spelldance, you will recover an amount determined by your Choreurgic Repletion.
If you have entered spelldance by the time your turn ends, you will recover vigour slots according to your Choreurgic repletion.

At the 5th Level, You've learnt to channel the vigour within to perform various feats. When entering spelldance you can choose to spend some vigour slots to apply one augment to your spelldance. You learn to use two at this level and learn one more at 9th and 15th level.
When reaching a level in this class that grants a Feat or an ASI. you can choose to swap one of the Augments for another.

entries.name: Mummer's Dance
entries: The Flickwrist spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your wizard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. For example, if you know the 1st-level spell shield and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast shield using either slot.

entries.name: Zephyr's Dance
entries: When you enter spelldance you can use a bonus action and any number of vigour slots to gain movement equal to 5 feet per slot. This movement provokes no opportunity attacks.

entries.name: Dance of Agony
entries: You can spend 3 vigour slots on to enhance Cantrips cast within this spelldance. Any saving throw incurred by the Cantrip is made at disadvantage.

entries.name: Mollifying Dance
entries: You can spend a vigour slot to impose a {@dice 1d4} penalty to creatures when making a saving throw for a Cantrip cast in the spell dance.

entries.name: Dance of Crashing Waves
entries: You can spend a number of vigour slots on this dance. if a large or smaller creature fails a saving throw for one Cantrip cast in the spell dance it is pushed number of feet away or closer equal to 5 times the vigour slots used

entries.name: Biding Dance
entries: You can spend a vigour slot on this dance. The next spelldance you enter before the end of your next turn will grant you 2 additional vigour slots. This augment cannot be then used on that spelldance.

entries.name: Dance of the Spiral
entries: You can spend a vigour slot to generate a strong dust devil from you till the beginning of your next turn. A spherical area of 10 foot radius around you is difficult terrain for creatures besides you.

entries.name: Drunkard's Dance
entries: You can spend a vigour slot to gain +2 to your AC till the beginning of your next turn.

entries.name: Dance of the Coiled Serpent
entries: You can spend a vigour slot to extend your spelldance till the beginning of your next turn. While in this state you can cast Cantrips at any creature you can see that makes an attack roll without using your reaction provided it is in range of the Cantrip.

entries.name: Dance of Torn Mind
entries: You may spend no vigour slots to enter this dance. While this dance is in effect, you may cast two Cantrips that require concentration and hold concentration on both of them. Though for as long as you hold concentration on both of them, your choreurgic repletion suffers by 1 vigour slot.

entries.name: Vengeful Dance
entries: You may spend 2 vigour slots to enter a retaliatory state. Till the beginning of your next turn, Creatures that make an attack targeting you are marked till the end of your next turn. The first Cantrip cast at each of them will impose disadvantage for its saving throw.

classFeature.name: Art Feature
entries: At the 6th Level, You gain a feature granted by your Choreurgic Art.

classFeature.name: Fleet of Foot
entries: At the 7th Level, If you are affected by a spell that isn't targeting you, you can use your reaction to move 10 ft before it hits potentially avoiding damage. Additionally, While wearing light or no armour you gain 10 feet of movement.

classFeature.name: Persistence
entries: At the 5th Level, your cantrips count as 3rd level spells for the purposes of resisting the effects of {@spell counterspell} and {@spell dispel magic}. This feature improves as you gain levels in this class.
Counting as 4th level spells at the 11 level and 5th level spells at the 17 level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM uses the optional Feats, you can instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Depleted Casting
entries: At the 9th level, as a bonus action you can make all cantrips cast this turn more potent at the cost of power. Cantrips you cast on that turn will have advantage on their attack rolls and they impose disadvantage on saving throws at the cost of 1 damage die rolled from each cantrip cast.

classFeature.name: Art Feature
entries: At the 10th level, You gain a feature granted by your Choreurgic Art.

classFeature.name: Perpetual Motion
entries: At the 11th Level, you can get up from being {@condition prone} with only 5 feet of movement. Additionally, non-magical difficult terrain does not hinder your movement.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM uses the optional Feats, you can instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Elastic body
entries: At the 13th, You have advantage on all saving throws and checks to avoid or escape an effect that causes you to be grappled or restrained.

classFeature.name: Magic Resistance
entries: At the 13th, When subjected to a saving throw caused by a spell, you can spend a reaction to gain +5 bonus to the roll.

classFeature.name: Art Feature
entries: At the 14th level, You gain a feature granted by your Choreurgic Art.

classFeature.name: Supreme Tachyurgy
entries: At the 15th level, you can cast three cantrips, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action cast a spell} action on your turn.
Unless you have the Extra Attack feature, only one of those cantrips cast can involve a weapon attack, otherwise two of them may involve weapon attacks.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM uses the optional Feats, you can instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Omneurgist
entries: At the 17th level, You know all the cantrips that can be learnt by a wizard.

classFeature.name: Esoteric techniques
entries: At the 18th level, great effort and experimentation has allowed you to simplify basic spells down to a technique. Pick two level 1 spells from the wizard spell list. They are now Cantrips for you and won't count towards spells known.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM uses the optional Feats, you can instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Magnum Opus
entries: You've toiled away your entire life to reach here. A spell that takes most years to master cast, expressed in splendid motion.

At the 20th level, choose a {@filter spell of upto 5th level|spells|class=wizard|level=1;2;3;4;5} from the wizard spell list. This spell becomes your Magnum Opus. You may cast this spell as a Cantrip once per turn, a number of times equal to your Intelligence Modifier per day.

classFeature.name: Infuse Item
entries: {@i 2nd-level artificer feature}
You've gained the ability to imbue mundane items with certain magical infusions, turning those objects into magic items.

entries.name: Artificer Infusions
entries: Artificers have invented numerous magical infusions, extraordinary processes that rapidly create magic items. To many, artificers seem like wonderworkers, accomplishing in hours what others need weeks to complete.
The description of each of the following infusions details the type of item that can receive it, along with whether the resulting magic item requires attunement.
Some infusions specify a minimum artificer level. You can't learn such an infusion until you are at least that level.
Unless an infusion's description says otherwise, you can't learn an infusion more than once.

entries.name: Infusing an Item
entries: Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch a nonmagical object and imbue it with one of your artificer infusions, turning it into a magic item. An infusion works on only certain kinds of objects, as specified in the infusion's description. If the item requires attunement, you can attune yourself to it the instant you infuse the item. If you decide to attune to the item later, you must do so using the normal process for attunement (see "{@book Attunement|DMG|7|Attunement}" in chapter 7 of the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|DMG}).

Your infusion remains in an item indefinitely, but when you die, the infusion vanishes after a number of days have passed equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 day). The infusion also vanishes if you give up your knowledge of the infusion for another one.
You can remove the attunement requirement of infused items you create. You can do so for a number of items equal to half of the infused items.

You can infuse more than one nonmagical object at the end of a long rest; the maximum number of objects appears in the Infused Items column of the Artificer table. You must touch each of the objects, and each of your infusions can be in only one object at a time. Moreover, no object can bear more than one of your infusions at a time. If you try to exceed your maximum number of infusions, the oldest infusion immediately ends, and then the new infusion applies.
If an infusion ends on an item that contains other things, like a {@item bag of holding}, its contents harmlessly appear in and around its space.

classFeature.name: Arcane Pioneer
entries: At 20th level, you begin to break down the barriers of your magic, gaining the ability to learn spells from outside your class.

You can add 6 spells from the {@filter from the sorcerer or warlock spell list|spells|class=sorcerer;warlock|level=1;2;3;4;5;6;7;8;9} to your spellbook, and can have 6 additional spells prepared. You can further add spells from the two spell lists through spell scrolls, similar to how you would wizard spells.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Invocations
entries: You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. A list of the available options can be found on the {@filter Optional Features|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=EI} page. When you gain certain warlock levels, you gain additional invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.

entries.name: Replacing and Gaining Invocations
entries: Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.
When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.
You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
Consult the {@table Weapons|tct} and {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
Consult the {@table Weapons|tct} and {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
Consult the {@table Weapons|tct} and {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
Consult the {@table Weapons|tct} and {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
Consult the {@table Weapons|tct} and {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
Consult the {@table Weapons|tct} and {@table Weapon Masteries|tct} tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 6th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Master of Armaments
entries: You are a master of weapons. From 9th level, whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can choose any of the kinds of Mastery weapons you're using and replace the Mastery property of each with another Mastery property. For example, you could replace the Longsword's Sap property with the Push property.
These property changes apply only for you, not for others, and the changes end for you when you finish your next Long rest.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 14th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Secrets
entries: At 20th level, you begin unshackling the limits of Mystic Arcanum. Whenever you take a Short Rest, you can regain the use of one expended Mystic Arcanum.

classFeature.name: Rage
entries: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action.
While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor:

items: You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
You can take a bonus action to extend your rage for one turn if you failed to attack or take damage to maintain it. This feature cannot extend the rage's duration over 10 minutes.

When you deal damage with a weapon attack using Strength, or take damage for the first time on a turn. you gain a charge of {@b Wrath}. The amount of wrath you have at any time cannot exceed your constitution modifier. Each charge of wrath is represented by your wrath die, as shown in the class table. You can use wrath in two ways, and you lose all existing stacks of wrath when you lose rage.
You can expend a wrath die on your turn to gain 5 feet of movement until the end of your turn.
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack using strength, you can choose to expend all of your wrath charges and deal damage equal to the number rolled.

entries: If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for up to 10 minutes. It ends early if you are knocked {@condition unconscious} or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action.

Once you have raged the maximum number of times for your barbarian level, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again. You may rage 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.

classFeature.name: Reckless Attack
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on weapon attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

classFeature.name: Primal Knowledge
entries: {@i 3rd-level barbarian}
When you reach 3rd level and again at 10th level, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice from the list of skills available to barbarians at 1st level.

In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: {@skill Acrobatics}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Stealth} or {@skill Survival}. When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility and senses.

classFeature.name: Brutal Critical
entries: Beginning at 9th level, your rage can give you occasional bursts of unfathomable power. When you land a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you take the maximum possible result on any damage die. Additionally, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for the critical hit with a melee attack.
This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Primal Champion
entries: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 26.

classFeature.name: Magical Secrets
entries: At 9th level, choose two additional spells from any classes, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip.
The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are not included in the number in the Spells Known column of the Bard table.

classFeature.name: Magical Secrets
entries: At 12th level, choose two additional spells from any classes, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip.
The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are not included in the number in the Spells Known column of the Bard table.

classFeature.name: Magical Secrets
entries: At 15th level, choose two additional spells from any classes, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip.
The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are included in the number in the Spells Known column of the Bard table.

classFeature.name: Wondrous Inspiration
entries: Your mere presence inspires those around you. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your bardic inspiration die increases to a d12.
You can expend a use of inspiration to inspire a creature of your choice within range as part of casting a levelled spell. You can only inspire a creature like this once per round.

classFeature.name: Divine Intervention
entries: Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

Imploring your deity's aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. The DM chooses the nature of the intervention; the effect of any cleric spell or cleric domain spell would be appropriate. If your deity intervenes, you can't use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.

Alternatively, as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Greater Divine Intervention
entries: At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.
Alternatively, you can choose to cast {@spell Wish|XPHB} when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish {@dice 1d4} Long Rests.

classFeature.name: Wild Shape
entries: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Number of Uses
entries: You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.

entries.name: Known Forms
entries: You know four Beast forms for this feature, chosen from among Beast stat blocks that have a maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} of 1/4 and that lack a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} (see appendix B for stat block options). The {@creature Rat|XPHB}, {@creature Riding Horse|XPHB}, {@creature Spider|XPHB}, and {@creature Wolf|XPHB} are recommended. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.

When you reach certain Druid levels, your number of known forms and the maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} for those forms increases, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. In addition, starting at level 8, you can adopt a form that has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}.
When choosing known forms, you may look in the {@variantrule Monster|XPHB} Manual or elsewhere for eligible Beasts if the Dungeon Master permits you to do so.

entries.name: Rules While Transformed
entries: While in a form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half of the hitpoints of the form you turn into (minimum of your druid level).

items.name: Game Statistics
entries: Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} Bonus for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.

items.name: No Spellcasting
entries: You can't cast spells, but shape-shifting doesn't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.

items.name: Objects
entries: Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form's limbs rather than your own. In addition, you choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it's practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's size and shape. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

classFeature.name: Second Wind
entries: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to {@dice 1d10} + your fighter level.
You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses whenever you finish a long rest. You gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter table.

classFeature.name: Tactical Mind
entries: You have a mind for tactics and getting the upper hand on and off the battlefield. Beginning at 2nd level, whenever you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself towards success.

Rather than regaining Hit Points,  you roll {@dice 1d10} and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

classFeature.name: Tactical Shift
entries: at 5th level, whenever you activate your Second Wind with a bonus action, you can move up to half your speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

classFeature.name: Indomitable
entries: Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail with a bonus equal to your fighter level. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

classFeature.name: Indomitable (2)
entries: You can now use your indomitable feature twice between long rests.

classFeature.name: Unconquerable
entries: When you're in great peril, you can tap into a deep well of resilience within yourself. Beginning at 18th level, If you fail a saving throw and your Indomitable feature is expended, you can use it again by expending a use of your Second Wind, which also heals you.

classFeature.name: Sorcerous Origin
entries: Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power, from the list of available origins.
Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. This font of magic, whatever its origin, fuels your spells. See {@book chapter 10|PHB|10} for the general rules of spellcasting and {@book chapter 11|PHB|11} for the {@filter sorcerer spell list|spells|class=sorcerer}.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 1st level, you know four cantrips of your choice from the sorcerer spell list. You learn an additional sorcerer cantrip of your choice at 4th level and another at 10th level.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Sorcerer table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your {@filter sorcerer spells|spells|class=sorcerer} of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these sorcerer spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
For example, if you know the 1st-level spell {@spell burning hands} and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast {@spell burning hands} using either slot.

entries.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
entries: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the sorcerer spell list.

You learn an additional sorcerer spell of your choice at each level except 12th, 14th, 16th, 18th, 19th, and 20th. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 3rd level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the sorcerer spells you know and replace it with another spell from the sorcerer spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your sorcerer spells, since the power of your magic relies on your ability to project your will into the world. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a sorcerer spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item arcane focus|phb} as a spellcasting focus for your sorcerer spells.

classFeature.name: Flexible Casting
entries: You can use your sorcery points to gain additional spell slots, or sacrifice spell slots to gain additional sorcery points. You learn other ways to use your sorcery points as you reach higher levels.

entries.name: Creating Spell Slots
entries: You can transform unexpended sorcery points into one spell slot as a bonus action on your turn. The created spell slots vanish at the end of a long rest. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level. You can create spell slots no higher in level than 5th.

entries.name: Converting a Spell Slot to Sorcery Points
entries: You can expend one spell slot and gain a number of sorcery points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

classFeature.name: Font of Magic
entries: At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by sorcery points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

classFeature.name: Sorcery Points
entries: You have 2 sorcery points, and you gain one additional point every time you level up, to a maximum of 20 at level 20. You can never have more sorcery points than shown on the table for your level. You regain all spent sorcery points when you finish a long rest.

classFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Metamagic options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Sorcerous Versatility
entries: {@i 4th-level sorcerer {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}}
Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, representing the magic within you flowing in new ways:

items: Replace one of the options you chose for the Metamagic feature with a different {@filter Metamagic option|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=MM} available to you.
Replace one cantrip you learned from this class's Spellcasting feature with another cantrip from the {@filter sorcerer spell list|spells|level=0|class=Sorcerer}.

classFeature.name: Magical Guidance
entries: {@i 5th-level sorcerer {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}}

You can tap into your inner wellspring of magic to try to conjure success from failure. When you make an ability check that fails, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll the {@dice d20}, and you must use the new roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.

classFeature.name: Sorcerous Origin feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain a feature granted by your Sorcerous Origin.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Innate Sorcery
entries: An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefit:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

entries: You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Sorcery Incarnate
entries: If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to activate it.

In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, your spell save DC increases by 1, and you can use up to two of your {@filter Metamagic options|optionalfeatures|feature type=MM} on each spell you cast.

classFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: At 10th level, you learn two additional metamagic option.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Sorcerous Origin feature
entries: At 14th level, you gain a feature granted by your Sorcerous Origin.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: At 17th level, you learn two additional metamagic option.

classFeature.name: Sorcerous Origin feature
entries: At 18th level, you gain a feature granted by your Sorcerous Origin.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Arcane Apotheosis
entries: You can use one metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery points on it.

classFeature.name: Canny
entries: Beginning at 1st level, You are an unsurpassed explorer and survivor, both in the wilderness and in dealing with others on your travels. You gain the following benefits:

items: Choose one of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses the chosen skill.
You can also speak, read, and write two additional languages of your choice.

classFeature.name: Ranger's Quarry
entries: Rangers are masters of the hunt, singling out prey out of a herd, isolating them and exploiting their weaknesses. You gain the following features:

entries.name: Hunter's Mark
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can use your bonus action to mark them as your quarry for the next hour. When you do so, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to track or find the creature. Your attacks also deal additional force damage equal to your Quarry die, which improves as shown in the ranger table.
You concentrate on this mark as if you were concentrating on a spell.

If a creature dies while marked by you, you can immediately use your reaction or use your bonus action on your next turn to move the mark on to another creature within your attack range (minimum of 60 feet).
You can use this feature twice, regaining half of the uses on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long rest. You gain more uses of this feature as shown in the ranger table.

entries.name: Mark Enhancements
entries: When you apply a mark on a creature, you can choose to enhance it in various ways by expending an additional use of Ranger's quarry.
You can only have one enhancement active on your hunter's mark. If you move the mark to a different creature, the enhancement is lost.

classFeature.name: Ranger's Hunt
entries: The following options are added to your possible hunter's mark enhancements. Additionally, you no longer need to concentrate in order to maintain the mark.

classFeature.name: Tireless
entries: As a bonus action, you can give yourself a number of temporary hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Wisdom modifier. You can use this special action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
In addition, whenever you finish a short rest, your {@condition exhaustion} level, if any, is decreased by 1.

classFeature.name: Refined Mark
entries: You have refined your hunter's mark, increasing its efficiency. Hunter's mark improves in the following ways:

items: Hunter's mark no longer requires a bonus action to apply or reapply.
You can apply two enhancements on a single mark, paying the cost for both enhancements.
You can replace or add mark enhancements on an active hunter's mark.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

classFeature.name: Ranger Imbibements
entries: Rangers are masters of adaptation, surviving through harsh climates and dangerous foes alike. They do so by assimilating the skills into their core instinct.

You learn two imbibements of your choice at level 2. A list of available options can be found on the {@filter Optional Features|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=RI} page. When you gain ranger levels, you gain additional imbibements of your choice, as shown in the imbibements column of the ranger table.
Additionally, when you gain an ability score improvement or a feat, you can choose one of the imbibements you know and replace it with another imbibement that you could learn at that level.

If a ranger imbibement has prerequisites, you must meet them to learn it. You can learn the imbibement at the same time that you meet its prerequisites. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

classFeature.name: Primal Awareness
entries: You can focus your awareness through the interconnections of nature: you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class if you don't already know them, as shown in the Primal Awareness Spells table. These spells don't count against the number of ranger spells you know.
You can cast each of these spells once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast a spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

classFeature.name: Ranger Archetype
entries: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate from the list of available archetypes. Your choice grants features at 3rd level, and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Martial Versatility
entries: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace a fighting style you know with another fighting style available to rangers. This replacement represents a shift of focus in your martial practice.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Ranger Archetype feature
entries: At 7th level, you gain a feature granted to you by your Ranger Archetype.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: Choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

classFeature.name: Ranger Archetype feature
entries: At 11th level, you gain a feature granted to you by your Ranger Archetype.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Ranger's Prey
entries: The following powerful options are added to your possible hunter's mark enhancements. These enhancements cost two uses of Ranger's Quarry

classFeature.name: Target Focus
entries: At 14th level, any attack roll you make against a creature under the effects of ranger's quarry is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. Additionally, you gain a new mark enhancement from your subclass.

classFeature.name: Ranger Archetype feature
entries: At 15th level, you gain a feature granted to you by your Ranger Archetype.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Feral Senses
entries: At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it. You are also aware of the location of any {@condition invisible} creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't {@condition blinded} or {@condition deafened}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Foe Slayer
entries: At level 20, your hunter's mark die increases to {@dice 2d6}.
You can have 3 enhancements on a hunter's mark. When you move your mark to a new target, you can choose to retain one of the mark enhancements.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with {@item thieves' tools|phb}. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with {@item thieves' tools|phb}) to gain this benefit.

classFeature.name: Sneak Attack
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.
You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't {@condition incapacitated}, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.
If you do not qualify for a sneak attack, you can still deal half of the sneak dice (rounded up) as part of the attack.
The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

classFeature.name: Thieves' Cant
entries: During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves' cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.

In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a thieves' guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for thieves on the run.

classFeature.name: Cunning Action
entries: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, or {@action Hide} action.

classFeature.name: Roguish Archetype
entries: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities from the list of available archetypes. Your archetype choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

classFeature.name: Steady Aim
entries: {@i 3rd-level rogue {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}}

As a bonus action, you give yourself advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this bonus action only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Cunning Strike
entries: You have developed cunning ways to use your sneak attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, You can add one of the following Cunning strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, Which is the number of sneak attack damage dice you must forego to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the poison attack, remomve 1d6 from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.
If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC is calculated as follows

classFeature.name: Disarm (Cost: 1d6)
entries: The target must succed on a dexterity saving throw, or it drops one item of your choice that it's holding.

classFeature.name: Poison (Cost: 1d6)
entries: You add a toxin to your strike, forcing the target to make a constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition poisoned} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the poisoned target can repeat its save, ending the effect on a success. To use this effect, you must have a poisoner's kit on your person.

classFeature.name: Trip (Cost: 1d6)
entries: If the target is large or smaller, it must succeed on a dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition prone} condition.

classFeature.name: Withdraw (Cost: 1d6)
entries: Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your speed without provoking Oppurtunity Attacks.

classFeature.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with {@item thieves' tools|phb}) to gain the benefit of Expertise.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an {@spell ice storm} spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

classFeature.name: Reliable Talent
entries: By 7th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Roguish Archetype feature
entries: At 9th level, you gain a feature granted by your Roguish Archetype.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 10th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Improved Cunning Strike
entries: When you reach 11th level, You can use up to two cunning strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Roguish Archetype feature
entries: At 13th level, you gain a feature granted by your Roguish Archetype.

classFeature.name: Blindsense
entries: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or {@condition invisible} creature within 10 feet of you.

classFeature.name: Devious Strikes
entries: You have practiced new ways to use your sneak attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

classFeature.name: Daze (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target must succed on a constitution saving throw, or it is dazed. Until the end of its next turn, it can move or take one Action on its turn, not both. You also can't take a Bonus Action or a Reaction.

classFeature.name: Knock Out (Cost: 6d6)
entries: The target must succed on a constitution saving throw, or it has the {@condition unconscious} condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The unconscious target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

classFeature.name: Obscure (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target must succed on a dexterity saving throw, or it has the {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn.

classFeature.name: Slippery Mind
entries: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Roguish Archetype feature
entries: At 17th level, you gain a feature granted by your Roguish Archetype.

classFeature.name: Elusive
entries: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Stroke of Luck
entries: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail an ability check, attack roll or saving throw, you can turn that roll into a 20. You can use this feature after the roll has been made, but before the rolls effects take place.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

classFeature.name: Martial Arts
entries: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons, which are {@item shortsword|tct|shortswords} and any {@filter simple melee weapons that don't have the two-handed or heavy property|items|source=tct|category=basic|type=simple weapon;melee weapon=u~u~sand|property=!heavy;!two-handed}.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item shield|phb}.

items: You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons. In addition, when you choose the Grapple or Shove option, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength to determine the saving throw DC.
You can roll a {@dice d4} in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or monk weapon. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk table.
You can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.

entries: Certain monasteries use specialized forms of the monk weapons. For example, you might use a club that is two lengths of wood connected by a short chain (called a nunchaku) or a sickle with a shorter, straighter blade (called a kama).

classFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

classFeature.name: Dedicated Weapon
entries: {@i 2nd-level monk {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}}

You train yourself to use a variety of weapons as monk weapons, not just simple melee weapons and shortswords. Whenever you finish a short or long rest, you can touch one weapon, focus your ki on it, and then count that weapon as a monk weapon until you use this feature again.
The chosen weapon must meet these criteria:

items: The weapon must be a {@filter simple or martial weapon|items|source=tct|category=basic|type=martial weapon;simple weapon|property=!heavy;!special}.
You must be proficient with it.
It must lack the heavy and special properties.

classFeature.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: You can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.

classFeature.name: Ki
entries: Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. You possess an amount of ki points as shown in the Ki Points column of the Monk table.

You can spend these points to fuel various ki features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more ki features as you gain levels in this class.

When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
Some of your ki features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

classFeature.name: Patient Defense
entries: You can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Ki Point to take both the {@action Disengage|XPHB} and the {@action Dodge|XPHB} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Step of the Wind
entries: You can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Ki Point to take both the {@action Disengage|XPHB} and {@action Dash|XPHB} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement
entries: Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in the Monk table.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

classFeature.name: Deflect Attacks
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to deflect melee or ranged attacks against you that deal Bludgeoning, Slashing and Piercing damage. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d10} + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can spend 1 ki point to redirect some of the attacks force. If you do so, choose a creature within 5 feet of you if the attack was a melee attack, or 60 feet of yourself that isn't behind total cover if the attack was a ranged attack. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier. The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

classFeature.name: Monastic Tradition
entries: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, chosen from the list of available traditions. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Slow Fall
entries: Beginning at 4th level, you can use your reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your monk level.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Focused Aim
entries: {@i 5th-level monk {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}}
When you miss with an attack roll, you can spend 1 to 3 ki points to increase your attack roll by 2 for each of these ki points you spend, potentially turning the miss into a hit.

classFeature.name: Ki-Empowered Strikes
entries: Starting at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

classFeature.name: Monastic Tradition feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain one feature granted by your Monastic Tradition.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: At 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a {@spell fireball} spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

classFeature.name: Stillness of Mind
entries: Starting at 7th level, at the start of your turn, you can choose to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}. When you do, you are unable to use your action though you may still use other actions like bonus actions and movement.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement improvement
entries: At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

classFeature.name: Purity of Body
entries: At 10th level, your mastery of the ki flowing through you makes you immune to disease and poison.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 10th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Monastic Tradition feature
entries: At 11th level, you gain one feature granted by your Monastic Tradition.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Tongue of the Sun and Moon
entries: Starting at 13th level, you learn to touch the ki of other minds so that you understand all spoken languages. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you say.

classFeature.name: Ki-fueled Body
entries: At 13th level, you have mastered the ability to move ki throughout your body, focusing it to improve your body. As a bonus action, you can spend 4 ki points to increase an ability score of your choice by 2 (Upto a maximum of 22) for 10 minutes. While that ability score is boosted in this way, you gain a bonus to ability checks and saving throws that use this ability score equal to your wisdom modifier. You can only benefit from one instance of this feature at a time.
At 20th level, you can increase Wisdom and Dexterity Upto a maximum of 26.

classFeature.name: Diamond Soul
entries: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

classFeature.name: Timeless Body
entries: At 15th level, your ki sustains you so that you suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however. In addition, you no longer need food or water.
Additionally, whenever you finish a short rest, you may reduce any exhaustion remaining by 1 level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Monastic Tradition feature
entries: At 17th level, you gain one feature granted by your Monastic Tradition.

classFeature.name: Empty Body
entries: Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become {@condition invisible} for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage.
Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast the {@spell astral projection} spell, without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. However, if you are atleast 19th level, that maximum increases to 22.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Perfect Self
entries: You have honed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 26.

classFeature.name: Divine Smite
entries: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon or an unarmed attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is {@dice 2d8} for a 1st-level spell slot, plus {@dice 1d8} for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of {@dice 5d8}. The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} if the target is an undead or a fiend, to a maximum of {@dice 6d8}.

classFeature.name: Radiant Strikes
entries: By 11th level, you are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage.

classFeature.name: Divine Steed
entries: Your pledge to your oath strengthens your steed. You always have the {@spell Find greater steed|XGE} spell prepared.
You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Memorize Spell
entries: Studying your spellbook for 1 minute,you can exend mental and magical effort to memorize a spell. Choose one spell of level 1 or higher from your spellbook that you don't have prepared. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest, and you forget the spell you memorized whenever you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Mirage
entries:
A man walks the desert, beaten and tattered, hunger gnawing at his insides, thirst clawing at his throat. His mind can barely hold onto his deepest desire, consumed by the aching void within. As he trudges forward, eyes half-blind from exhaustion, he sees something—an oasis shimmering in the distance, a disruption in the endless dunes. Water, life, salvation! His heart surges with a final spark of hope, propelling him toward the mirage. Without hesitation, he dives into what he believes is cool, refreshing water, only to be swallowed by the scorching sand beneath.

A figure coalesces from the heat, standing over the man’s crumpled form, its face unreadable beneath a veil of shimmering illusions. The oasis dissolves into the blazing sun as the last vestiges of the man's life slip away. The contract is complete, the deception flawless, the death inevitable.

Mesmers who learn the art of the Mirage tap into the deepest fears and desires of their targets, weaving illusions that play upon the mind’s most desperate longings. They are not just masters of deception—they manipulate false truths so convincingly that even reality bends to their will. A The Mirage is an artist of the mind, crafting deadly illusions that blur the line between what is real and what is imagined, until it no longer matters. To face one is to question your own senses, to doubt every step, until the illusion becomes your reality—and your downfall.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Convergence
entries: {@i 3rd-level Mirage feature}

The greatest strength of a Mirage is the element of surprise. A Mirage appears as quickly as it disappears. At 3rd level, you have learned to control your illusions to aid you more actively in combat. Once per turn, when you or one of your clones makes a melee attack, you may invoke all other active clones to join in the attack.

items: If you are making the attack, each clone within 100 feet of you is immediately teleported into your space, joining you in the attack.

If one of your clones within 100ft of you is making the attack, you can choose to immediately teleport to its space, along with all other clones within 100 feet of you, and make the attack yourself instead.
