On a failure, you automatically succeed on any checks you make while talking to or trying to get information out of the creature. This effect ends after 10 minutes.

subclassFeature.name: Unerring Eye
entries: {@i 13th-level Assassin feature}

Your senses are almost impossible to foil. As an action, you sense the presence of illusions, shapechangers not in their original form, and other magic designed to deceive the senses within 30 feet of you, provided you aren't {@condition blinded} or {@condition deafened}. You sense that an effect is attempting to trick you, but you gain no insight into what is hidden or into its true nature. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.
creatures can no longer gain advantage on attack rolls against you as a result of being unseen by you.

Additionally, if you miss with an attack roll that qualified for sneak attack against a creature affected by your Insightful Fighting feature, you can still deal damage to that creature equal to half of your sneak attack die (rounded up).

subclassFeature.name: Eye for Weakness
entries: {@i 17th-level Inquisitive feature}

You learn to exploit a creature's weaknesses by carefully studying its tactics and movement. While your Insightful Fighting feature applies to a creature, your Sneak Attack damage against that creature increases by {@dice 5d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Mastermind
entries: {@i 3rd-level Mastermind feature}

Your focus is on people and on the influence and secrets they have. Many spies, courtiers, and schemers follow this archetype, leading lives of intrigue. Words are your weapons as often as knives or poison, and secrets and favors are some of your favorite treasures.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Intrigue
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the {@item disguise kit|phb}, the {@item forgery kit|phb}, and one {@item gaming set|PHB} of your choice. You also learn two languages of your choice.

Additionally, you can unerringly mimic the speech patterns and accent of a creature that you hear speak for at least 1 minute, enabling you to pass yourself off as a native speaker of a particular land, provided that you know the language.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Tactics
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the {@action Help} action as a bonus action. Additionally, when you use the {@action Help} action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you, rather than within 5 feet of you, if the target can see or hear you.

subclassFeature.name: Mind of Deceit
entries: No matter what you say, magic that would determine if your are telling the truth indicates you are being truthful if you so choose, and you can't be compelled to tell the truth by magic.

subclassFeature.name: Insightful Manipulator
entries: {@i 9th-level Mastermind feature}
Starting at 9th level, you gain all the tools necessary to gain the upper hand before a fight.

subclassFeature.name: Know Your Enemy
entries: Starting at 9th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:

items: Intelligence score
Wisdom score
Charisma score
Class levels (if any)

entries: At the DM's option, you might also realize you know a piece of the creature's history or one of its personality traits, if it has any.

subclassFeature.name: Soul of Deceit
entries: Your thoughts cant be read by telepathy or other means, unless you allow it. You can present false thoughts by succeeding on a Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check contested by the mind reader's Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

subclassFeature.name: Plan of Attack
entries: The following options are now part of your Cunning Strike feature.

subclassFeature.name: Find the Opening (Cost: 2d6)
entries: You automatically take the help action against the target.

subclassFeature.name: Thwart (Cost: 3d6)
entries: The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you can give it disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes using one attribute of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Misdirection
entries: {@i 13th-level Mastermind feature}

Beginning at 13th level, you can sometimes cause another creature to suffer an attack meant for you. When you are targeted by an attack while a creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to have the attack target that creature instead of you.

subclassFeature.name: Battleplan
entries: {@i 17th-level Mastermind feature}
You can direct your allies with perfect synchronicity.

As an action, you can setup a plan of attack for the next round of combat. Choose a number of creatures (including yourself) equal to your dexterity modifier. For the next round of combat, their initiatives are set to 20. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Scout
entries: {@i 3rd-level Scout feature}

You are skilled in stealth and surviving far from the streets of a city, allowing you to scout ahead of your companions during expeditions. Rogues who embrace this archetype are at home in the wilderness and among barbarians and rangers, and many Scouts serve as the eyes and ears of war bands. Ambusher, spy, bounty hunter—these are just a few of the roles that Scouts assume as they range the world.

subclassFeature.name: Skirmisher
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you are difficult to pin down during a fight. You can move up to half your speed as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Survivalist
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} and {@skill Survival} skills if you don't already have it. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those proficiencies.

subclassFeature.name: Hawk's Mastery
entries: {@i 9th-level Scout feature}
Your prowess in scouting rivals that of a hawk.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Mobility
entries: your walking speed increases by 10 feet. You also gain a climbing and swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

subclassFeature.name: Target Priority
entries: You gain two more options for your Cunning Strike feature.

entries.subclassFeature: Reposition (Cost: A number of d6 equal to the creatures affected)|Rogue|DRK|Scout|DRK|9

subclassFeature.name: Birds Eye View (Cost: 1d6)
entries: You keep a keen eye on the target. It cannot benefit from the {@condition invisible} condition until the end of your next turn, as long as the creature is in your line of sight.

subclassFeature.name: Reposition (Cost: A number of d6 equal to the creatures affected)
entries: Choose a number of creatures that you can see. Immediately after the attack, the chosen creatures can move up to 10 feet without provoking any opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Ambush Master
entries: {@i 13th-level Scout feature}
You excel at leading ambushes and acting first in a fight.

You have advantage on initiative rolls. In addition, You can choose to provide advantage on attack rolls for you and your allies against a creature you land an attack on until the start of your next turn. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

subclassFeature.name: Sudden Strike
entries: {@i 17th-level Scout feature}

You can strike with deadly speed. If you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as a bonus action. This attack can benefit from your Sneak Attack even if you have already used it this turn, but you can't use your Sneak Attack against the same target more than once in a turn.

subclassFeature.name: Swashbuckler
entries: {@i 3rd-level Swashbuckler feature}

You focus your training on the art of the blade, relying on speed, elegance, and charm in equal parts. While some warriors are brutes clad in heavy armor, your method of fighting looks almost like a performance. Duelists and pirates typically belong to this archetype.
A Swashbuckler excels in single combat, and can fight with two weapons while safely darting away from an opponent.

subclassFeature.name: Fancy Footwork
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to land a strike and then slip away without reprisal. During your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can't make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Rakish Audacity
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your confidence propels you into battle. You can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma modifier.

You also gain an additional way to use your Sneak Attack; you don't need advantage on your attack roll to use Sneak Attack against a creature if you are within 5 feet of it, no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. All the other rules for Sneak Attack still apply to you.

subclassFeature.name: Panache
entries: {@i 9th-level Swashbuckler feature}

Your charm becomes extraordinarily beguiling. As an action, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check contested by a creature's Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. The creature must be able to hear you, and the two of you must share a language.

If you succeed on the check and the creature is hostile to you, it has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you and can't make opportunity attacks against targets other than you. This effect lasts for 1 minute, until one of your companions attacks the target or affects it with a spell, or until you and the target are more than 60 feet apart.

If you succeed on the check and the creature isn't hostile to you, it is {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute. While {@condition charmed}, it regards you as a friendly acquaintance. This effect ends immediately if you or your companions do anything harmful to it.
You also gain the following Cunning Strike options.

subclassFeature.name: Goad (Cost: 1d6)
entries: The target must succed on a Wisdom saving throw, or until the end of its next turn, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you and can't mmake opportunity attacks against creatures other than you.

subclassFeature.name: Awe (Cost: 1d6)
entries: Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Charmed} condition until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Elegant Maneuver
entries: {@i 13th-level Swashbuckler feature}
You run circles around your enemies. You gain the following features:

subclassFeature.name: Tiptoe
entries: You can use a bonus action on your turn to gain advantage on the next Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check you make during the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Dashing Strike
entries: You gain the following Cunning Strike options.

subclassFeature.name: Parrying Stance (Cost: 2d6)
entries: Roll a d6. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a bonus to your Armor Class equal to the number rolled.

subclassFeature.name: Invigorate (Cost: 2d6)
entries: Choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Until the end of that creature's next turn, whenever it makes an attack roll or saving throw, it can roll a d6 and add that number to the attack roll or saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Master Duelist
entries: {@i 17th-level Swashbuckler feature}

Your mastery of the blade lets you turn failure into success in combat. If you miss with an attack roll, you can roll it again with advantage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma bonus (Minimum of one). You regain all expended uses at the end of a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Domain
entries: Developed in {@book Wildemount|TDCSR|3|Wildemount} by the {@book Claret Orders|TDCSR|2|Claret Orders}, the Blood Domain centers around the understanding of the natural life force as it exists within the body, and the divine conduit it can become. Those who take up this domain understand that the power of blood is the power of sacrifice, the balance of life and death, and the spirit's anchor within the mortal shell.

Gods who grant the power of the Blood Domain, including {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TDCSR} and {@deity The Matron of Ravens|Exandria|TDCSR}, direct their followers to tap into the connection between body and soul, exploit the hidden reserves of will within one's own vitality, and corrupt the bodies of others through the secret rites of {@variantrule hemocraft|TDCSR}. Clerics of good gods use {@variantrule hemocraft|TDCSR} to fill their self-sacrifice with purpose and power, while clerics with fewer morals use the blood of others to achieve their own malevolent ends.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodletting Focus
entries: Starting at 1st level, your divine magic draws the blood from magically inflicted wounds, worsening the agony of your foes. When you cast a damage-dealing spell of 1st level or higher whose duration is instantaneous, any creature with blood that takes damage from the spell takes extra necrotic damage equal to 2 + the spell's level.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Blood Domain Spells table.

subclassFeature.name: Death Domain
entries: The Death domain is concerned with the forces that cause death, as well as the negative energy that gives rise to undead creatures. Deities such as {@deity Chemosh|Dragonlance}, {@deity Myrkul}, and {@deity Wee Jas|Greyhawk} are patrons of necromancers, death knights, liches, mummy lords, and vampires. Gods of the Death domain also embody murder ({@deity Anubis|Egyptian}, {@deity Bhaal}, and Pyremius), pain ({@deity Iuz|Greyhawk} or {@deity Loviatar}), disease or poison ({@deity Incabulos|Greyhawk}, {@deity Talona}, or {@deity Morgion|Dragonlance}), and the underworld ({@deity Hades|Greek} and {@deity Hel|Norse}).
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

subclassFeature.name: Forge Domain
entries: The gods of the forge are patrons of artisans who work with metal, from a humble blacksmith who keeps a village in horseshoes and plow blades to the mighty elf artisan whose diamond-tipped arrows of mithral have felled demon lords. The gods of the forge teach that, with patience and hard work, even the most intractable metal can be transformed from a lump of ore to a beautifully wrought object. Clerics of these deities search for objects lost to the forces of darkness, liberate mines overrun by orcs, and uncover rare and wondrous materials necessary to create potent magic items. Followers of these gods take great pride in their work, and they are willing to craft and use heavy armor and powerful weapons to protect them. Deities of this domain include {@deity Gond}, {@deity Reorx|Dragonlance}, {@deity Onatar|Eberron}, {@deity Moradin|Nonhuman}, {@deity Hephaestus|Greek}, and {@deity Goibhniu|Celtic}.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with {@item smith's tools|phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Knowledge Domain
entries: {@i Unearth Secrets and Master the Mind}

The Knowledge Domain values learning and understanding above all. Clerics who tap into this domain study esoteric lore, collect old tomes, delve into secret places, and examine the processes of the mind. To them, knowledge is more valuable than material wealth, and learning is an act of worship. Libraries, universities, and other educational institutions also draw on the power of the Knowledge Domain.

Gods of knowledge vary from masters of arcane magic to patrons of craft and invention. In Faerûn, Clerics of the Knowledge Domain worship deities of learning and ingenuity such as {@deity Oghma|Faerûnian|FRHoF} and {@deity Gond|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, among many others.

subclassFeature.name: Blessings of Knowledge
entries: You gain proficiency with one type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice and in two of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, or {@skill Religion|XPHB}. You have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in those two skills.

subclassFeature.name: Knowledge Domain Spells
entries: When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Knowledge Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Command|DRK}, {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB}*, {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}*, {@spell Identify|XPHB}*

subclassFeature.name: Unfettered Mind
entries: You gain {@variantrule telepathy|XPHB} out to 60 feet. When you use this {@variantrule telepathy|XPHB}, you can simultaneously contact a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one).
Additionally, you gain proficiency in Intelligence saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain saving throw proficiency with one ability in which you lack it.

subclassFeature.name: Visions of the Past
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can call up visions of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute in meditation and prayer, then receive dreamlike, shadowy glimpses of recent events. You can meditate in this way for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score and must maintain {@status concentration} during that time, as if you were casting a spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Divine Foreknowledge
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you magically expand your mind to the future. For 1 hour, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of this feature by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Object Reading
entries: Holding an object as you meditate, you can see visions of the object's previous owner. After meditating for 1 minute, you learn how the owner acquired and lost the object, as well as the most recent significant event involving the object and that owner. If the object was owned by another creature in the recent past (within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score), you can spend 1 additional minute for each owner to learn the same information about that creature.

entries.name: Area Reading
entries: As you meditate, you see visions of recent events in your immediate vicinity (a room, street, tunnel, clearing, or the like, up to a 50-foot cube), going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score. For each minute you meditate, you learn about one significant event, beginning with the most recent. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important in your current situation.

subclassFeature.name: Life Domain
entries: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy—one of the fundamental forces of the universe—that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality and health through healing the sick and wounded, caring for those in need, and driving away the forces of death and undeath. Almost any non-evil deity can claim influence over this domain, particularly agricultural deities (such as {@deity Chauntea}, {@deity Arawai|Eberron}, and {@deity Demeter|Greek}), sun gods (such as {@deity Lathander}, {@deity Pelor|Greyhawk}, and {@deity Re-Horakhty|Egyptian}), gods of healing or endurance (such as {@deity Ilmater}, {@deity Mishakal|Dragonlance}, {@deity Apollo|Greek}, and {@deity Diancecht|Celtic}), and gods of home and community (such as {@deity Hestia|Greek}, {@deity Hathor|Egyptian}, and {@deity Boldrei|Eberron}).
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Light Domain
entries: Gods of light—including {@deity Helm}, {@deity Lathander}, {@deity Pholtus|Greyhawk}, {@deity Branchala|Dragonlance}, {@deity the Silver Flame|Eberron}, {@deity Belenus|Celtic}, {@deity Apollo|Greek}, and {@deity Re-Horakhty|Egyptian}—promote the ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty, often using the symbol of the sun. Some of these gods are portrayed as the sun itself or as a charioteer who guides the sun across the sky. Others are tireless sentinels whose eyes pierce every shadow and see through every deception. Some are deities of beauty and artistry, who teach that art is a vehicle for the soul's improvement. Clerics of a god of light are enlightened souls infused with radiance and the power of their gods' discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies and burning away darkness.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Light Domain Spells
rows: {@spell guardian of faith}, {@spell wall of fire}

subclassFeature.name: Warding Flare
entries: When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself makes an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, causing light to flare before it hits or misses.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Order Domain
entries: The Order Domain represents discipline, as well as devotion to a society or an institution and strict obedience to the laws governing it. On Ravnica, the domain is favored by clerics of the Azorius Senate, who use it to maintain and enforce the law, and of the Orzhov Syndicate, who exploit law and order for their personal gain. On other worlds, gods who grant access to this domain include {@deity Bane}, {@deity Tyr}, {@deity Majere|Dragonlance}, {@deity Erathis|Dawn War|DMG}, {@deity Pholtus|Greyhawk}, {@deity Wee Jas|Greyhawk}, {@deity Aureon|Eberron}, {@deity Maglubiyet|Nonhuman}, {@deity Nuada|Celtic}, {@deity Athena|Greek}, {@deity Anubis|Egyptian}, {@deity Forseti|Norse}, and {@deity Asmodeus|Dawn War|DMG}.

The ideal of order is obedience to the law above all else, rather than to a specific individual or the passing influence of emotion or popular rule. Clerics of order are typically concerned with how things are done, rather than whether an action's results are just. Following the law and obeying its edicts is critical, especially when it benefits these clerics and their guilds or deities.

Law establishes hierarchies. Those selected by the law to lead must be obeyed. Those who obey must do so to the best of their ability. In this manner, law creates an intricate web of obligations that allows society to forge order and security in a chaotic multiverse.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Nature Domain
entries: Gods of nature are as varied as the natural world itself, from inscrutable gods of the deep forests (such as {@deity Silvanus}, {@deity Obad-Hai|Greyhawk}, {@deity Chislev|Dragonlance}, {@deity Balinor|Eberron}, and {@deity Pan|Greek}) to friendly deities associated with particular springs and groves (such as {@deity Eldath}). Druids revere nature as a whole and might serve one of these deities, practicing mysterious rites and reciting all-but-forgotten prayers in their own secret tongue. But many of these gods have clerics as well, champions who take a more active role in advancing the interests of a particular nature god. These clerics might hunt the evil monstrosities that despoil the woodlands, bless the harvest of the faithful, or wither the crops of those who anger their gods.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Acolyte of Nature
entries: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice. This cantrip doesn't count against the number of cleric cantrips you know. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Survival}.

subclassFeature.name: Tempest Domain
entries: Gods whose portfolios include the Tempest domain—including {@deity Talos}, {@deity Umberlee}, {@deity Kord|Greyhawk}, {@deity Zeboim|Dragonlance}, {@deity the Devourer|Eberron}, {@deity Zeus|Greek}, and {@deity Thor|Norse}—govern storms, sea, and sky. They include gods of lightning and thunder, gods of earthquakes, some fire gods, and certain gods of violence, physical strength, and courage. In some pantheons, a god of this domain rules over other deities and is known for swift justice delivered by thunderbolts. In the pantheons of seafaring people, gods of this domain are ocean deities and the patrons of sailors. Tempest gods send their clerics to inspire fear in the common folk, either to keep those folk on the path of righteousness or to encourage them to offer sacrifices of propitiation to ward off divine wrath.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to create a perfect visual illusion of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The illusion is intangible and doesn't occupy its space. It lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. The illusion is animated and mimics your expressions and gestures. While it persists, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cast Spells
entries: You can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses.

entries.name: Distract
entries: When both you and your illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature, given how distracting the illusion is to the target.

entries.name: Move
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move the illusion up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is within 120 feet of yourself.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Duplicity
entries: At 17th level, you can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use Invoke Duplicity. Additionally, when one of the illusions end, you or a creature of your choice within 5 feet of it regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Cleric level.

subclassFeature.name: Twilight Domain
entries: The twilit transition from light into darkness often brings calm and even joy, as the day's labors end and the hours of rest begin. The darkness can also bring terrors, but the gods of twilight guard against the horrors of the night.

Clerics who serve these deities-examples of which appear on the Twilight Deities table-bring comfort to those who seek rest and protect them by venturing into the encroaching darkness to ensure that the dark is a comfort, not a terror.

entries.name: Domain Spells
entries: {@i 1st-level Twilight Domain feature}
You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Twilight Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work.

entries.caption: Twilight Domain Spells
rows: {@spell aura of vitality}, {@spell Leomund's tiny hut}

subclassFeature.name: War Domain
entries: War has many manifestations. It can make heroes of ordinary people. It can be desperate and horrific, with acts of cruelty and cowardice eclipsing instances of excellence and courage. In either case, the gods of war watch over warriors and reward them for their great deeds. The clerics of such gods excel in battle, inspiring others to fight the good fight or offering acts of violence as prayers. Gods of war include champions of honor and chivalry (such as {@deity Torm}, {@deity Heironeous|Greyhawk}, and {@deity Kiri-Jolith|Dragonlance}) as well as gods of destruction and pillage (such as {@deity Erythnul|Greyhawk}, {@deity the Fury|Eberron}, {@deity Gruumsh|Nonhuman}, and {@deity Ares|Greek}) and gods of conquest and domination (such as {@deity Bane}, {@deity Hextor|Greyhawk}, and {@deity Maglubiyet|Nonhuman}). Other war gods (such as {@deity Tempus}, {@deity Nike|Greek}, and {@deity Nuada|Celtic}) take a more neutral stance, promoting war in all its manifestations and supporting warriors in any circumstance.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: War Priest
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can make one attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
entries: When you or a creature within 30 feet of you misses with an attack roll, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and give that roll a +10 bonus, potentially causing it to hit. When you use this feature to benefit another creature's attack roll, you must take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to do so.

subclassFeature.name: Peace Domain
entries: The balm of peace thrives at the heart of healthy communities, between friendly nations, and in the souls of the kindhearted. The gods of peace inspire people of all sorts to resolve conflict and to stand up against those forces that try to prevent peace from flourishing. See the Peace Deities table for a list of some of the gods associated with this domain.

Clerics of the Peace Domain preside over the signing of treaties, and they are often asked to arbitrate in disputes. These clerics' blessings draw people together and help them shoulder one another's burdens, and the clerics' magic aids those who are driven to fight for the way of peace.

entries.name: Domain Spells
entries: {@i 1st-level Peace Domain feature}
You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Peace Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work.

entries.caption: Peace Domain Spells
rows: {@spell aura of purity}, {@spell Otiluke's resilient sphere}

subclassFeature.name: Emboldening Bond
entries: {@i 1st-level Peace Domain feature}

You can forge an empowering bond among people who are at peace with one another. As an action, you choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you (this can include yourself) equal to your proficiency bonus. You create a magical bond among them for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again. While any bonded creature is within 30 feet of another, the creature can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw it makes. Each creature can add the {@dice d4} no more than once per turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary
entries: {@i 2nd-level Twilight Domain feature}
You can use your Channel Divinity to refresh your allies with soothing twilight.

As an action, you present your holy symbol, and a sphere of twilight emanates from you. The sphere is centered on you, has a 30-foot radius, and is filled with dim light. The sphere moves with you, and it lasts for 1 minute or until you are {@condition incapacitated} or die. Whenever a creature (including you) ends its turn in the sphere, you can grant that creature one of these benefits:

items: You grant it temporary hit points equal to {@dice 2d4}. This amount changes when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to {@dice 3d4} at level 5, {@dice 4d4} at level 9, {@dice 5d4} at level 13 and {@dice 6d4} at level 17.
You use your reaction to end one effect on it causing it to be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Land
entries: {@i Celebrate Connection to the Natural World}

The Circle of the Land comprises mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites. These Druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of their communities.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Moon
entries: {@i Adopt Animal Forms to Guard the Wilds}
Druids of the Circle of the Moon draw on lunar magic to transform themselves. Their order gathers under the moon to share news and perform rituals.

Changeable as the moon, a Druid of this circle might prowl as a great cat one night, soar over the treetops as an eagle the next day, and then crash through undergrowth as a bear to drive off a trespassing monster. The wild is in the Druid's blood.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Forms
entries: You can channel lunar magic when you assume a Wild Shape form, granting you the benefits below.

entries.name: Challenge Rating
entries: The maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} for the form equals your Druid level divided by 3 (round down).

entries.name: Armor Class
entries: Until you leave the form, your AC equals 13 plus your Wisdom modifier if that total is higher than the Beast's AC.

entries.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half of the forms hit points + two times your Druid level.

subclassFeature.name: Moonlight Mastery
entries: Your body attunes to the phases of the moon. You gain the following benefits.

subclassFeature.name: Moonlight Step
entries: You magically transport yourself, reappearing amid a burst of moonlight. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll you make before the end of this turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also regain uses by expending a level 2+ spell slot for each use you want to restore (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Wild Shape
entries: At 10th level, you can expend two uses of Wild Shape at the same time to transform into an elemental. Choose one of {@creature air elemental}, {@creature earth elemental}, {@creature fire elemental}, or a {@creature water elemental}. You learn and add this form to your wild shape. You can change the chosen elemental form whenever you gain a level in this class.
You learn an additionl elemental form when you reach 14th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: The Archfey
entries: Your patron is a lord or lady of the fey, a creature of legend who holds secrets that were forgotten before the mortal races were born. This being's motivations are often inscrutable, and sometimes whimsical, and might involve a striving for greater magical power or the settling of age-old grudges. Beings of this sort include the Prince of Frost; the Queen of Air and Darkness, ruler of the Gloaming Court; Titania of the Summer Court; her consort Oberon, the Green Lord; Hyrsam, the Prince of Fools; and ancient hags.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Archfey lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. Each of these spells count as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Fey Presence
entries: {@i 1st-level Archfey feature}

Starting at 1st level, your patron bestows upon you the ability to project the beguiling and fearsome presence of the fey. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot radius originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. The creatures that fail their saving throws are all {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Steps of the Fey
entries: {@i 6th-level Archfey feature}
Starting at 6th level, your patron bestows you the ability to move between boundaries of the planes.

subclassFeature.name: Tricky Transposition
entries: You can cast {@spell misty step} without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
In addition, whenever you cast that spell, you immediately use your Fey Presence feature, without expending its use.

subclassFeature.name: Misty Escape
entries: You can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. You can cast {@spell misty step} as a reaction in response to taking damage.
In addition, whenever you cast that spell, you can choose one of the following additional effects instead of using Fey Presence.

subclassFeature.name: Disappearing Step
entries: You have the {@condition invisible} condition until the start of your next turn or until immediately after you make an attack roll or cast a spell.

subclassFeature.name: Dreadful Step
entries: Creatures within 5 feet of the space you left or the space you appear in (your choice) must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or take {@dice 2d10} Psychic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Beguiling Defenses
entries: {@i 10th-level Archfey feature}
Your patron teaches you how to guard your mind and body. You are immune to the {@condition charmed} condition.

In addition, immediately after a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage you take by half (round down), and you can force that attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker takes Psychic damage equal to the damage you take.
Once you use this reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot when you use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Guardian Coil
entries: {@i 6th-level Fathomless feature}

Your Tentacle of the Deeps can defend you and others, interposing itself between them and harm. When you or a creature you can see takes damage while within 10 feet of the tentacle, you can use your reaction to choose one of those creatures and reduce the damage to that creature by {@dice 2d8}. Additionally, the next attack made by the tentacle has a bonus to its damage equal to the amount it reduced.

subclassFeature.name: Grasping Tentacles
entries: {@i 10th-level Fathomless feature}

You learn the spell {@spell Evard's black tentacles}. It counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know. You can also cast it twice without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

Whenever you cast this spell, your patron's magic bolsters you, granting you a number of temporary hit points equal to your warlock level. Moreover, damage can't break your {@status concentration} on this spell.

subclassFeature.name: The Fiend
entries: {@i 1st-level Fiend feature}

You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Fiends powerful enough to forge a pact include demon lords such as Demogorgon, Orcus, Fraz'Urb-luu, and Baphomet; archdevils such as Asmodeus, Dispater, Mephistopheles, and Belial; pit fiends and balors that are especially mighty; and ultroloths and other lords of the yugoloths.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Fiend lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. Each of these spells count as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Dark One's Blessing
entries: {@i 1st-level Fiend feature}

Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1). You also gain this benefit if someone else reduces an enemy within 10 feet of you to 0 hitpoints.

subclassFeature.name: Dark One's Own Luck
entries: {@i 6th-level Fiend feature}

You can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a {@dice d10} to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Fiendish Resilience
entries: {@i 10th-level Fiend feature}
You can choose two damage types when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

subclassFeature.name: The Great Old One
entries: {@i 1st-level Great Old One feature}

Your patron is a mysterious entity whose nature is utterly foreign to the fabric of reality. It might come from the Far Realm, the space beyond reality, or it could be one of the elder gods known only in legends. Its motives are incomprehensible to mortals, and its knowledge so immense and ancient that even the greatest libraries pale in comparison to the vast secrets it holds. The Great Old One might be unaware of your existence or entirely indifferent to you, but the secrets you have learned allow you to draw your magic from it. Entities of this type include Ghaunadar, called That Which Lurks; Tharizdun, the Chained God; Dendar, the Night Serpent; Zargon, the Returner; Great Cthulhu; and other unfathomable beings.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Great Old One lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. Each of these spells count as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Awakened Mind
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can form a telepathic connection between your mind and the mind of another. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself and create a telepathic bond. You and the chosen creature can speak telepathically with each other while the two of you are within a number of miles equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 mile). To understand each other, you must speak mentally in a language the other knows.

The telepathic connection lasts for a number of minutes equal to your Warlock level. It ends early if you have the {@condition incapacitated} condition or die, or if you use this feature to form a connection with a different creature.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Spells
entries: When you cast a Warlock spell that deals damage, you can change its damage type to Psychic. In addition, when you cast a Warlock spell that is from the Enchantment or Illusion school of magic, you can do so without verbal or somatic components.

subclassFeature.name: Clairvoyant Combatant
entries: {@i 6th-level Great Old One feature}

You learn to read the attacks of minds you touch. When you form a telepathic bond with a creature with your Awakened Mind feature, you can force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature for the duraton of the bond.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a spell slot of level 2 or higher (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Eldritch Hex
entries: {@i 10th-level Great Old One feature}

Your alien patron grants you a powerful curse. You always have the {@spell hex} spell prepared. When you cast Hex and choose an ability, the target also has Disadvantage on saving throws of the chosen ability for the duration of the spell.

subclassFeature.name: The Hexblade
entries: You have made your pact with a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell—a force that manifests in sentient magic weapons carved from the stuff of shadow. The mighty sword Blackrazor is the most notable of these weapons, which have been spread across the multiverse over the ages. The shadowy force behind these weapons can offer power to warlocks who form pacts with it. Many hexblade warlocks create weapons that emulate those formed in the Shadowfell. Others forgo such arms, content to weave the dark magic of that plane into their spellcasting.

Because the Raven Queen is known to have forged the first of these weapons, many sages speculate that she and the force are one and that the weapons, along with hexblade warlocks, are tools she uses to manipulate events on the Material Plane to her inscrutable ends.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Hexblade lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. Each of these spells count as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Hex Warrior (Variant)
entries: {@i 1st-level Hexblade feature}
You acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

subclassFeature.name: The Raven Queen
entries: Your patron is the Raven Queen, a mysterious being who rules the Shadowfell from a palace of ice deep within that dread realm. The Raven Queen watches over the world, anticipating each creature's death and ensuring that it meets its end at the proscribed time and place. Warlocks sworn to the Raven Queen receive visions and whispers from her in their dreams, sending them on quests and warning them of impending dangers.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Raven Queen lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. Each of these spells count as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Sentinel's Vigilance
entries: {@i 1st-level Raven Queen feature}

Starting at 1st level, the Raven Queen grants you a Raven spirit that watches over you. A spectral raven only you or a creature with truesight can see, appears perched on your shoulders. It cannot be targeted by any spell or attack and cannot take any damage. It grants you advantage on death saving throws and bonus to perception checks equal to your charisma modifier.

You can send your raven spirit to protect those on the border of life and death. As a bonus action on your turn or as a reaction when a creature rolls a death saving throw while within 30 ft of you, you stabilize the dying creature and grant it the effects of the Sanctuary spell. You can use this feature proficiency bonus number of times per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Boon of the Raven Spirit
entries: {@i 6th-level Raven Queen feature}

Starting at 6th level, the raven spirit empowers your mind and modicum of power granted to you by your patron. You gain immunity to the frightened condition. In addition, your chosen pact boon is improved as shown below.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Chain
entries: Your familiar gains a bonus to it's hit point maximum equal to twice your warlock level and it's proficiency bonus scales with your proficiency bonus. While your familiar is alive, you and your familiar get advantage on ability checks using skills for which you both have proficiency. Your familiar can now share the same initiative as you and take it's turn during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Blade
entries: Your pact weapon deals an extra 1d6 damage when it hits. You can change the damage type of your pact weapon to necrotic or cold when you deal damage to a creature with it. Additionally when you hit a creature, it must succeed on a constitution saving throw against your spell save dc or be restrained until the end of your next turn. You can do so for a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Talisman
entries: When you perform the ritual to receive an amulet, you receive a number of amulets equal to half your proficiency bonus(rounded up). The number of uses on the features provided by these talismans to their wearers are shared by all the talismans, but they recharge on a short rest instead of a long rest. When a talisman wearer uses one of it's features, they get temporary hitpoints equal to your warlock level.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Tome
entries: When you deal necrotic or cold damage through spells, you can add your proficiency bonus to the damage dealt. During a long rest, you can prepare a number of spells equal to your proficiency bonus from the spell list of any class, for which you have spell slots for, and these spells are considered as warlock spells for you. The spells prepared in such a way do not count towards the number of spells known by you.

subclassFeature.name: Aegis of the Ravens
entries: {@i 10th-level Raven Queen feature}
The Raven spirit granted to you has influenced your physique, over the course of it's companionship. You gain resistance to cold and necrotic damage.

As a bonus action, you can manifest spectral raven wings that give you magical flight with flying speed equal to your movement speed for one minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

As an action, you can assume the appearance and statistics of a raven, once per long rest. You gain a bonus to stealth checks equal to your charisma modifier, a flying speed equal to 100 ft and you can stay in this form for a number of hours equal to your charisma modifier. You can't cast any spells, but you can concentrate on spells while in this form.

While in this form, you are vulnerable to all damage and the damage you take cannot be reduced in any way, including resistances. Any damage taken in this form is carried over and reduced from your hitpoints. If you were flying while you take damage, then you lose the form immediately and start falling, unless you have a way to prevent it. However, you only take half the fall damage in this situation.

subclassFeature.name: Queen's Eminent
entries: {@i 14th-level Raven Queen feature}

You get blessed by the Raven Queen herself for your service that has been matched by few. As a bonus action you can now channel your Raven spirit to supercharge your pact boon, as described below. The effect remains until you end it as an action, the duration ends, you fall unconcious or you become incapacitated. You can use this feature once per short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Chain
entries: For one minute, your familiar becomes immune to all damage. It's movement speed is doubled and once per turn, while delivering a touch range spell using it's reaction, it can deal extra necrotic damage or heal the target creature for an amount equal to your charisma modifier. It loses the ability to take the attack action and gains two new actions - 'Imperil' and 'Shelter'.

When the familiar takes the 'Imperil' action, it gives advantage to the first attack roll every turn until the start of it's next turn, against one hostile creature that is within 15 feet of it and on a hit by an attack roll with the advantage, the familiar adds 1d8 cold damage to the damage dealt by the attack.

When the familiar takes the 'Shelter' action, it gives disadvantage to the first attack roll every turn until the start of it's next turn, against one allied creature that is within 15 feet of it and allied creatures within 15 feet of it regain the maximum number of hit points possible from any healing.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Blade
entries: For one minute, you enter a state of frenzy and you become unable to cast spells for the same duration. Your pact weapon deals a critical when you roll 19 or 20 on the d20 for the attack roll and once per turn, you take the maximum possible result on any damage die when you land a critical hit with your pact weapon.

While in the state of frenzy, when you take damage that reduces you to 0 hit points and doesn't kill you outright, you do not fall unconcious until the end of your next turn. Taking damage in this state causes death saving throw failures as normal and three failures can still kill you.

On the subsequent turn after you activate this feature, you can only take the attack action to make attacks with your pact weapon and at the end of your turn, you heal for half the highest damage dealt by you in a single attack. This feature can be used only once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Talisman
entries: For one minute, all the talisman wearers can choose to be resistant to one type of damage at the start of their turn(no action required). When any of the wearers regain hitpoints from any spell or feature, all of the wearers regain hitpoints equal to your charisma modifier.

For the same duration, all talisman wearers take the maximum possible result on dice rolls when using any of the features granted by the talisman. The creature that gains temporary health from using a feature of the talisman, adds your charisma modifier when calculating the total temporary health it receives.

subclassFeature.name: Pact of the Tome
entries: For one minute, your spells ignore resistance to cold and necrotic damage. Once per turn for the same duration, you can reroll the damage dice for your cold and necrotic damage spells upto a number of dice equal to your charisma modifier. Once during this one minute duration, you can push the limits of your sepllcasting.

When you deal necrotic or cold damage using a spell, you take the maximum possible result on all damage dice. If you reduce any creature to zero hitpoints while using this feature, you regain the use of this feature. You can only do so once per short rest.

subclassFeature.name: School of Abjuration
entries: {@i Shield Companions and Banish Foes}

Your study of magic is focused on spells that block, banish, or protect—ending harmful effects, banishing evil influences, and protecting the weak. Abjurers are sought when baleful spirits require exorcism, when locations must be guarded against magical spying, and when portals to other planes of existence must be closed. Adventuring parties value Abjurers for the protection they provide against a variety of hostile magic and other attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Abjuration Savant
entries: Choose two Wizard spells from the Abjuration school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Abjuration school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Ward
entries: You can weave magic around yourself for protection. When you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The ward has a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum equal to twice your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead, and if you have any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If the damage reduces the ward to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you take any remaining damage. While the ward has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it can't absorb damage, but its magic remains.

Whenever you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, the ward regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice the level of the spell slot. Alternatively, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a spell slot, and the ward regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice the level of the spell slot expended.
Once you create the ward, you can't create it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: School of Evocation
entries: {@i Create Explosive Elemental Effects}

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.

subclassFeature.name: Evocation Savant
entries: Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Cantrip
entries: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: College of Dance
entries: Bards of the college of Dance know that the Words of Creation can't be contained within speech or even song; they are uttered by the movements of celestial bodies and flow through the motions of even the smallest creatures. To these bards, dance is art freed from the constraints of a single point in space and time; it is meaning unconfined by narrow definitions of words and structures of grammar. The college of Dance practices a way of being in harmony with the ever-whirling cosmos, emphasizing agility, speed, and grace.

subclassFeature.name: Dazzling Footwork
entries: {@i 3rd-level College of Dance feature}
Your practice of dance gives you the ability to gracefully dodge and make agile strikes. While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield, you gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Unarmored Defense:} Your base armor class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Charisma modifier.

{@b Agile Strikes:} When you expend a use of your Bardic inspiration as part of an Action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction, you can make one Unarmed Strike as part of that Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.

{@b Bardic Damage:} You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack rolls of your Unarmed Strikes, and when you deal damage with an Unarmed Strike, you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to a roll of your Barding Inspiration die plus your Dexterity modifier. This roll doesn't expend the die.

subclassFeature.name: Inspiring Movement
entries: {@i 3rd-level College of Dance feature}

When an enemy you can see ends its turn within 5 feet of an ally of yours who is within 60 feet of you, you can use your Reaction and expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to move up to half your Speed. Then roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and the ally can move up to a number of feet equal to 5 times the numebr rolled. None of this feature's movement provokes Opportunity Attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Leading Evasion
entries: {@i 6th-level College of Dance feature}

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and you take only half damage if you fail. If any creatures within 5 feet of you are making the same Dexterity saving throw, you can share this benefit with them for that save.
You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition incapacitated} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Tandem Footwork
entries: {@i 6th-level College of Dance feature}

When you roll initiative, you can spend one use of your Bardic Inspiration if you don't have the {@condition incapacitated} condition. When you do so, roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and choose a number of creatures within 60 feet of yourself (you can choose yourself), up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). Each of them gains a bonus to their Initiative equal to the number rolled.

subclassFeature.name: Irresistible Dance
entries: {@i 14th-level College of Dance feature}

You always have the {@spell Otto's irresistible dance} spell prepared. You can cast it without expending a spell slot. Once you cast this spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of the feature by expending three uses of your bardic inspiration (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: College of the Moon
entries: {@i Inspire Allies with Primal Tales}

The College of the Moon traces its origins to the ancient druidic circles of the Moonshae Isles, who entrusted the first Bards of this tradition with chronicling the stories of the islands and their people. Bards of this college draw from the isles' fey magic and the primal power of the moonwells to bolster their allies, protect the natural world, and inspire their bardic works.

subclassFeature.name: Blessing of Moonlight
entries: You always have the {@spell Moonbeam|XPHB} spell prepared.

When you cast {@spell Moonbeam|XPHB}, you can modify the spell so that you glow faintly while the spell is active. While glowing, you shed {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} out to 5 feet, and whenever a creature fails its saving throw against the effects of this Moonbeam, another creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself regains {@dice 2d4} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature to modify a casting of Moonbeam, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Eventide's Splendor
entries: You become suffused with the might of the moon, improving your Moon's Inspiration in the following ways.

entries.name: Shadow of the New Moon
entries: When you use Inspired Eclipse, the creature who received the Bardic Inspiration die can also have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition and immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. The creature remains {@condition Invisible|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Vibrance of the Full Moon
entries: When you use Lunar Vitality, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and use the number rolled in place of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Aberrant Scourge
entries: One fine morning, you wake up to realise that you have a worm companion residing in your brain. Whether it obeys your will or you have been completely subdued by it is unclear. However, what is clear is that you have formed an unusual relationship with it - Symbiosis. As you gain levels in this class, your control over your mutation increases and you will be able to pioneer a path that has never been explored before.

subclassFeature.name: Awakening
entries: {@i 3rd-level Aberrant Scourge feature}

You can now communicate telepathically with one creature within 60 ft of you at a time and they can respond back to you telepathically. The creature must not be hostile to you and must understand atleast one language. You also understand and can communicate in Deep Speech.

You can attempt to grapple a creature when you enter rage and once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or an unarmed strike. If a creature is moved forcibly while being {@condition grappled} by you, you can also move to keep grappling the creature. The amount of movement used up in such a way cannot exceed your total movement speed and is reduced from the distance you can move on your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Transmogrification
entries: {@i 6th-level Aberrant Scourge feature}
When you successfully grapple a creature or start your turn while grappling a creature, you can choose to deal Psychic damage equal to your Strength modifier and gain one charge of wrath.

When attempting to grapple, you can do so telekinetically as translucent tentacles visible only to you and the target creature, wraps around the target creature. The maximum range for the telekinetic grapple extends to within 10 ft of you or upto the reach of your melee weapon, if it is higher.
You also get to choose one focus from the two options listed below. You can change your chosen focus on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mind Path
entries: You are immune to magic that allows other creatures to read your thoughts or determine whether you are lying. You gain resistance to Psychic damage (the resistance becomes immunity when you reach level 17 in this subclass). While raging, you can use your Strength modifier in place of Intelligence when subjected to Intelligence saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Body Path
entries: When you enter rage, you can choose to grow upto one size larger (upto two sizes larger when you reach level 17 in this subclass) and while you are raging, you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition incapacitated}, {@condition stunned}, {@condition paralyzed} or {@condition unconscious}.

subclassFeature.name: Metamorphosis
entries: {@i 10th-level Aberrant Scourge feature}

You have immunity to the {@condition charmed} and {@condition frightened} conditions while you are raging and you dispel any of these conditions on yourself when you start raging. When a {@condition grappled} creature deals damage to you, you can immediately use your reaction to make one melee weapon attack or unarmed strike against it.
You also get to choose one focus from the two options listed below and you can choose a different focus from the one you chose previously. You can now change your chosen focus on a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mind Path
entries: When you are grappling a creature and you use the Reckless Attack feature, the {@condition grappled} creature must roll an Intelligence saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) and on a failure, it is {@condition stunned} until the start of your next turn. This effect is dispelled from the {@condition grappled} creature if your rage ends or if it is not {@condition grappled} by you anymore.

subclassFeature.name: Body Path
entries: For every 7 damage you take while raging, you can deal Psychic damage equal to one roll of your wrath die to the {@condition grappled} creature.

subclassFeature.name: Transcendent Causatum
entries: {@i 14th-level Aberrant Scourge feature}

When attempting to grapple a creature telekinetically, a translucent illithid form of you appears instead of tentacles to grapple the target, and it is visible only to you and the target creature. Your illithid form is one size larger than you and grows or shrinks to maintain the size difference if your size changes. Any creature can move freely through or end its turn inside the space occupied by your illithid form and it provides no cover to other creatures.

When you are grappling a creature, you gain a +2 bonus to your AC and your movement speeds increase by 10ft. While raging you also gain a bonus to your Attack Rolls, Ability Checks and Saving Throws equal to the number of creatures you are grappling.
You also get to choose one focus from the two options listed below and you can choose a different focus from the one you chose previously. You can now change your chosen focus when you enter rage.

subclassFeature.name: Mind Path
entries: A {@condition grappled} creature attempting to use any means to end the {@condition grappled} condition on itself must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) to be able to use those features. It gains a penalty to the save equal to the number of turns it spent being grappled by you in the last minute. When a creature dies while it is {@condition grappled} by you, you regain hitpoints equal to your barbarian level and you gain 4 wrath charges.

subclassFeature.name: Body Path
entries: You can grapple a maximum of three creatures at the same time with your illithid form. When you use a subclass feature to affect a creature that you have {@condition grappled}, you can choose any number of creatures that are also {@condition grappled} by you to be affected simultaneously. When a creature dies while it is {@condition grappled} by you, you regain hitpoints equal to half your barbarian level and you gain 2 wrath charges.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Frostwarden
entries: There exist a small but tight knit community of people that brave the harsh winters and the frozen lands. Growing in such extreme weather has conditioned their physique extensively and many of these people are also blessed by the Beast of Winter. Thus they become powerful guardians of their land and are adept at protecting their kinsman. As you gain levels in this class, your abilities will shape you to become an exemplary protector that commands the cold.

subclassFeature.name: Rimed Aegis
entries: {@i 3rd-level Frostwarden feature}
While raging, whenever a creature hits you for the first time on a turn, it takes Cold damage equal to your Barbarian level.

When you finish a long rest, you can sacrifice any amount of hitpoints that you have to the {@color Beast of Winter|#33ffff}. Your maximum hitpoints is also reduced by that amount but you obtain the {@b Frozen Bulwark} that has hitpoints equal to the amount of hitpoints you sacrificed, until you finish your next long rest. When you take damage, it is reduced from your {@b Frozen Bulwark} before it is reduced from your hitpoints. However you can only restore hitpoints to your {@b Frozen Bulwark} when you deal wrath damage by an amount equal to the total rolled by your wrath dice.

As a bonus action, you can emit a blast of chillness around you upto 20ft away. Hostile creatures within range must roll a Constitution saving throw(DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) and on a failure they receive the {@b Winter's Mark} until the end of your next turn. Creatures with {@b Winter's Mark} have their movement speed reduced by 10ft and once per turn when they take Cold damage, they take additional Cold damage equal to one roll of your Wrath die. When you use this bonus action when a creature already has {@b Winter's Mark}, it must roll the saving throw again regardless of how far away it is from you.

subclassFeature.name: Frigid Mantle
entries: {@i 6th-level Frostwarden feature}
While raging, you gain resistance to Cold damage and your weapon can deal Cold damage instead of its usual damage type.

While your {@b Frozen Bulwark} has atleast 1 hitpoint, you radiate the {@b Sentinel Aura} upto 10ft from you. Hostile creatures within the aura are taunted and have disadvantage on any attack roll that isn't against you.
When you Reckless Attack, your critical hit range is increased by 1 for any opportunity attack you make against creatures within your {@b Sentinel Aura}.

subclassFeature.name: Arctic Retribution
entries: {@i 10th-level Frostwarden feature}
You permanently gain Cold resistance and all Cold damage you deal pierces resistance to it.
While raging, you now deal the Cold damage equal to your Barbarian level whenever a creature deals damage to you for the first time on a turn instead of just when they hit you.
While raging, whenever a hostile creature starts its turn within 10ft of you while you are not {@condition incapacitated}, you apply {@b Winter's Mark} on it.

subclassFeature.name: Cryogenic Ire
entries: {@i 14th-level Frostwarden feature}
While raging you also gain resistance to Fire damage and immunity to the {@condition prone} condition.
When you Reckless Attack, your critical hit range is now increased by 1 for any melee attack roll you make against creatures within your {@b Sentinel Aura}, instead of just opportunity attacks.
Creatures with {@b Winter's Mark} are now affected by {@b Sentinel Aura} regardless of how far away it is from you.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Pulsing Engine
entries: At some point in history, a mad scientist wanted to combine two things that were fundamentally incompatible: Spellcasting and Raging. The multiple trials and decades of research information culminated in one prospective solution. A magical item that can forcefully channel mana into a Barbarian to allow them to cast spells while raging. When it was first attempted, the results ranged from horrendous disconfiguration to death by mana overload. By carefully tuning it's power capacity and refining it's working principle, the Arcane Heart was created: a mechanical pacemaker that also functioned as a magical core, allowing a Barbarian to cast spells by expending their life force while raging.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: {@i 3rd-level Pulsing Engine feature}

When you reach 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast spells through your Arcane Heart. Choose one of Sorcerer, Warlock or Wizard spell list. Your Arcane Heart will be able to learn and store spells from only that class' spell list.

Casting a spell while you are raging causes you to take {@b 10 Necrotic damage} that cannot be reduced in any way. You can maintain concentration on any spell you cast, only until the start of your next turn while you are raging, at which point you inevitably drop concentration on them.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice. You learn another cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

entries.name: Arcane Heart charges (Spell Slots)
entries: The Pulsing Engine Features table shows how many Arcane Heart charges you have to cast your Pulsing Engine spells. The table also shows the level of those charges, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Arcane Heart charges when you finish a Long Rest.

For example, when you're a level 5 Pulsing Engine, you have two level 2 Arcane Heart charges. To cast the level 1 spell Witch Bolt, you must spend one of those charges, and you cast it as a level 2 spell.

entries.name: Arcane Heart level (Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher)
entries: The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Barbarian levels, as shown in the Spells Known column of the Barbarian Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Arcane Heart Level column for your level. When you reach level 7, for example, you learn a new spell, which can be of levels 1 or 2.
Whenever you gain a Barbarian level, you can replace one spell on your list with another spell of an eligible level from your chosen spell list.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Constitution is your spellcasting ability for your spells, since your spells are stored in your Arcane Heart. You use your Constitution whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Constitution modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use your Arcane Heart as a spellcasting focus for your Pulsing Engine spells.

subclassFeature.name: Mana Frenzy
entries: {@i 3rd-level Pulsing Engine feature}
You gain access to cantrips and level 1 spells. Your Arcane Heart works as a spellcasting focus for your spells, and you add your Constitution modifier to any Arcana skill check you make.
While raging, Arcana checks you make have advantage and casting a spell by expending a charge of your Arcane Heart grants you 10 Temporary Hitpoints.

subclassFeature.name: Seamless Overdrive
entries: {@i 6th-level Pulsing Engine feature}

You gain access to level 2 spells. Additionally, when you make a {@dice d20} Roll, you can roll the wrath die you get at your current level and add it as a bonus to the roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
When you take the attack action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

subclassFeature.name: Auxiliary Power
entries: {@i 10th-level Pulsing Engine feature}
You gain access to level 3 spells. You gain resistance to Force damage and while raging, your weapon can deal Force damage instead of it's usual damage type.
Once per long rest, you can use your Bonus action to regain hitpoints equal to half your maximum hitpoint, and you also gain the maximum amount of Wrath charges you can hold.

subclassFeature.name: Brutal Clarity
entries: {@i 14th-level Pulsing Engine feature}
While raging, you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and any attack rolls for spells have Disadvantage against you.
You can now maintain concentration on spells you cast by taking {@b 10 Necrotic damage} at the start of each of your turns. This Necrotic damage can't be reduced in any way.

subclassFeature.name: The Raven Queen
entries: Your patron is the Raven Queen, a mysterious being who rules the Shadowfell from a palace of ice deep within that dread realm. The Raven Queen watches over the world, anticipating each creature's death and ensuring that it meets its end at the proscribed time and place. Warlocks sworn to the Raven Queen receive visions and whispers from her in their dreams, sending them on quests and warning them of impending dangers.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Raven Queen lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

subclassFeature.name: Sentinel's Vigilance
entries: {@i 1st-level Raven Queen feature}

Starting at 1st level, the Raven Queen grants you a Raven spirit that watches over you. A spectral raven that only you, a creature you allow or a creature with truesight can see appears perched on your shoulders. It cannot be targeted by any spell, magical effect or attack and cannot take any damage. It grants you advantage on Death saving throws and can keep watch while you are resting, waking you up when it senses anything within 60ft of you using your senses and ability checks.

You can send your Raven spirit to protect those on the border of life and death. As a bonus action on your turn or as a reaction when a creature is about to roll a Death Saving Throw while within 30 ft of you, you stabilize the dying creature and grant it the effects of the {@spell Sanctuary} spell.
