A creature stabilized from a use of this feature can choose to make Death saving throws at the start of each of its turns and it regains 1 hitpoint after one minute or when it rolls 3 successes on its Death saving throws. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Boon of the Raven Spirit
entries: {@i 6th-level Raven Queen feature}

Starting at 6th level, the raven spirit empowers your mind and the modicum of power granted to you by your patron. You gain immunity to the {@condition frightened} condition. In addition, one of your chosen pact boons becomes your Prime Pact Boon and it is improved as shown below.

items: Your familiar can now share the same initiative as you and take its turn during your turn. You can telepathically communicate with your familiar and perceive through its senses as long as you are on the same plane of existence.

Your familiar's proficiency bonus is equal to your proficiency bonus. While your familiar is alive, you and your familiar get advantage on ability checks using skills for which the both of you share proficiency.

When your familiar is targeted by an attack or is about to roll a saving throw, you can use your reaction to dismiss your familiar to its pocket dimension and return to that space at the start of your next turn. When you do so, it does not take any damage from the triggering effect.
Your pact weapon deals an extra {@dice 1d6} damage when it hits.
When you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can cause the pact weapon to deal Cold damage.

When you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can choose to curse it until you take a short or long rest. You can only have one creature cursed at a time. You have advantage on Wisdom(Perception) checks against the cursed creature and it does not benefit from the {@condition Invisible} condition against you.
When you perform the ritual to receive an amulet, you receive a number of amulets equal to your proficiency bonus.
The number of uses on the features provided by these talismans are shared by all the talismans, but they recharge on a short rest instead of a long rest.
When a talisman wearer uses one of its expendable/rechargeable features, they can choose to gain temporary hitpoints equal to your Warlock level.
When you deal Necrotic or Cold damage through spells, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.
Once per long rest, when you can cast a Warlock spell with a spell slot you can do so as if the spell slot expended was one level higher.

During a long rest, you can prepare 2 spells(upto 5th lvl) from the Wizard, Sorcerer or Bard spell list and these spells are considered as Warlock spells for you. The spells prepared in such a way do not count towards the number of spells known by you.
While wearing the cloak, you are under the effects of {@spell Nondetection} spell.

You have the {@spell Blink} spell always prepared and you can cast it once per short rest without expending a spell slot. For the duration of the spell, you can use your reaction to reroll the {@dice d6} and if either roll succeeds you can choose either yourself or an allied creature within 30ft of you to be affected by the spell.
You gain proficiency in Dexterity(Stealth) checks and your proficiency bonus is doubled when making them.
Your pact weapon's short and long range is increased by 15 ft and 45 ft respectively. The sound of shots fired with your pact weapon can only be heard while within 60 ft of you.
When you attack a creature with your pact weapon, you can have it deal Necrotic or Cold damage instead of its normal damage type.
When a hostile creature ends its turn within 5ft of you, you can move upto 10ft without provoking attack of opportunity.

subclassFeature.name: Aegis of the Ravens
entries: {@i 10th-level Raven Queen feature}

The Raven spirit granted to you has influenced your physique, over the course of its companionship. You gain resistance to Cold and Necrotic damage. You also gain one Eldritch Invocation of your choice, which must have a prerequisite of your chosen Prime Pact Boon and you must meet the warlock level requirement(if any).

As a bonus action, you can manifest spectral raven wings that give you magical flight with flying speed equal to your movement speed for one minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Queen's Eminent
entries: {@i 14th-level Raven Queen feature}

You get blessed by the Raven Queen herself for your service that has been matched by few. You can choose to replace your 6th and 7th level Mystic Arcanum with a spell of the same level from the Wizard spell list.

The Raven spirit grants you celerity and an uncanny sense of intuition. Your movement speed increases by 10ft and a hostile creature cannot benefit from advantage on attacks against you as a result of being unseen.
Your Prime Pact Boon is also improved as described below.

items: When you cast a Warlock spell that doesn't have a range of 'self', you can do so as if you were in your familiar's place. Your familiar adds your Charisma modifier as a bonus to all Attack Rolls, Ability Checks and Saving Throws it makes.

Attacks you make with your pact weapon are critical hits on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}. You can take the maximum possible result on the base damage die of your pact weapon when you hit a creature with it.

The dice for features provided by the talismans increase by one size. Once per round when a talisman wearer rolls dice for a feature granted by the talisman, they can roll twice and choose the higher result.
At the end of a rest, each talisman wearer gains resistance to one damage type of your choice until the next time they take a rest.

When you cast a Warlock spell with a spell slot, you can reroll a number of damage dice equal to your Charisma modifier. Once per short rest when you cast a Warlock spell that deals Cold or Necrotic damage, you take the maximum possible result on all damage dice on the turn you cast the spell.

Your cloak's storage space is now connected to a Demiplane. When storing or retrieving items in the cloak the weight and size restrictions no longer apply. You can also store and retrieve allied creatures that are directly under your command (ex: Summons, familiars, etc) in the cloak.

Once per short rest as a bonus action you can fill a sphere of 30ft radius with the energy of Shadowfell plane for one minute, and you can move the area upto 30ft as a bonus action. The area is filled with magical Dim Light and hostile creatures have disadvantage on attacks against allied creatures in the area. Allied creatures are unaffected by the Dim Light and when they enter or are inside the sphere, they can spend 10ft of movement to teleport and end up in another space of their choice within the sphere.

You reroll any 1 or 2 on your pact weapon's damage die when you roll damage. When a creature targets you with an attack or forces you to make a saving throw, immediately after that roll is resolved you can use your reaction to make one attack with your pact weapon against that creature, provided it is within the range of your pact weapon.

subclassFeature.name: The Crazed Architect
entries: Your patron is the Crazed Architect, a being who severed itself from reality in its obsession to make the most technologically advanced weapons. Now it reaches out to mortals from its workshop and shares with them a fraction of its works to test their performance. Pactmakers that show promise might even be blessed with some of its knowledge and access to its workshop.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Crazed Architect lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

subclassFeature.name: Tools for the Job
entries: {@i 1st-level Crazed Architect feature}

Starting at 1st level, you gain proficiency in firearms and {@item tinker's tools|XPHB}. If you already have proficiency in {@item tinker's tools|XPHB}, you can get proficiency in another {@item artisan's tools|XPHB} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: The Crazed Architect's Accord
entries: {@i 1st-level Crazed Architect feature}

Your patron gifts you the {@b Composite Weapons Casing(CWC)}. The CWC let's you copy the data of any firearm but destroys them in the process. As a free action, you can generate a firearm whose data has already been analysed and stored in the CWC. A firearm generated by the CWC disintegrates after ten minutes or if a creature other than you tries to wield it.

You ignore any misfire chance on a firearm generated by your CWC. As an action, you can transform your CWC into a trinket that you can wear on yourself and back to its original form. When you generate a firearm that has the two-handed property, your CWC transforms into a trinket on your person as part of the free action. When you try to attack using a firearm that is not generated by the CWC, it automatically misfires.

Additionally, when you are holding your CWC in one of your hands, you gain a bonus to your AC as if you were holding a shield and the hand holding the CWC counts as a free hand for the purpose of casting spells with somatic component. Your CWC qualifies as a weapon for your pact boon and its invocations. Any firearm generated by the CWC automatically benefits from those features as well.

subclassFeature.name: Synchronicity
entries: {@i 1st-level Crazed Architect feature}

Whenever you make an attack with a firearm, you gain a stack of {@b 'Synchronicity'}. You can have a maximum of three stacks and you lose all stacks of {@b 'Synchronicity'} when you end your turn without attacking with your firearm. You gain the following benefits based on the number of {@b 'Synchronicity'} stacks you have:
1 - Your movement speed increases by 10 ft.
2 - You gain +1 to your AC and Saving Throws.
3 - Attack rolls you make with firearms cannot be affected by disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Armament Barrage
entries: {@i 6th-level Crazed Architect feature}

When an allied creature(including you) within 40 ft of you is critically hit by a hostile creature, or an allied creature(excluding you) within 40 ft of you critically hits a hostile creature, you can use your reaction to make one attack with a firearm against that hostile creature, provided it is within the range of your firearm.

Your CWC also offers limited arcane capabilities, as you are now able to store one spell in it, that you cast with an action and a spell slot. The spell is stored in your CWC until you finish a long rest, at which point the spell effect dissipates without activating. You can activate the spell stored in your CWC as a bonus action.

subclassFeature.name: Zero Energy Loss
entries: {@i 10th-level Crazed Architect feature}

You gain expertise in {@item tinker's tools|XPHB} and if a magical effect or spell affects Space(ex: Graviturgy magic) or Time(ex: Chronurgy magic), you can identify that nature without an ability check. However you must make the required ability check to identify the complete effects and you get a bonus to the check equal to your Charisma modifier.

Whenever you expend a Warlock spell slot, your CWC gains a {@b 'ZEL'} charge. Your CWC can have a maximum amount of {@b 'ZEL'} charges equal to the maximum amount of Warlock spell slots you have according to your Warlock level. Your CWC retains the charges until you take a short or long rest, at which point it resets to zero charges. You can expend a charge as a bonus action to perform one of the following special actions:

{@bold Falling Blast} - You throw your CWC upto 30 ft away and then teleport to catch it, landing in the spot you threw it. You may then make one weapon attack against a creature within 10 ft of where you left.

{@bold Glimpse Maneuver} - You can only choose this special action if your movement speed is not 0 from any condition affecting you and when you do so, choose a space within 10 ft of you. Until the end of your turn, your movement speed increases by an amount equal to (5*proficiency bonus)ft, and you are not affected by difficult terrain or reductions to your speed. For the duration, you can also move freely in any direction and move through any matter but you cannot end your movement in a space that is occupied. At the end of your turn, you teleport back to the space you chose or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

{@bold Bullet Raid} - You choose a point within 5 ft of you and then teleport 20 ft away from where you are. Hostile creatures within 20 ft of the point you chose must make a Strength saving throw against your Spell Save DC and on a failure they are pulled in a straight line towards the point, ending in an unoccupied space as close as possible (even if that space is in the air). Immediately after that you spray fire with your firearm at creatures in a 30 ft cone originating from you in any direction, and each creature in the cone must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC, taking {@dice 3d8} piercing damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

{@bold Collapsing Realm} - Until the end of your turn, you do not provoke attack of opportunity and your movement speed is doubled. When you move within 5 ft of a creature, you can move them upto 10 ft in any direction. A hostile creature also takes Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Hypermatrix
entries: {@i 14th-level Crazed Architect feature}

You are now able to perceive the Hypermatrix, a tessellated abstraction of Reality, upto a range of 60 ft from you and you gain a bonus to Wisdom(Perception) and Intelligence(Investigation) within the same range equal to your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Hyperspace Rift
entries: You distort spacetime around you and create the Hyperspace Rift to bring in support from the Multiverse. You can do this as a bonus action, and it lasts for one minute or until you die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a Warlock spell slot to use it again.
The Hyperspace Rift grants the following effects:

items: You can now perceive the Hypermatrix upto a range of 300ft.
You gain one additional reaction you can take each round. You can use only one reaction per triggering effect.

Whenever you gain a Synchronicity stack, an identical looking version of yourself from another timeline appears as a tangible illusion(includes audible, visual, tactile, and olfactory elements) from your space and ends in the nearest unoccupied space to you. The illusion occupies its space and a creature can physically interact with the illusion but doing so let's it make a relevant ability check against your Spell Save DC to realise the illusory nature on a success. At any time you have a number of these illusions equal to the number of Synchronicity stacks you have. When you lose Synchronicity stacks or when this ability ends, all the illusions enter the space you are in and disappear.

Each of these illusions can be individually controlled with mental commands(no action) and they can move upto your movement speed in a turn but cannot leave the range of your Hypermatrix. When you move or take an action you can have your illusions mimic your movements and when you hit a creature with a firearm, all the illusions also attack the creature simultaneously adding 3 extra Force damage for each illusion you have.

While this ability is active, you can use an action to compress the energy used to distort the spacetime around you, thereby ending this ability and creating a gravitational bomb that you shoot at a point within 120ft of you. The bomb then explodes dealing {@dice 4d8} Force damage to all creatures in a 60ft radius and an additional {@dice 3d8} Force damage for each {@b 'ZEL'} charge used since your last rest. A creature takes half the damage on a successful Constitution Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Omen Domain
entries: The Omen Domain consists of priests who act as agents of Fate instead of a particular deity. Their enigmatic personalities and occultic practices earn them a dubious reputation, however there are many accounts of great disasters averted by their forewarning and exemplary people whose lives were turned around by fortuitous encounters that were predicted by them. They are also known to be masters of rituals and divinations, and often choose to remain elusive until they believe their intervention is necessary.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

subclassFeature.name: Seraphic Orison
entries: When you cast a spell with a spell slot to restore hitpoints, you can give one of the creatures affected by the spell a {@b Blessing} die until the end of your next turn. A creature can only hold one {@b Blessing} die at a time and it can expend the die to roll a {@dice d4} and add it to one Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Third Eye
entries: You gain proficiency in Insight skill. You also gain proficiency in either {@item Playing Cards|XPHB} or {@item Three-Dragon Ante Set|XPHB} and you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your cleric spells.

Your Mind's Eye grants you knowledge of mystical rituals. You learn two 1st-level spells with the Ritual tag from any class's spell list and can cast them only as rituals. These spells do not count towards the number of spells you can prepare. You can learn more spells with the Ritual tag by spending 2 hours in meditation and 50 gp of incense for each level of the spell. You can only learn Ritual spells that are equal to or less than the highest Spell level you get to cast from your Cleric levels.

subclassFeature.name: Sanctified Grace
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity as a bonus action to open your spectral eye that appears embedded in your forehead between your brows and gain supernatural means to influence the fate of other creatures for 10 minutes.

During this 10 minutes, whenever you cast a Cleric spell with a spell slot to heal a creature, you can choose another creature within 30ft of yourself to regain {@dice 1d6} hitpoints and also gain a {@b Blessing} die. You also have advantage on Perception and Insight checks for the duration.

subclassFeature.name: Fortune-teller's Paraphernalia
entries: Starting at 6th level, you gain access to the {@table Major Arcana|HEC} deck of the Tarot Cards. When you finish a long rest you can choose a number of Tarot Cards equal to twice your proficiency bonus from the deck and store it in your {@b Concealed Hand}. A creature other than you cannot see the face of the card, only seeing vibrant colours in a swirling pattern on both sides of the card.

You can only play a Tarot Card from your {@b Concealed Hand} and activate either its {@b Upright} or {@b Reversed} effect when you do so. Once you do so, you cannot play another Tarot card until the start of your next turn. The conditions to play the card are in the description of their effects. Once played, a card hovers beside you for the duration of its effect after which it disappears in a flash of bright light returning to your deck.

subclassFeature.name: Fateweaver's Stratagem
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you cast a spell that heals creatures with a 5th level spell slot or lower, roll a {@dice 1d6} and on a 6 you regain the spell slot spent in the casting of the spell. You can recover upto 3 spell slots from this feature between long rests.

When you cast healing spells with a spell slot, you can now give all creatures affected by it a {@b Blessing} die until the end of your next turn. You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to play one Tarot Card from the {@table Major Arcana|HEC} deck that you do not have in your {@b Concealed Hand}.

subclassFeature.name: Hunt Domain
entries: The Hunt Domain is a reclusive order of clerics that have been trained to the extreme for one purpose - to kill all that is unholy. Clerics of this domain are extremely well versed in tracking and eliminating dangerous creatures. They are also known for their ability to survive against all odds and keep fighting in unfair conditions for extended amounts of time.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

entries.caption: Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Freedom of Movement}, {@spell Shadow of Moil|XGE}

subclassFeature.name: Faithbound Arsenal
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency in Survival skill and with firearms. You have advantage on Death Saving Throws. When you are flanked by two or more creatures, you also gain advantage on attacks against them while you remain flanked.

As a special ritual that takes 10 minutes to complete, you {@b Consecrate} upto two weapons of your choice, thereby forming a divine bond with them and granting you the following benefits - you can use them as spellcasting focus for your cleric spells and the hand wielding the weapon can perform the somatic component of your cleric spells.
You can expend one flask of Holy Water as a bonus action to make one of your consecrated weapons deal either Necrotic or Radiant damage in addition to its usual damage type for one minute.

subclassFeature.name: Hallowed Pursuit
entries: When you cast {@spell Hunter's Mark|DRK}, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity, to enter the {@b Bloodlust} state for one minute. Your {@b Bloodlust} state ends when you are {@condition incapacitated} or you die. When your {@b Bloodlust} state is about to end by any other means, you can use your reaction to expend another use of your Channel Divinity to extend the duration of your {@b Bloodlust} state by one minute.

While in {@b Bloodlust} state your movement speed increases by 10ft and you gain the ability to concentrate on another Cleric spell alongside {@spell Hunter's Mark|DRK}. When you fail a concentration saving throw, you lose concentration on both spells and when your {@b Bloodlust} state ends, you must choose one of the two spells to drop concentration on.

While in {@b Bloodlust} state you consider a creature marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|DRK} spell as {@b Prey}. You know the exact location of your {@b Prey} while it is within 300ft of you and when you hit it with a weapon attack, you can learn whether it is resistant, vulnerable or immune to a single damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Cascade
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice with your consecrated weapon, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn. Your consecrated weapons ignore resistance to the weapon's damage type on hit.

subclassFeature.name: Sacrosanct Carnage
entries: Starting at 17th level, you gain increasing bonuses based on the intensity of the battle. You gain the {@b Fervour Counter} which increases whenever you heal creatures, deal damage or receive damage by an amount equal to the total calculated for each instance. You can only gain 350 {@b Fervour} in a round. You gain all the bonuses whose {@b Fervour} count is less than or equal to your {@b Fervour Counter} at any given time. The {@b Fervour Counter} resets to zero at the end of your turn, except when you are in the {@b Bloodlust} state, in which case it resets to zero when your {@b Bloodlust} state ends.

entries.caption: Fervour Counter
rows: A 60 ft aura expands from you and remains centered on you. Whenever a creature within the aura deals or receives a critical hit, the total calculated is added to your {@b Fervour} counter.
You gain Truesight upto 30 ft from you. The {@b Prey} cannot benefit from being {@b Heavily Obscured} against allied creatures that are within the aura.

You gain immunity to {@condition Charmed} condition. Additionally you and allied creatures within the aura gain advantage on saving throws to avoid and end effects that include the {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Deafened}, {@condition Frightened}, or {@condition Poisoned} condition.
You regain the maximum number of Hit Points possible from any healing. When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die of your consecrated weapons, you can reroll the damage dice and must use the new roll.

When you kill a hostile creature or when a hostile creature dies within 10 ft of you, you can use your reaction to gain one of the hostile creature's damage resistances or immunities as a resistance until you complete a short or long rest. You can have atmost two resistances from this ability and you can replace a previously gained resistance with a new one. When the {@b Prey} dies, you receive this benefit as long as you are within 300ft of it and you do not need to use your reaction to gain the resistance.
Cleric spells of 5th level or lower that require an Action to be cast, can now be cast by you with a Bonus Action instead.

Any attack roll you make with your consecrated weapon is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}. When you deal a critical hit with your consecrated weapons, you momentarily inflict {@b Madness} on that creature, forcing it to immediately use its reaction to make one attack against another random creature within reach or itself if there are no other creatures within its reach.

subclassFeature.name: Oblivion Domain
entries: The Oblivion Domain consists of eerie clerics who are in service of beings forgotten by most. Though sparse in number, there will always be traces of these clerics throughout history. The beginnings and purpose of these clerics have remained as incomprehensible as the deities they serve. However, they are known to bring cosmic horror to their aid and twist the laws of divinity to create paradoxical phenomenon.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

subclassFeature.name: Void-Touched Revelation
entries: Your blood increases in viscosity and becomes a darker shade of red, granting you increased vitality and a chilling visage. Your hitpoint maximum increases by 1 for every level you gain in this class. You add your Wisdom modifier to any Intimidation check you make.
Once per turn, when you force a saving throw on a creature using a Cleric spell, you can heal another creature within 30ft of it by an amount equal to the spell level.

subclassFeature.name: Blessing of the Inscrutable Madness
entries: Starting at 2nd level, when you cast a Cleric spell that applies an effect over an area, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to increase one parameter by 5ft or 10ft and you take Psychic damage(pierces resistance and immunity) equal to 2*PB or 4*PB respectively, at the end of each of your turns for the duration of the spell. This damage cannot make you roll Concentration saving throws.
Additionally, the next Cleric spell that you cast to restore hitpoints gains a bonus to the healing done equal to your Cleric level for one creature.

subclassFeature.name: Mantle of the Waking Nightmare
entries: Starting at 6th level, you gain resistance to Psychic damage and your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. Once per turn when you take Psychic damage, you can give one creature within 60ft of you disadvantage on saving throws using one ability score until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Herald of the Crawling Chaos
entries: Starting at 17th level, you gain immunity to Psychic damage. You also gain immunity to the {@condition charmed} and {@condition frightened} conditions. You can target creatures that you have banished with disadvantage on one saving throw from your 6th level subclass feature as long as you are within 60ft of the space that they would reappear in when those effects end.

When a creature fails the saving throw against your Cleric spells, you can force it to roll an additional Intelligence saving throw, and on a failure you banish only its conciousness to a Demiplane at the edge of the Far Realms for one minute, leaving its body behind. You can only banish one creature in such a way at a time and that creature also has the {@condition incapacitated} condition for the duration of its banishment.

While the creature starts its turn with its conciousness in the Demiplane it can roll the Intelligence saving throw again and on a success it escapes the Demiplane, ending the banishment. On a failure it takes Psychic damage equal to twice your Wisdom modifier as it starts bleeding black ooze from all of its orifices because of the maddening voices and sinister noises assaulting its mind. If any creature other than you deals damage to the creature, you must make a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration as if you took the damage, and on a failure this banishment ends immediately.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of The Sanctified Knuckle
entries: Something awakened within you when you first slapped a person. Maybe it was a moment of false bravado, or an outburst of your repressed anger, or maybe it was something else entirely. Regardless, you felt a surge of power and strength in a body you once considered weak. Thus hit the profound realisation, a perpetual effort towards becoming a true GIGACHAD or GIGACHADESS. As you focus on your Workout regime and using your newfound strength for the betterment of others, you follow in the steps of the first SIGMA MALE or FEMALE, and create your own legacy that would inspire others for years to come.

entries.subclassFeature: Tenets of The Sanctified Knuckle|Paladin|DRK|Sanctified Knuckle|HEC|3

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

entries.name: Triune Incarnation
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to bring out your latent potential and indomitable physique. As a bonus action you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to gain a Perfect Physique of your choice for 10 minutes. You can also increase or decrease your size by one category for the same duration.

entries.caption: Triune Incarnation
rows: You use your Strength modifier for unarmed attacks and you cannot wield a shield. You gain advantage on Strength Checks and Strength Saves. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and hit a creature with unarmed strikes, you deal additional damage equal to your Strength modifier to the target and creatures within 10ft of it.

You use your Charisma modifier for unarmed attacks and you can wield a shield. You gain advantage on Constitution Checks and Constitution Saves. You gain a bonus to your grapple checks equal to your Constitution modifier and once per turn, you can attempt to {@condition grapple} a creature as part of an unarmed strike.

You use your Dexterity modifier for unarmed attacks and you cannot wield a shield. You gain advantage on Dexterity Checks and Dexterity Saves. Your unarmed damage die is one die type lower and when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to make unarmed strikes, you can make one extra unarmed strike as part of the action.

entries.name: Unyielding Spirit
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to bolster the vitality of your allies and free them from any shackles binding them. As an action you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to choose upto two creatures within 30ft of you and dispel one of {@condition restrained}, {@condition stunned}, {@condition paralyzed} or {@condition petrified} conditions from them. The creatures can then gain temporary hitpoints equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Adaptive Conduit
entries: Your body becomes a valid target for any effect that requires a weapon target and they benefit any unarmed attacks you make.

Any unarmed attacks you make can deal Radiant damage instead of their usual damage type. Your unarmed damage die becomes a {@dice 1d8} and your natural weapon damage die also becomes the same if it was lower. When you reach level 9 in this class, they both become a {@dice 1d10} instead.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of Sanctified Knuckle table. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of The Sanctified Knuckle
entries: These paladins share the following tenets:

entries.name: Never stop the Grind
entries: The hustle never ends. You must always keep working to become Stronger, Faster and Smarter. NO PAIN, NO GAIN BABY!

entries.name: Exemplary Strength
entries: Strength must be used to help others overcome their struggles and not oppress them for your own benefit. You lead by example and punish those that exploit others.

entries.name: Haters gonna Hate
entries: As a wise man once said, {@b 'The Lion Does Not Concern Himself With The Opinions Of The Sheep'}. Ignore those that seek to drag you down to their level of Depravity. If ignoring does not work, a tight Bitch-slap will.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Boundless Resolve
entries: Starting at 7th level, You emit an aura of celerity. Allies within the aura can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically end {@condition prone} and {@condition grappled} conditions. Additionally, an allied creature that enters the aura or starts its turn in the aura, can use a bonus action to {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} until the end of their turn.
At level 18, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Ascendant Strike
entries: Your body has now reached the pinnacle of your race's anatomy. Regardless of physical traits that would appear due to age, you always look attractive. You also suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically.
You gain proficiency in Persuasion or Intimidation. If you already have proficiency in either skill, you can gain expertise in it instead.
You gain additional benefits from your {@b Channel Divinity: Triune Incarnation}, as shown below:

entries.caption: Triune Incarnation Improvement
rows: Your unarmed damage dice is doubled in count. Additionally, when you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can push it upto 10ft in any direction.

You gain +2 to unarmed attack rolls, unarmed damage rolls and concentration saving throws. While you are concentrating on a spell, you gain a bonus to your unarmed damage equal to the level of the spell. All creatures have advantage on attack rolls against a creature {@condition grappled} by you.

When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to make unarmed strikes, you can now make two extra unarmed strikes as part of the action. Your movement speed increases by 15ft and on your turn, you can move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move while you are unarmored or wearing light armor. During your turn, if you make an unarmed strike against a creature, that creature can't make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Inexorable Riposte
entries: You have reached a major milestone in your journey and receive an enlightenment: {@b 'The Best Defense Is A Good Offense'}. As an action, you transform yourself into an Avatar of Peerless Form, granting you the following benefits for one minute:

items: Your reach for unarmed attacks increases by 10 feet.
When you roll a 1 or a 2 on your unarmed and smite damage dice, you can reroll the damage dice once and you must use the new result.

When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to immediately make one unarmed strike against that creature regardless of the distance between you two. On a hit you halve the damage you take, and on a critical hit you take no damage from the attack.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: College of Dirge
entries: Bards of the College of Dirge are trained to utilise a deadly combo of concealable weapons and potent toxins. These bards usually work in a similar fashion to an assassin or a contract killer. However, unlike those commonly found in these professions, these bards actively infiltrate social circles and work together as a team to take down their targets, often disguising their deadly intentions behind friendly gestures.

subclassFeature.name: Lifetaker's Arsenal
entries: At 3rd level, you can add your Charisma modifier to your initiative rolls. You also gain proficiency with {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB} and {@item Blowgun|XPHB}.

In addition, you learn the {@spell Encoat|TCT} cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of bard cantrips you know. When you cast the spell, the number of attacks you can make that gain the additional poison damage is equal to your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Sibilant Blade
entries: When you inspire an ally with your Bardic Inspiration feature, you can immediately make one weapon attack as part of the same action. You can only use a {@item Blowgun|XPHB} or a weapon with the Light property for this attack, and you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of your Strength or Dexterity.

subclassFeature.name: Tormentor's Emerald
entries: At 6th level, when you make a damage roll that deals Poison damage, it ignores Resistance to Poison damage. You can apply poison on your weapon/ammunition using a bonus action, instead of an action. When you apply poison on your weapon/ammunition, it stays potent for upto 10 minutes now.

subclassFeature.name: Incisive Agony
entries: When you make a damage roll that deals Poison damage, you treat Immunity to Poison damage as Resistance instead. You can use your Spell Save DC as the DC for any poison you use.

Once until the start of your next turn, when a creature takes Poison damage from you, you can inflict the {@condition Dazed|DRK} condition on it until the end of your next turn. Alternatively, you can force it to roll a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC and inflict the {@condition Incapacitated} condition on it until the end of your next turn, only on a failure.

subclassFeature.name: Seer of Fate
entries: You know Gambling? You think it's bad? You've probably heard of people ruining their life by Gambling all their wealth away, or by taking on too much debt in hopes that they'll hit it rich and pay it all back. You know the trith is, you only really lose in Gambling when you quit.

Wizards of this tradition firmly believe that there is a 'Method to Madness', and they aim to influence the invisible threads of fate to play in their favour. However, Fate acts in mysterious ways and it might chose to punish you when you attempt to bend it to your will.

subclassFeature.name: The House Edge
entries: You add your Intelligence modifier to any Insight and Sleight of Hand checks you make.

You gain proficiency with {@item Dice Set|XPHB} and you can use it as an arcane focus for your wizard spells. While using it, you can conceal the verbal and somatic components of a wizard spell as normal chitchat and dice rolling.

subclassFeature.name: Playing the Odds
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can make the following bets:

{@b Risky Bet 6} - Once per turn, when you are about to make a {@dice d20} Roll, you can roll a {@dice 1d6} before that. On a 1, the {@dice d20} Roll is made with disadvantage, and on a 6 the {@dice d20} Roll is made with advantage.

{@b Safe Bet 6} - When you or an ally within 60ft has just made a {@dice d20} Roll, you can use your Reaction to add a {@dice 1d4} to the {@dice d20} Roll. You must use this feature before the DM declares any effects of the roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: High Roller
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can make the following bets:

{@b Risky Bet 12} - Once per turn, when you are about to cast a wizard spell with a spell slot, you can roll a {@dice 1d12} before that. On a 1 or 2, your casting of the spell fizzles and you lose the action used to cast the spell but not the spell slot. On a 11 or 12, you cast the spell as if the spell slot expended was of one higher level.

{@b Safe Bet 12} - When you make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can add your Intelligence modifier to that roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: To Tempt Fate Twice
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can make the following bets:

{@b Risky Bet 20} - Once per turn, when you are about to roll damage for a wizard spell you have cast, you can roll a {@dice 1d20} before that. On a 1, 2 or 3, roll the damage for the spell and for every die that rolled the maximum, reduce the total damage of the spell by another roll of the same die. On a 18, 19, or 20, roll the damage for the spell and for every die that rolled the maximum, increase the total damage of the spell by another roll of the same die. The maximum number of dice you can add to the total damage is equal to your Intelligence modifier.

{@b Safe Bet 20} - When you roll damage dice for a wizard spell you cast, you can add extra damage equal to 2 + the spell slot level used in the casting of the spell. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Eyes on the Jackpot
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can make the following bets:

{@b Risky Bet 100} - When you succeed on any of the other {@b Risky Bets}, you can roll a 1d100. On a roll of 1 to Class level, the {@b Risky Bet} you succeeded on is turned into a failure instead. On a roll of (100 - Class level + 1) to 100, the {@b Risky Bet} you succeeded on is further empowered as shown below:

items: {@b Risky Bet 6} - You also add your Intelligence modifier to the {@dice d20} Roll.
{@b Risky Bet 12} - You cast the spell as if the spell slot expended was of two higher levels.
{@b Risky Bet 20} - The damage dice explode on rolling either of the two highest values that can be rolled with the die, and the maximum limit for the number of explosions is doubled.

entries: {@b Safe Bet 100} - When you make a {@b Risky Bet} and fail, you can use your Reaction to nullify the drawback. However, you cannot make anymore {@b Risky Bets} until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodmagic
entries: Your magical spark comes from the touch of Ichor, the essence of Divinity, or from an intimate blessing bestowed by the Arcane Weave. While many can only dream of such fortune, you are aware that such a gift comes with strings attached. Your blood exhibits strange properties like a different color, thicker viscosity, iridescence, etc. While your arcane abilities and control over vital energy is strengthened significantly, it often comes at the cost of your own vitality. Besides your intimate connection to Divinity or the Arcane Weave, often makes you a perfect test subject or an invaluable sacrifice. As such, being targeted by evil cultists and obsessed researchers is a common occurence for those who tread this path.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodmagic Spells
entries: {@i 1st-level Bloodmagic feature}

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Bloodmagic Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must deal Necrotic damage and be from the {@filter Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock or Wizard spell list|spells|damage type=necrotic|level=1;2;3;4;5|class=Cleric;Sorcerer;Warlock;Wizard}.

subclassFeature.name: Ichor's Providence
entries: {@i 1st-level Bloodmagic feature}

You gain two {@dice 1d4} Hit dice instead of one {@dice 1d6} Hit die for every level you take in this subclass, and the additional Hipoints you gain for each level is calculated by rolling {@dice 2d4} and adding your Constitution modifier to it. You do not add your Constitution modifier to the Hitpoints you regain from expending a Hitdie like you normally would. However, when you expend your Hitdice to regain Hitpoints, you take the maximum result for each Hitdie instead of rolling like usual.
While you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Constitution modifier + your Charisma modifier.

When you cast a Sorcerer spell, you mark one creature targeted by it as a {@b Blood Offering} for one minute. At the start of your turn, you can activate the {@b Blood Offering} mark to deal {@dice 1d6} Necrotic damage to the creature and heal yourself for the same amount. You can only have one creature marked as a {@b Blood Offering} at a time and when you attempt to mark a second creature, the first creature loses it's {@b Blood Offering} mark.

In addition, you learn the {@spell Clotshot|TCT} and {@spell Transfusion|TCT} cantrips, and they don't count against the number of sorcerer cantrips you know. The {@spell Transfusion|TCT} spell has a casting time of an Action for you and you can target any creature that possesses blood with it(not limited to humanoid). The {@spell Clotshot|TCT} spell creates two darts when you cast it, and the darts automatically strike the creatures you target within range without rolling an attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Scarlet Apostle
entries: {@i 6th-level Bloodmagic feature}
You gain resistance to Necrotic damage and you become immune to diseases.

Whenever you use Metamagic on a spell, you can expend any number of Hitdice and reduce the sorcery points spent by 1 for each Hitdie you expend. When you do so, you take {@dice 1d4} Necrotic damage (cannot be reduced by any means) for each Hitdie you expend and you must resolve the effects of taking this damage before you resolve the effects of the spell.

When you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, you can sacrifice your Hitpoints to deal extra damage to one creature affected by the spell. Roll any number of {@dice 1d10}s upto a maximum equal to the spell's level and you take the resulting total as Necrotic damage (cannot be reduced by any means). You then add (5 * the number of {@dice 1d10}s you rolled) Necrotic damage to one target of the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Tempered Bloodlust
entries: {@i 14th-level Bloodmagic feature}
Your {@b Blood Offering} die is now a {@dice 1d10}. As a Bonus action, you can enter the {@b Bloodrage} state for one minute and gain the following benefits:

items: When you enter this state, your Current and Maximum Hitpoints is increased by the amount of Temporary Hitpoints you have. You lose the Current and Maximum Hipoint bonus when you exit the {@b Bloodrage} state. You then lose all your Temporary Hitpoints and you cannot gain any Temporary Hitpoints while in the {@b Bloodrage} state.
The limit for the number of creatures you can mark as {@b Blood Offering} is now equal to your Charisma modifier.
You gain resistance to Piercing, Bludgeoning and Slashing damage.

When you enter this state you choose one of Piercing, Bludgeoning or Slashing damage. During this state, when you cast a Sorcerer spell or use your class and subclass features, you can convert any Necrotic damage component into the type of physical damage you chose previously.

entries: You exit the {@b Bloodrage} state earlier if you fall {@condition unconscious}. Once you use this bonus action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Sanguine Equilibrium
entries: {@i 18th-level Bloodmagic feature}
You gain immunity to Necrotic damage. While you are Bloodied, the effects of the {@b Blood Offering} mark are doubled, and you have advantage on Constitution checks and Constitution saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Juggernaut
entries: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Juggernaut stand so resolutely that none can deter them, and they swing their weapons with such force that all who stand against them are flung aside. In might and in spirit, juggernauts are immovable object and unstoppable force all at once.

Juggernaut barbarians can be found all over Tal'Dorei, and are common among the goliath warriors of the Rivermaw Herd that wanders the Dividing Plains. Some dwarves and humanoid survivalists of the Cliffkeep Mountains adopt this fighting style as an extension of their rugged determinism. And a number of stalwart juggernauts hail from the jungles of the Rifenmist Peninsula, having cast off the oppressive yoke of the Tz'Arrm, Helm of the Emperor.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit of the Mountain
entries: At 3rd level, you harness your fury to anchor your feet to the ground, becoming a bulwark of strength. While you are raging, you can't be knocked {@condition prone} or moved along the ground against your will.

subclassFeature.name: Thunderous Blows
entries: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, your rage instills you with the strength to shove and smash your way through your foes, making any battlefield your domain. When you hit a creature with a melee attack while you're raging, you can push that creature up to 5 feet away from you in a direction of your choice. A creature that is Huge or larger makes a Strength saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier. On a success, the creature is not pushed.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Forced Movement
entries: Usually when one creature moves out of a hostile creature's reach, the hostile creature can use its reaction to make an {@action opportunity attack}. However, forced movement—such as being pushed by a Path of the Juggernaut barbarian's {@subclassFeature Thunderous Blows|Barbarian|DRK|Juggernaut|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3} feature—doesn't provoke {@action opportunity attack||opportunity attacks}.

Likewise, a juggernaut barbarian's {@subclassFeature Hurricane Strike|Barbarian|DRK|Juggernaut|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|10} feature allows an ally to make a melee weapon attack as a reaction only if the foe ends its forced movement within 5 feet of the ally. If a foe is pushed through other spaces within 5 feet of your allies, those allies can't make normal {@action opportunity attack||opportunity attacks} against the foe.

subclassFeature.name: Demolishing Might
entries: Starting at 6th level, your melee weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage, and deal double damage to objects and structures.

subclassFeature.name: Resolute Stance
entries: Also at 6th level, you can temporarily refocus your combat ability to make yourself a bulwark of defense. At the start of your turn (no action required), you can assume a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn. While in this stance, you can't be {@condition grappled}, attack rolls against you have disadvantage, and your weapon attacks are made with disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Hurricane Strike
entries: Starting at 10th level, your blows can hurl foes through the air and into the attacks of your allies. Once until the start of your next turn, when you push a creature at least 5 feet, you can then leap into an unoccupied space next to the creature. If you do so, the creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier or be knocked {@condition prone}. This leap costs no movement and does not provoke {@action opportunity attack||opportunity attacks}.
Additionally, whenever you push a creature into a space within 5 feet of one of your allies, the ally can use its reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Thunderous Blows (10th Level)
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can push a creature up to 10 feet when you hit it with a melee attack while you're raging.

subclassFeature.name: Unstoppable
entries: At 14th level, your fury in battle makes you unstoppable. While you're raging, your speed cannot be reduced, and you are immune to the {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition prone}, and {@condition stunned} conditions.

If you are {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, or {@condition stunned}, you can still use a bonus action to enter a rage (even if you can't otherwise take actions). You also dispel these conditions on yourself when you start raging.

subclassFeature.name: College of Tragedy
entries: Not all grand stories conclude in triumphant victory. Many tales end with death and despair, and bards of the College of Tragedy know that sorrow and pathos are emotions just as potent as joy and delight. These bards specialize in the power of tragic storytelling, weaving words and spells together to dramatic and devastating effect.

subclassFeature.name: Poetry in Misery
entries: When you join the College of Tragedy at 3rd level, you learn to harness the beauty in failure, finding inspiration in even the direst twists of fate. Whenever you or an ally within 30 feet of you rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to soliloquize and regain one expended use of your Bardic Inspiration feature.

subclassFeature.name: Sorrowful Fate
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you exploit a foe's peril to instill deep feelings of sorrow and doom. When you or an ally you can see forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to change the type of saving throw to a Charisma save instead.

If the target fails this save, roll a Bardic Inspiration die. The target takes psychic damage equal to the result, and is plagued with regret for 1 minute. If the target is reduced to 0 hit points during this time and can speak, they are magically compelled to utter darkly poetic final words before succumbing to their injuries.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest, or until you are reduced to 0 hit points.

subclassFeature.name: Impending Misfortune
entries: Also at 6th level, your words can twist the power of fate to create triumph from the promise of future despair. When you make an attack roll or a saving throw, you can gain a +10 bonus to the roll, but the next attack roll or saving throw you make takes a −10 penalty. If not used, this penalty disappears when you finish a short or long rest.
You can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest, or until you are reduced to 0 hit points.

subclassFeature.name: Tale of Hubris
entries: At 6th level, you learn to weave a magical narrative that draws out the fatal arrogance of your foes. When a creature scores a critical hit against you or an ally within 60 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction and expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to target the attacking creature and evoke the story of their downfall. For 1 minute or until the target suffers a critical hit, any weapon attack against the target scores a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

subclassFeature.name: Nimbus of Pathos
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, you can touch a willing creature as an action and empower it with tragic heroism. For 1 minute, the creature is surrounded by mournful music and ghostly singing, granting it the following benefits and drawbacks:

items: The creature has a +4 bonus to AC.
It has advantage on attack rolls and saving throws.
When the creature hits a target with a weapon attack or spell attack, that target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} radiant damage.
Any weapon attack against the creature scores a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

entries: When this effect ends, the creature immediately drops to 0 hit points and is dying. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Tale of Hubris (14th Level)
entries: At 14th level, the critical hit range of this feature increases to 17–20.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Domain
entries: Developed in Wildemount by the Claret Orders, the Blood Domain centers around the understanding of the natural life force as it exists within the body, and the divine conduit it can become. Those who take up this domain understand that the power of blood is the power of sacrifice, the balance of life and death, and the spirit's anchor within the mortal shell.

Gods who grant the power of the Blood Domain, including The Ruiner and The Matron of Ravens, direct their followers to tap into the connection between body and soul, exploit the hidden reserves of will within one's own vitality, and corrupt the bodies of others through the secret rites of hemocraft. Clerics of good gods use hemocraft to fill their self-sacrifice with purpose and power, while clerics with fewer morals use the blood of others to achieve their own malevolent ends.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodletting Focus
entries: Starting at 1st level, your divine magic draws the blood from magically inflicted wounds, worsening the agony of your foes. When you cast a damage-dealing spell of 1st level or higher whose duration is instantaneous, a creature that takes damage from the spell takes extra necrotic damage equal to 2 + the spell's level.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Blood Domain Spells table.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Crimson Bond
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to form a supernatural bond with a creature you can see, or with a creature for which you possess a blood sample. This bond lasts for 1 hour or until your {@status concentration} is broken (as if concentrating on a spell).

While the bond is in effect, you can use an action to learn the target's approximate distance and direction from you, as well as its current hit points and any conditions affecting it, as long as the target is within 10 miles of you. Alternatively, you can use your action to attempt to connect with the target's senses. You take {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage and the target makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a successful save, the bond ends. On a failure, you can choose to either see or hear through the target's senses for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1 minute). During this time, you are {@condition blinded} or {@condition deafened} (respectively) with regard to your own senses. When the connection ends, the bond is lost.
Regardless of the outcome, the target feels a wave of unease pass over it when it makes this save.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Blood Puppet
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to briefly control a creature's actions—whether that creature is living or dead. As an action, you target a Large or smaller creature or corpse within 60 feet of you that has blood. A creature you target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition charmed} by you. An {@condition unconscious} creature automatically fails its saving throw, and isn't {@condition incapacitated} while you control its actions. A corpse targeted by this effect gains a semblance of life that you control.
On the affected creature or animated corpse's turn, you can command it (no action required) to move up to its speed and use its action to do one of the following:

items: Interact with an object
Make a single {@action attack}
Do nothing

entries: An animated corpse or an {@condition unconscious} creature takes its turn immediately after yours, but can't move or take actions unless you command it to do so. Its statistics are the same as when it was alive or conscious.

An affected living creature makes a new saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. For any target, your control lasts for 1 minute or until you are {@condition incapacitated}, or you use this ability again on another target.

subclassFeature.name: Sanguine Recall
entries: At 6th level, you can sacrifice a portion of your own vitality to recover expended spell slots as an action. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to or less than half your cleric level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You take {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage for each spell slot level recovered, which can't be reduced in any way. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

For example, if you're an 8th-level cleric, you can recover up to four levels of spell slots—a single 4th-level slot, two 2nd-level slots, a 3rd-level slot and a 1st-level slot, or four 1st-level slots. You then take {@damage 4d6} necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Blood Puppet (17th Level)
entries: At 17th level, you can use this feature to target a Huge or smaller creature or corpse.

subclassFeature.name: Vascular Corruption Aura
entries: At 17th level, you can use your action to emit a deathly aura of necrotic energy that causes the veins of nearby foes to burst and bleed. For 1 minute, any hostile creature that moves within 30 feet of you for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes {@damage 5d6} necrotic damage. Hostile creatures can't regain hit points while within the aura.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Moon Domain
entries: Since the The Founding, all mortal creatures have looked to the skies and sensed the power and mystery carried by Catha and Ruidus, the two moons of Exandria. The Moonweaver herself is said to guide her worshipers from within the pale glow of Catha, revealing hidden paths and granting inspired dreams to those who pray to that moon. Distant, dark Ruidus is often regarded with awe and apprehension, considered a portent for fell deeds and bad luck.

Clerics of the Moon Domain draw on their divine connection to the moons to wield light and shadow, invoke good fortune and ill favor, and reveal or conceal as they see fit. Most Moon clerics worship the Moonweaver herself, but her followers are as varied as the stars in the sky. Some seek to protect the vulnerable and do good in the world, while others meddle with impunity and distort the truth for selfish gain. Other Moon clerics worship not the gods but the moons themselves, especially those with an innate connection to the lunar cycles through lycanthropy.

subclassFeature.name: Clarity of Catha
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you learn to shine light upon the mind's most dire moments, shielding those you protect. When a creature within 60 feet of you that you can see makes a Wisdom saving throw, you can use your reaction to grant that creature advantage on the save.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Moon Domain Spells table.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Blessing of the Full Moon
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to infuse your allies with bestial power. As an action, you instill a willing creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that you can see with one of the following blessings of your choice:

items.name: Blessing of the Watchful Moon
entries: For 1 hour, the blessed creature's speed increases by 10 feet, and it has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception} or {@skill Survival}) checks involving smell or made to track a creature.

items.name: Blessing of the Blood-Drenched Moon
entries: For 10 minutes, the blessed creature has advantage on attack rolls against a target if at least one of the blessed creature's allies is within 10 feet of the target and the ally isn't {@condition incapacitated}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Mind of Two Moons
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to invoke the twofold arcana of Exandria's moons. By expending one use of Channel Divinity, you can cast a second {@status concentration} spell while already concentrating on a first spell, as long as both spells are on your list of Moon Domain spells. If you need to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain your {@status concentration} on both spells, you make the save with disadvantage. On a failure, you lose {@status concentration} on both spells.

subclassFeature.name: Eclipse of Ill Omen
entries: At 17th level, you can call upon the vermillion moon Ruidus to flare in the sky above you, eclipsing all other light. Its power surrounds you even where the sky can't be seen, and even on other planes. As a bonus action, you can manifest an area of reddish, dim light in a 60-foot radius around you. In addition to the normal effects of dim light, creatures in the area make saving throws with disadvantage. When you create this eclipse, you can choose any number of creatures that are unaffected by it.

This eclipse lasts while you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell) for up to 1 minute. Concentrating on this feature counts as concentrating on a Moon Domain spell for the purpose of your {@subclassFeature Channel Divinity: Mind of Two Moons|Cleric|DRK|Moon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|6|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Mind of Two Moons} feature.

Additionally, once per turn when you deal radiant damage to any creatures in this area of dim light, you can curse one of those creatures until the eclipse ends (no action required). A creature cursed in this way has its speed halved and can't regain hit points while it is within the area of dim light.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Blighted
entries: Those who channel the magic of life and nature often find themselves drawn to a particular shrine or natural site, binding their body and spirit to these places of power. Such druids draw vitality from their chosen location, protecting it with their lives—but not all succeed in defending these sacred realms.

Whether through the subtle corruption of vile magics, the tainted presence of an ancient terror, or a terrible mistake unleashed by druids themselves, a land can become cursed with magic that warps any druid bound to that land. Twisted by their connection to an unhallowed territory, these guardians come to embody the defiled nature they serve, exalting the natural process of decay and using it to further their goals—or sometimes to seek a means to end the curse that plagues them.

subclassFeature.name: Blighted Shape
entries: Also at 2nd level, your physical form begins to show effects of the corruption you wield, tracing blackened veins across your skin, producing gnarled, bony protrusions, or other eerie phenomena. You gain proficiency in the Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) skill.

Additionally, while you are transformed by your Wild Shape feature, you gain a +2 bonus to AC as gnarled spines protrude from your body. Your beast form also gains {@sense darkvision} with a radius of 60 feet, or an additional 60 feet of {@sense darkvision} if it already has that sense.

subclassFeature.name: Defile Ground
entries: Starting at 2nd level when you choose this circle, you can use a bonus action to corrupt a patch of land or an area of water in a 10-foot radius circle centered on a point within 60 feet of you. This corruption lasts for 1 minute. The corrupted area is difficult terrain for creatures that are hostile to you. Additionally, when a creature in the area takes damage from an attack or spell for the first time on a turn, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage. You can move this patch of corruption up to 30 feet as a bonus action. Flying creatures are unaffected by the corruption.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Call of the Shadowseeds
entries: At 6th level, you learn to summon the feral children of the forest from the life force of your enemies. When a creature that is not undead or a construct takes damage within the area of your {@subclassFeature Defile Ground|Druid|DRK|Blighted|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2} feature, you can use your reaction to summon a {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the creature. You can direct the {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling} to make an attack against any creature within 5 feet of it as a part of this reaction. The {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling} then acts on your initiative, obeying your verbal commands.

The {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} remains in your service until it's reduced to 0 hit points, until the end of your next long rest, or until you summon another {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling}, at which point it crumbles into foul-smelling mulch. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
The {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling} uses the statistics below. Its features scale based on your level and proficiency bonus (PB).

subclassFeature.name: Defile Ground (10th Level)
entries: Starting at 10th level, the area of your defiled ground increases to a 20-foot radius circle. You can now move this patch of corruption up to 60 feet as a bonus action. Additionally, the extra damage dealt by your defiled ground increases to {@damage 1d8} when you reach 10th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: Foul Conjuration
entries: Starting at 10th level, the creatures you conjure are malformed and bloated with toxins. Any beast, fey, or plant (including your {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}) summoned or created by your spells or class features gains the following traits:

entries.name: Blighted Resilience
entries: The creature has immunity to necrotic and poison damage and to the {@condition poisoned} condition.

entries.name: Toxic Demise
entries: When the creature is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes in a burst of toxic mulch or fetid viscera. Each creature within 5 feet of the exploding creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take necrotic damage based on the creature's challenge rating (see the table below). As an action, you can also cause a summoned creature to explode, immediately killing it.

entries.caption: Toxic Demise Damage
rows: {@damage (#$prompt_number:min=1,title=Enter the creature's CR!,default=1$#)d10|A number of d10s of necrotic damage equal to the creature's challenge rating}
{@damage (#$prompt_number:min=1,title=Enter your Proficiency Bonus!,default=1$#)d8|A number of d8s of necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus}

subclassFeature.name: Defile Ground (14th Level)
entries: Starting at 14th level, the area of your defiled ground becomes a 20-foot radius sphere and it can now affect flying creatures within the area. The extra damage dealt by your defiled ground increases to {@damage 1d10} when you reach 14th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: Incarnation of Corruption
entries: At 14th level, your physical form begins to take on the tainted traits of the land you are bonded to. Your skin grows ashen, and your eyes darken or turn completely white. Spines and jagged spurs emerge from your body, granting you resistance to necrotic damage and a +2 bonus to AC.

Additionally, whenever you start your turn within the radius of the corruption created by your {@subclassFeature Defile Ground|Druid|DRK|Blighted|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2} feature, you can use a bonus action to gain temporary hit points equal to your druid level.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Cobalt Soul
entries: Driven by the pursuit of knowledge and its scholars' worship of The Knowing Mentor, the Library of the Cobalt Soul is one of the best-respected and most heavily guarded repositories of tomes, history, and information in all Exandria. People from all lands come to the library to seek knowledge, and those particularly dedicated to the virtues of truth often pledge their minds and bodies to the Cobalt Soul's cause. To become a member of the Library of the Cobalt Soul is to give oneself over to a quest dedicated to unveiling life's mysteries, bringing light to the secrets of concealed evil, and guarding the most powerful and dangerous of truths from those whose unwholesome thirst for knowledge might bring death and suffering to others.

The monks of the Library of the Cobalt Soul are the embodiment of the maxim: "Know your enemy." Through tireless research, they steel themselves against the unrelenting tides of evil. Through rigorous training, they learn to break through their foes' mental and physical defenses. Then, once the fight is done, they record their findings for future generations of monks to study.

subclassFeature.name: Extract Aspects
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can strike pressure points to intuit crucial information about a foe. When you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can analyze it. Whenever an analyzed creature misses you with an attack, you can immediately use your reaction to make an unarmed strike against that creature if it's within your reach. This benefit lasts until you finish a short or long rest.
Additionally, when you analyze a creature, you learn all of its damage vulnerabilities, damage resistances, damage immunities, and condition immunities.

subclassFeature.name: Extort Truth
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can precisely strike a hidden cluster of nerves on a creature, temporarily preventing it from masking its true thoughts and intent. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 ki point to force it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is unable to speak a deliberate lie, and all Charisma checks directed at the creature are made with advantage for up to 10 minutes. You know if it succeeded or failed on its saving throw.

An affected creature is aware of the effect and can thus avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive in its answers as long as the effect lasts.
If you wish to impose this effect on a creature without injuring it, you can attack the creature to simply touch it, dealing no damage on a hit.

subclassFeature.name: Mystical Erudition
entries: Also by 6th level, you have extensively studied the history and lore within the archives of the Library of the Cobalt Soul. You learn one language of your choice, and you gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}. If you already have proficiency in one of the listed skills, you can instead choose to double your proficiency bonus for any ability check you make that uses the chosen proficiency.

subclassFeature.name: Mind of Mercury
entries: Starting at 11th level, you've honed your awareness and reflexes through mental aptitude and pattern recognition. Once per turn, if you've already taken your reaction, you may spend 1 ki point to take an additional reaction. You can use only one reaction per triggering effect.

subclassFeature.name: Mystical Erudition (11th Level)
entries: You gain an additional language and an additional skill proficiency from the list: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}—(or you can double the bonus of an existing proficiency from the list) at 11th level.

subclassFeature.name: Debilitating Barrage
entries: Upon reaching 17th level, you've gained the knowledge to manipulate a creature's ki to undermine their fortitude. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to cause the creature to gain vulnerability to one damage type of your choice for 1 minute, or until the end of a turn in which it has taken damage of that type.

If a creature has resistance to the damage type you choose, this resistance is suppressed for 1 minute, rather than gaining vulnerability. A creature that is immune to the damage type you choose is unaffected. A creature who is affected by this feature cannot be affected by it again for 24 hours, unless you use double the amount of ki points than the last time.

subclassFeature.name: Mystical Erudition (17th Level)
entries: You gain an additional language and an additional skill proficiency from the list: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}—(or you can double the bonus of an existing proficiency from the list) at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Open Sea
entries: The Oath of the Open Sea calls to seafaring warriors, swashbuckling sailors, and traveling guardians who seek the thrill of a limitless horizon. Driven to search for adventure and mystery across and beneath every endless oceanic expanse, paladins who swear this oath stand against those who would deny liberty to like-minded travelers, rooting out tyranny and corruption wherever it is found.

Such guardians believe in the natural beauty of the sea, often making offerings and prayers to entities or deities such as The Wildmother or The Stormlord who influence safe passage. At the same time, they answer the call to hunt the monstrous creatures that too often bloody the waters with wanton violence and ill intent, and which terrorize the folk of the sea and shore.

entries.subclassFeature: Tenets of the Open Sea|Paladin|DRK|Open Sea|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Visibility
entries: Fog and other effects can obscure vision for you, your enemies, and your allies. When you heavily obscure an area using your Marine Layer Channel Divinity option, all creatures within the area have their vision completely blocked, and creatures outside the area can't see in. Creatures that can't see automatically fail ability checks that require sight. Also, attack rolls against creatures that can't see have advantage, and their own attack rolls have disadvantage.

Creatures in a lightly obscured area have disadvantage only on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight. The rules for when your vision is obscured are described completely in the fifth edition core rules.

subclassFeature.name: Fury of the Tides
entries: As a bonus action, you channel the powerful might of the waves to bolster your attacks for 1 minute. Once per turn for the duration, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can choose to push the target 10 feet away from you. If pushed into an obstacle or another creature, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Marine Layer
entries: As an action, you channel the sea to create a thick cloud of fog that surrounds you for 20 feet in all directions.
