The fog moves with you, remaining centered on you and making its area heavily obscured. You and each creature within 5 feet of you instead treat the area as lightly obscured. This fog lasts for 10 minutes, spreads around corners, and cannot be dispersed unless you choose to end this effect (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of the Open Sea Spells table. Spells marked with an asterisk are new spells described on the {@filter spells page|spells|source=TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}.

entries.caption: Oath of the Open Sea Spells
rows: {@spell create or destroy water}, {@spell expeditious retreat}
{@spell call lightning}, {@spell freedom of the waves|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}*
{@spell commune with nature}, {@spell freedom of the winds|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}*

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of the Open Sea
entries: Freedom can be a selfless virtue or a selfish want. For paladins who swear the Oath of the Open Sea, freedom is the highest calling, and a gift to be granted to all.

entries.name: No Greater Life than a Life Lived Free
entries: One should be free to chart their own path without oppression. Those who would exert their power to dominate others shall be smote.

entries.name: Trust the Skies
entries: The guidance of a strong breeze. The rumbling warnings of a coming storm. Nature is a source of portent and council that should be heeded.

entries.name: Adapt Like the Water
entries: The waters of the ocean can shift around any obstacle—or become the most impassable obstacle of all. They carve away the land to reveal the secrets of the past, or swallow the truth and hide it forever. To embrace this fluidity is to be ready for any challenge.

entries.name: Explore the Uncharted
entries: The world is filled with mystery. Through the pursuit of enigmatic ends, one can uncover those who hide their foul deeds, and find the path to becoming something great.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Liberation
entries: Starting at 7th level, you fill nearby creatures with the energy of movement. While you're not {@condition incapacitated}, you and creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you cannot be {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained}, and ignore penalties on movement and attacks while underwater. Creatures that are already {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained} when they enter the aura can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically escape unless they are bound by magic restraints.

subclassFeature.name: Stormy Waters
entries: At 15th level, you can call on the force of crashing waters as a reaction whenever a creature moves into or out of your reach. You can make an Opportunity Attack against the creature as a Reaction, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked {@condition prone}.

subclassFeature.name: Mythic Swashbuckler
entries: At 20th level, you learn to channel the spirits of historic sea captains to briefly become a paragon of heroic adventure. As an action, you embrace these spirits of the sea to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks and you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. If you already have a climbing speed, it is doubled.
If you are within 5 feet of a creature and no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature.
You can take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action.
You have advantage on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saving throws against effects you can see.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Runechild
entries: The mysterious weave and flow of magic is feared by many folk across Exandria. But while some spellcasters must study the essence and nature of magic in the hope of learning to harness it, sorcerers possess an innate talent to sculpt and wield the errant strands of power that shape the world. For some sorcerers, the body becomes a conduit for this power, which is collected and stored in the form of natural runes—and which sees a sorcerer named as a Runechild.

The talents of a Runechild are rare, and sorcerers with this origin are sought after for study by mages and scholars alike, driven by a prevalent belief that the secrets of their runes can help understand the mysteries of magic. Others sometimes seek to enslave Runechild sorcerers, using their bodies as tortured spell batteries for diabolic pursuits. Runechild sorcerers were subjugated throughout the Age of Arcanum, and many of their contemporaries now search for ways to hide their essence—a task that isn't easy given the revealing nature of their gifts.

subclassFeature.name: Essence Runes
entries: At 1st level, your body begins to express your innate magic as runes traced out across your skin. You start with 1 essence rune, and gain an additional rune whenever you gain a level in this class. These runes can manifest anywhere on your body, though the first usually manifests on the forehead. Your essence runes remain invisible when inert.

At the end of a turn during which you spent one or more sorcery points, a number of your essence runes equal to the number of sorcery points you spent begin to glow with stored energy, becoming charged runes. You use these charged runes to power your Runechild subclass features. Also, as a bonus action, you may spend a sorcery point to convert two essence runes into two charged runes.
If you have no sorcery points and no charged runes, you can convert a single essence rune into a charged rune as an action.
If you have 5 or more charged runes, you emit bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet.
If you expend a charged rune to use one of your Runechild features, it returns to being an inert essence rune. Any charged runes also revert to inert essence runes after you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Glyph of Aegis
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can release the stored arcane power within your runes to absorb or deflect threatening attacks. Whenever you take damage, you can expend any number of charged runes as a reaction. Roll a number of {@dice d8|d8s} equal to the number of runes you expended, and reduce the damage by the total.

subclassFeature.name: Runic Magic
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Runic Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

When you gain a level in this class, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be {@filter an abjuration or transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list|spells|school=A;T|class=Sorcerer;Warlock;Wizard}.

entries.caption: Runic Spells
rows: {@spell longstrider}, {@spell protection from evil and good}

subclassFeature.name: Glyph of Aegis (6th Level)
entries: When you reach 6th level, you can touch a creature as an action and expend up to 3 charged runes to transfer your protective power to it for up to 1 hour. The next time that creature takes damage within the next hour, it rolls {@dice 1d8} per charged rune spent and reduces the damage by the total. You can't transfer this power to a creature already under the effect of Glyph of Aegis.

subclassFeature.name: Manifest Inscriptions
entries: Also at 6th level, you can reveal hidden glyphs and enchantments that surround you. As an action, you expend one charged rune to reveal hidden or invisible arcane traps, marks, runes, wards, sensors, or glyphs within 60 feet of you. They glow with dim light in a 5-foot radius for 1 minute.

You have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks to discern the nature of any magic revealed in this way for the duration. If the glyphs you reveal mean something in a language you can't read, you can understand them while they are glowing as if you knew that language.

subclassFeature.name: Sigilic Augmentation
entries: At 6th level, you can channel your runes to temporarily bolster your physical capabilities. When you make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution ability check, you can expend a charged rune as a reaction to gain advantage on the roll.

In addition, when you are forced to make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, you can use your reaction and expend a charged rune to gain advantage on the saving throw. Once you use this feature in this way, you can't use it in this way again until you complete a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Glyph of Aegis (14th Level)
entries: Your Glyph of Aegis die becomes a {@dice d10} at 14th level.

subclassFeature.name: Runic Torrent
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, you can channel runic energy to overpower even the staunchest defenses. When you cast a spell, you can expend 2 charged runes to cause the spell to deal force damage instead of its usual damage types. Additionally, all creatures targeted by the spell or within the spell's area must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone or pushed up to 15 feet away from the spell's point of origin (your choice).
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you complete a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Exemplar
entries: Starting at 18th level, you can use a bonus action and expend a charged rune to become a being of pure magical energy. While in your exemplar form, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have a flying speed of 60 feet.
Creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against your sorcerer spells.
You have resistance to damage dealt by spells.
Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you regain hit points equal to the spell's level.

entries: Your exemplar form lasts until the end of your turn. However, you can expend a charged rune at the end of your turn (no action required) to extend the duration until the end of your next turn. When your exemplar form ends, you are {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a long rest, unless you spend 7 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Magic
entries: Considered taboo by many societies and magic practitioners, the use of blood magic—also known as hemocraft—is a rare art that harnesses the latent powers of a creature's vitality to fuel and amplify the caster's own capabilities, while manipulating and weakening the bodies of enemies from the inside. Some of the more macabre mages seeking to empower their arcane pursuits turn to hemocraft as a means of bolstering their spells, giving their own life's blood to reach new heights of frightening magical prowess.

The secrets of hemocraft and other forms of blood magic were once the sole purview of the mysterious Claret Orders. In recent years, however, these secrets have begun to spread beyond the order's members and into the hands of less scrupulous mages. Blood magic has a bad reputation in Tal'Dorei, even though its powers can be used for much more than evil.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Channeling
entries: When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an {@item arcane focus}.

In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking {@damage 1d10} necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum {@damage 1d10}). This damage can't be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

subclassFeature.name: Sanguine Burst
entries: Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you've cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell's level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can't be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Bond of Mutual Suffering
entries: At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took.
You can use this feature once. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Glyph of Hemorrhaging
entries: Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Bond of Mutual Suffering (14th Level)
entries: At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

subclassFeature.name: Thicker than Water
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

action.name: Aural Symbiosis (1/Day)
entries: One humanoid that the ostinato can see within 5 feet of it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Charisma saving throw or the ostinato merges with it, becoming an enjoyable, repetitive tune in its host's mind. The ostinato can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect. The target retains control of its body and is aware of the ostinato's presence only as a melody, not as a living entity. The target no longer needs to eat or drink, gains the ostinato's Magic Resistance trait, and has advantage on Charisma checks. It also has disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws and it can't maintain concentration on spells or other effects for more than a single turn. The target can make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check once every 24 hours; on a success, it realizes that the music it hears comes from an external entity.

The Aural Symbiosis lasts until the target drops to 0 hit points, the ostinato ends it as a bonus action, or the ostinato is forced out by a dispel evil and good spell or comparable magic. When the Aural Symbiosis ends, the ostinato bursts forth in a thunderous explosion of sound and reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target. All creatures within 60 feet, including the original target, take 21 ({@damage 6d6}) thunder damage, or half damage with a successful {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. The target becomes immune to this ostinato's Aural Symbiosis for 24 hours if it succeeds on the saving throw or after the Aural Symbiosis ends.

action.name: Voracious Aura (1/Day)
entries: While merged with a humanoid (see Aural Symbiosis), the ostinato feeds on nearby creatures. Up to nine creatures of the ostinato's choice within 60 feet of it can be targeted. Each target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Charisma saving throw or take 3 ({@damage 1d6}) necrotic damage and have its hit point maximum reduced by the same amount until it finishes a long rest. weapon.name: Arcane Cannon
weapon.crew: 3x Lvl 1-7 spellcasters or 1x lvl 8+ spell caster
entries: It takes 1 action to choose the firing mode, 1 action to aim it, and 1 action to fire it. If the user is a spellcaster of level 8 or highter, then they may do all these three on one action. When the airship is started, this arcane cannon whirls to life with 20 charges. Each use of the arcane cannon consumes a portion of this charge based on the firing mode.
The Arcane Cannon's effects have a saving DC of 19 and a +11 to hit on attacks.

action.name: Firing Mode : Chain Lightning (6 Charges)
entries: You create a bolt of lightning that arcs toward a target of your choice that you can see within 150ft. Three bolts then leap from that target to as many as three other targets, each of which must be within 30 feet of the first target. A target can be a creature or an object and can be targeted by only one of the bolts.
A target must make a Dexterity saving throw. The target takes {@damage 10d8} lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Firing Mode : Chain Enervation (7 Charges)
entries: You fire a bolt of negative energy at one creature you can see within 200ft. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the bolt does {@damage 12d6} necrotic damage and the creature must make a successful Constitution saving throw or gain two levels of {@condition exhaustion}. The bolt then leaps to another target within 50 feet of the previous target that hasn't already been targeted by the spell; if more than one is available, you may choose which target to attack. The effect continues attacking creatures one after another in a chain until it misses or there are no more creatures eligible to be hit.

action.name: Firing Mode : Circle of Death (6 Charges)
entries: A sphere of negative energy ripples out in a 60-foot-radius sphere from a point within 150 feet range. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. A target takes {@damage 8d6} necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Firing Mode : Cloak bubble (4 Charges)
entries: The entire ship becomes {@condition invisible} until the spell ends (1 hour). Anything the ship is carrying is {@condition invisible} as long as it is on the ship.

action.name: Firing Mode : Deadline (5 Charges)
entries: You fire a 1-inch-wide, 60-foot-long beam of senescent energy that pierces through creatures, objects, and structures alike at untraceable speed. An object or structure pierced by the beam has its AC permanently reduced by 4 if it is inorganic. If it is organic, the point pierced by the beam and the object or structure's material within 1 foot of the beam decays and ages until it is brittle enough to break by a light touch.

A creature pierced by the beam must make a Constitution saving throw. It takes {@damage 10d8} necrotic damage and instantly ages {@dice 2d4 x 10} years on a failed save; if this damage would reduce a creature to 0 hit points, it falls {@condition unconscious} and is stable instead of dying, and it ages an additional year for each point of damage it took in excess of its current hit points. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't aged.

The aging can be reversed with the greater restoration spell or more powerful magic, but only if it is cast within 24 hours of failing the saving throw. After that time, only a wish spell can reverse the effect.

optionalfeature.name: Enhanced Arcane Focus
entries: While holding this item, a creature gains a +1 bonus to spell attack and damage rolls. In addition, the creature ignores half cover when making a spell attack.
The bonus increases to +2 when you reach 10th level in this class.

optionalfeature.name: Administerer
entries: As a bonus action, you may load an ampoule of potion or poison as an injectible dart. You can then replace an attack with an application of the potion or poison to a single target. You need not make an attack roll for a willing creature within range but you must if you recieve disadvantage from any source. The target then on a hit takes no damage from an ampoule and recieves its benefits.

optionalfeature.name: Enhanced Tools

optionalfeature.name: Adamantine Armour

entries: While wearing this armour, any critical hit against you turns into a normal hit.

entries: While wearing it, if the armour normally imposes disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks or has a Strength requirement, this version of the armour doesn't. A mithral chain shirt or breastplate can be worn under normal clothes. At level 10, this armour gains a +1 bonus to AC.

optionalfeature.name: Strengthened Link

{@b Aggressive Stance}

items: The defender's movement speed increases by 10 feet.
The defender has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of it's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't {@condition incapacitated}.
It gains +2 to it's attack and damage rolls.

entries: {@b Defensive Stance}

items: When the defender uses its deflect attack feature, it can target a creature within 10 feet.

You can task the defender to guard a creature. On it's turn, it can spend an action to shadow a creature horizontally adjacent to it. If the creature moves, the defender follows by taking the same route. It stops following if the creature teleports more than 5 feet away from the defender. While the defender remains adjacent to the creature, both of them gain the benefit of a {@action dodge} action. Till the start of it's next turn, if any creature within 10 feet attempts to attack either creature, the defender can use it's reaction to make one attack.
It gains +2 AC.

entries: {@i Requires Infusion}
Doubles the range of spells cast from the cockpit

optionalfeature.name: Sabre
entries: A massive blade that deals {@damage 1d12} Slashing damage on a hit.

optionalfeature.name: Scutum
entries: Not so much a weapon as it is a shield that grants +2 AC wehn slotted. You can bash with it for {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage.

optionalfeature.name: Pincers
entries: A tentacle like grappling implement. You can pick up objects and grapple creatures with this. An attack made with the Pincers against a grappled target is made with advanatage dealing {@damage 1d8} piercing damage on a hit.

optionalfeature.name: Bolts
entries: A lightweight cannon that shoots bolts of force dealing {@damage 1d8} force damage on a hit.

optionalfeature.name: DK Beam
entries: {@i Requires two weapon slots}
A heavy cannon that blast disintegrating energy dealing {@damage 1d12} necrotic damage on a hit.

optionalfeature.name: Rolling Guns
entries: {@i Requires two weapon slots}
a set of two repeating guns that fire rapidly dealing {@damage 2d4} piercing damage on a hit. After using an action to attack with this weapon you may use a bonus action to make another.

optionalfeature.name: Energy Sabre
entries: An upgrade of the {@optfeature Sabre|tct}. It now deals an additional {@damage 1d8} fire or lightning damage (decided on hit).

optionalfeature.name: Barrier
entries: An upgrade of the {@optfeature Scutum|tct}. It now deals {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage to a creature and grants the next attack made against it advantage before the start of the creatures turn.
As a reaction to an ally within 5 of you getting attacked, you can add the barriers AC bonus to the creature's AC.

optionalfeature.name: Appendage
entries: An upgrade of the {@optfeature Pincers|tct}. It's reach increases by a further 5 feet. It's damage increases to {@damage 1d10} and a grappled creature takes lightning damage equal to your Intelligence modifier at the start of it's turn.

optionalfeature.name: Javelins
entries: An upgrade of the {@optfeature Bolts|tct}. It now deals {@damage 1d10} damage on a hit. Once per turn when you hit a creature with this weapon you can force it to make a Strength Saving Throw, being either pushed away by 15 feet or falling {@condition prone} pm a failure.

optionalfeature.name: Atomizer
entries: {@i Requires two weapon slots}
An upgrade of the {@optfeature DK Beam|tct}. The weapon now deals an additional {@damage 1d6} damage and can change its damage type to radiant on any attack.

optionalfeature.name: Running Guns
entries: {@i Requires two weapon slots}

An upgrade of the {@optfeature Rolling Guns|tct}. It no longer has its's bonus action attack. Instead, Once on your turn when you make an attack with this weapon, you can make an additional attack with it as part of the attack.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Cloak
entries: Your grants you a cover to protect you from harm. It can take take form of a cloak, a robe or a cape. The cloak acts as mystical storage that appears non-magical to divination magic. With your hand within the cloak you may draw or stow an item no heavier than 10 lbs. and as large as can be obscured by the cloak. The cloak this way can store items upto 50 lbs. in weight. When inspected by anyone besides the pact keeper the cloak appears to be a plain piece of cloth with no trace of the items stored.

If you lose or destroy the cloak, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive another from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a rest, destroying the previous one in the process. The cloak becomes extremely brittle when you die and it's contents manifesting nearby.

optionalfeature.name: Twice Armed
entries: You can now turn a second magical weapon into your pact weapon. You must perform the required ritual as usual and if attempting to do the ritual for a third magical weapon, a pact weapon of your choice must break its bond with you.

You can summon two pact weapons or two of the same pact weapon with an action, provided both your hands are free and gain the benefit of the {@optfeature two-weapon fighting} feature when fighting with them.

optionalfeature.name: Protection of the Cloak
entries: You may flip the cloak as a reaction to an attack and gain the benefit of the {@spell shield} spell. You may use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Shroud's Embrace
entries: The cloak wraps tighter and produces warmth or chill as necessary. The wearer of the cloak has resistance to cold damage. In addition, you and everything you wear and carry are unharmed by temperatures as low as -50 degrees Fahrenheit and as high as 150 fahrenheit.

optionalfeature.name: Breakfall Veil
entries: The wearer of the Pact of the Cloak descends at 60 feet per round and may move 2 feet horizontally for every foot they descend. The wearer experiences no damage from falling this way.

optionalfeature.name: Cowl of Oblivion
entries: You know the spell {@spell Greater Invisibility}. For you, it is a warlock spell and it doesn't count against the limit on the number of spells you know and can cast it once without expending a warlock spell slot.

optionalfeature.name: Mantle of Mercy
entries: Once per short rest, you can use a reaction to receive only half damage from an instance.

optionalfeature.name: Cerement of Safety
entries: When you drop to 0 hitpoint you can with your remaining consciousness designate a place you can see within 10 feet of you. You turn {@condition invisible}, teleport there and you fall {@condition unconscious}. When you are {@condition unconscious} even when you are sleeping, you remain invisible to all besides people you have designated as allies.

optionalfeature.name: Know Thy Blade
entries: You are able to use the mastery property of your pact weapon.

optionalfeature.name: Otherworldy Creation
entries: You know the {@spell fabricate} spell and can cast it once per day without a spell slot. You also gain an alternate way to cast this spell. This way, the spell becomes a conjuration spell as the components are sent to an extraplanar destination and return near instantly as the product you desired.

optionalfeature.name: Instruction of the Archive
entries: The Archive empowers your Book of Shadows, granting you the ability to record spells. Choose {@filter three Wizard Spells|spells|level=1|class=wizard} when you receive this invocation. You can now prepare two additional spells every long rest that are recorded within this book. You may also record spells in this book as a wizard would in his spellbook.

optionalfeature.name: Token of Ability
entries: Whenever making a dice roll by the talisman, you may roll another dice and add it to the result.

optionalfeature.name: Bestowed Sapience
entries: Your Patron bestows your familiar witha a fragment of the Archives wisdom.

items: Familiars your summon now possess an Intelligence score of 17 and are sapient creatures.
You can summon {@creature inkling mascot|scc} or {@creature oblex spawn|mpmm} when you cast {@spell find familiar}.
When rolling for initiative you can choose have your familiar have the same initiative as you.
You can command your familiar to attack without an action.

optionalfeature.name: Cleave
entries: If you hit a creature with a melee attack using this {@table Cleaving Weapons|tct|weapon}, you can make an attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don’t add your ability modifier to that damage, unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Graze
entries: If your attack roll with this {@table Grazing Weapons|tct|weapon} misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can’t be increased in any way, other than increasing the ability modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Push
entries: If you hit a creature with this {@table Push Weapons|tct|weapon}, you can push the creature up to 10 feet away from you horizontally if it is no more than one size larger than you.

optionalfeature.name: Sap

prerequisite.other: Versatile property or No other properties

entries: If you hit a creature with this {@table Sapping Weapons|tct|weapon}, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Slow
entries: If you hit a creature with this {@table Slowing Weapons|tct|weapon} and deal damage to the creature, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If you hit the creature more than once with this property, the Speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Topple
entries: If you hit a creature with this {@table Toppling Weapons|tct|weapon}, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition prone} condition.

optionalfeature.name: Vex
entries: If you hit a creature with this {@table Vexing Weapons|tct|weapon} and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tumble
entries: If you hit a creature with a melee attack from this {@table Tumbling Weapons|tct|weapon} and deal damage to the creature, You can move through into the creature's space once without spending movement speed.

optionalfeature.name: Adopted Magics
entries: Choose 2 cantrips and a level 1 spell from the {@filter Sorcerer|spells|level=0;1|class=sorcerer}, {@filter Wizard|spells|level=0;1|class=wizard} or {@filter Warlock|spells|level=0;1|class=warlock} spell lists. They now count as druid spells for you, are always prepared and do not count towards the number of spells prepared.

optionalfeature.name: Bestial Speech
entries: You can cast {@spell speak with animals} at will without expending a spell slot.

optionalfeature.name: Monstrous Shape
entries: You can now Wild Shape into Monstrosities. you must still meet the CR limitation.

optionalfeature.name: Borrowed Essence
entries: As part of a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.

optionalfeature.name: Flow of Entropy
entries: You can cast {@spell chaos bolt} as a cantrip once per turn.
You mast cast it more than once at level 11

optionalfeature.name: Ballroom Bane

spell: A cantrip that causes poison damage

entries: A creature who fails the saving of {@filter a poison cantrip you cast|spells|damage=acid|level=0} you cast will be {@condition poisoned} till the start of your next turn.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to poison damage.

optionalfeature.name: Break Down

spell: A cantrip that causes acid damage

entries: Once per turn, a creature who fails the saving throw of {@filter an acidic cantrip you cast|spells|damage=acid|level=0} you cast will have it's AC reduced by 1 until the start of your next turn.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to acid damage.

optionalfeature.name: Move and Shake

spell: A cantrip that causes thunder damage

entries: Once per turn, when you cast {@filter a cantrip that deals thunder damage|spells|damage=thunder|level=0}, you may force a creature receiving such damage to make a Strength save, failing which will make it either fall {@condition prone} or be pushed horizontally upto 10 feet. You may force the save a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier before a long rest
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to thunder damage.

optionalfeature.name: Smooth as Ice

spell: A cantrip that causes cold damage

entries: Once per casting of {@filter a cantrip that deals cold damage|spells|damage=cold|level=0}, you freeze a 10 foot radius area around your target, rendering it difficult terrain regardless of whether the attack hits or not. This area lasts till the start of your next turn.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to cold damage.

optionalfeature.name: Burning Sensation

spell: A cantrip that causes fire damage

entries: When you roll damage for {@filter a cantrip that deals fire damage|spells|damage=fire|level=0}, treat the dice as exploding dice.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to fire damage.

optionalfeature.name: Auxiliary Power

spell: A cantrip that causes lightning damage

entries: When a creature takes damage from {@filter a cantrip that deals lightning damage|spells|damage=lightning|level=0}, For each die that rolled max, you may roll another damage die and damage a creature within 30 feet of the target.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to lightning damage.

optionalfeature.name: Life-Tap Dance

spell: A cantrip that causes necrotic damage

entries: When a creature takes damage from {@filter a cantrip that deals necrotic damage|spells|damage=necrotic|level=0}, For each die that rolled max, you may roll a damage die and heal yourself or willing creature within 30 feet of the target for the amount.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to necrotic damage.

optionalfeature.name: Blinding Lights

spell: A cantrip that causes radiant damage

entries: Once per turn, when a creature takes damage from {@filter a cantrip that deals radiant damage|spells|damage=radiant|level=0}, You can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw or be blinded till the start of your next turn. You can force the save a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier.
Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to radiant damage.

optionalfeature.name: Know Thine Every Move

spell: A cantrip that causes psychic damage

entries: Once per turn, when a creature takes damage from {@filter a cantrip that deals psychic damage|spells|damage=psychic|level=0}, You create a fleeting mental link with the target. While linked like this you gain the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: You know the creatures location, while it remains within 60 feet of you.
It does not gain the benefits of being {@condition invisible} or hidden from you.
It cannot receive advantage on attacks against you.

entries: Additionally, your cantrips ignore resistance to psychic damage.

optionalfeature.name: Wind Warp
entries: In addition to the area of effect of {@spell Air Trick|tct} increasing to a 10 foot cube, You gain the following options when you cast it:-

items: You can cause a light or strong breeze to pass through the area, creatures in the area of a strong breeze are {@condition deafened}.

You can create a dense fog in the area, {@quickref Vision and Light|PHB|2||heavilly obscuring} it. You can also use your action to thicken or rarify fog in as you like, making it heavily obscured, lightly obscured or transparent. Any wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses it.
You can cause a deafening burst of sound. Creatures must succeed a Constitution saving throw or be deafened until the end of their next turn. It can also be heard upto 700 feet away.

optionalfeature.name: Quick Temper
entries: You may cast the {@spell Blade Ward} spell as a bonus action a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier. You gain all such uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Jeté
entries: As a bonus action on your turn, you can leap 10 feet without spending your movement.
The leap distance improves as you take levels in this class. Going to 20 at level 5, 30 feet at level 11 and 40 feet at level 17.

optionalfeature.name: Enhanced Elusion
entries: You may wear medium armour and still retain the benefits of Elusion and Fleet of Foot.
Additionally, If a medium armour you are wearing imposes disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks, it no longer does so.

optionalfeature.name: The Toss from Across
entries: Your range for Flickwrist cantrips is doubled. This does not apply to cantrips with the range of 'Self'.

optionalfeature.name: Arsenal of the Mind
entries: When you cast {@spell Phantom Weapon|tct}, You may instead conjure upto two weapons that you can hold and gain the following benefits with them:

items: You treat attacks with them as weapon attacks, using your Dexterity modifier for Attack and Damage rolls.
They count as poise weapons if they arent ranged or {@b Heavy}, gaining the {@b Light} property if so
Thrown weapons reappear in your hand instead of disappearing after being thrown.
Ranged weapons may conjure ammunition as part of the attack if not provided.

optionalfeature.name: Style Fusion
entries: With some effort you have combined two casting styles into one. As a result, you learn one Casting Style option in addition to the one you know.
Whenever you reach a level that grants an additional Choreurgic Mastery, you can replace this feat's casting style with another one from this class that you don't have.

optionalfeature.name: Will-o-Wisp Waltz
entries: You recieve the following options and features when you cast {@spell Dancing Lights}:-

items: Upon casting the spell, you may have the created lights hover around you, following you as you move.

You may use a bonus action to launch an orb from where it is 60 feet towards a creature you can see, making a ranged spell attack against it. The light is then extinguished, dealing {@damage 2d6} radiant damage on a hit. You may do the same with a conglomeration of orbs, with it instead dealing {@damage 4d6} radiant damage.

A union of orbs instead sheds bright light in a 20 feet around it and dim light for another 20 feet. {@condition invisible} creatures or objects in its bright light it do not benefit from the condition.

The number of lights produced by this spell increases as you gain levels in this class, gaining two more each at level 5,11 and 17. A union of these orbs grants more light as well, each radius improving by 10 feet at level 5,11 and 17.

optionalfeature.name: Choreum Proxima
entries: While not wearing shields, medium or heavy armour, your AC equals 10 + your Intelligence modifier + your Dexterity modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Effortless Moves
entries: Cantrips that require concentration, no longer do when you cast them. Though if you cast a concentration cantrip while another is still active, the earlier casting ends.

optionalfeature.name: Free Expression
entries: You may cast a cantrip without its verbal and material component. Checks made to dispel or {@spell counterspell} your cantrips are also made with disadvantage.

optionalfeature.name: Art of Long-Fire
entries: The reach of {@spell Green-Flame Blade|tce} extends to the reach of your weapon. In addition, you can cause the fire to leap from the target to a different creature of your choice that you can see within 15 feet of it.

optionalfeature.name: Gale
entries: The spell {@spell Gust|xge} improves in the following ways when you cast it:-

items: The spell can now affect creatures of large size
When a creature fails the saving throw, it is pushed upto 20 away.
The object that can be moved can way upto 20 pounds and can be pushed upto 30 feet away.

optionalfeature.name: Hook Turn
entries: When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to cast a cantrip at the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack. The spell must have a casting time of 1 action and must target only that creature.

optionalfeature.name: Enhanced Deflection
entries: You may attempt to grant advantage to a creature 30 feet away against a spells saving throw and you may do so with one hand free.

optionalfeature.name: Enhanced Stability
entries: You can also reroll one damage die of a cantrip you cast, regardless of the result.

optionalfeature.name: Deepened Esotericism
entries: You can pick an additional 2 cantrips from the {@filter Druid|spells|level=0|class=Druid}, {@filter Cleric|spells|level=0|class=Cleric}, {@filter Warlock|spells|level=0|class=Warlock} or {@filter Bard|spells|level=0|class=Bard}. They count as Flickwrist cantrips and you may add it to the cantrips you know. These cantrips do not count towards your Cantrips Known limit.
Flickwrist cantrips do not benefit from Eldritch Invocations.

optionalfeature.name: Enhanced Spellbending
entries: As long as you know the location of the creature and an unobstructed path of a length less than or equal to the range exists between you and the target, you can target it and do not suffer any disadvantages from it remaining unseen or {@condition invisible}

optionalfeature.name: Lengthened 'Lectric Lasso
entries: When you cast {@spell Lightning Lure|tce}, the range of the spell increases to 30 feet. And on a failure, you may move the target in any horizontal direction that isnt further from you. On a failure, you may also choose to deal the damage it would have received if it had landed 5 feet next to you.

optionalfeature.name: Fuego
entries: You can cast {@spell burning hands} as a cantrip once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Stone's Throw
entries: You can cast {@spell catapult|xge} as a cantrip once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: The Grand Illusion
entries: you can cast {@spell silent mage} as a cantrip.

optionalfeature.name: Sun's Arrows
entries: You can cast {@spell scorching ray} as a cantrip once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Sauté
entries: You can cast {@spell jump} as a cantrip.

optionalfeature.name: 1-Tonne-Stomp
entries: You can cast {@spell earth tremor|xge} as a cantrip once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Bolts out of the Blue
entries: You can cast {@spell magic missile} as a cantrip.

optionalfeature.name: Captivating Performance
entries: You can cast {@spell enthrall} as a cantrip once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Weave Sense
entries: You can cast {@spell detect magic} as a cantrip.

optionalfeature.name: Elemental Fluidity
entries: You can change the damage type of a cantrip cast to the type of one cast prior on the same turn.

optionalfeature.name: Hasty Haven
entries: Once per turn, you can cast {@spell sanctuary} as a cantrip. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence Modifier before a long rest

optionalfeature.name: Delayed Departure
entries: When you cast {@spell spare the dying}, the target you stabilize continues to make death saving throws but now at advantage, ignoring failed saves and reviving on a roll of 19 or 20. Additionally, if damaged while stabilized by this spell, the creature takes one less failure.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Chain
entries: You learn the {@spell find familiar} spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.

When you cast the spell, you can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: {@creature imp}, {@creature pseudodragon}, {@creature quasit}, or {@creature sprite}.
Additionally, when you take the {@action Attack} action or cast {@spell eldritch blast}, you allow your familiar to use its reaction to make one attack of its own.

optionalfeature.name: Protection of the Blade
entries: You gain proficiency in Medium armor.

optionalfeature.name: Lifedrinker
entries: When you hit a creature with your pact weapon, the creature takes extra necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

optionalfeature.name: Devouring Blade
entries: The Extra Attack of your {@optfeature Thirsting Blade|XPHB} invocation confers two extra attacks rather than one.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Blade
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can conjure a pact weapon in your hand—a Simple or Martial Melee weapon of your choice with which you bond—or create a bond with a magic weapon you touch; you can't bond with a magic weapon if someone else is attuned to it or another Warlock is bonded with it. Until the bond ends, you have proficiency with the weapon, and you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}.

Whenever you attack with the bonded weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity; and you can cause the weapon to deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage or its normal damage type.

Your bond with the weapon ends if you use this feature's {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} again, if the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you die. A conjured weapon disappears when the bond ends.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Talisman
entries: Your patron gives you an amulet, a talisman that can aid the wearer when the need is great. When the wearer fails an ability check, they can add a {@dice d6} to the roll, potentially turning the roll into a success. This benefit can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and all expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.

If you lose the talisman, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous amulet. The talisman turns to ash when you die.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Tome
entries: Stitching together strands of shadow, you conjure forth a book in your hand at the end of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. This Book of Shadows (you determine its appearance) contains eldritch magic that only you can access, granting you the benefits below. The book disappears if you conjure another book with this feature or if you die.

entries.name: Cantrips and Rituals
entries: When the book appears, choose three cantrips, and choose two level 1 spells that have the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag. The spells can be from any class's spell list, and they must be spells you don't already have prepared. While the book is on your person, you have the chosen spells prepared, and they function as Warlock spells for you.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use the book as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Chain
entries: You learn the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell and can cast it as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action without expending a spell slot.

When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: {@creature Imp|XPHB}, {@creature Pseudodragon|XPHB}, {@creature Quasit|XPHB}, {@creature Skeleton|XPHB}, {@creature Slaad Tadpole|XPHB}, {@creature Sphinx of Wonder|XPHB}, {@creature Sprite|XPHB}, or {@creature Venomous Snake|XPHB} (see appendix B for the familiar's stat block).
Additionally, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Banishing Arrow
entries: You use abjuration magic to try to temporarily banish your target to a harmless location in the Feywild. The creature hit by the arrow must also succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished. While banished in this way, the target's speed is 0, and it is {@condition incapacitated}. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it vacated or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
After you reach 10th level in this class, a target also takes {@damage d6} force damage when the arrow hits it. This damage increases to {@damage 2d6} at 18th level.

optionalfeature.name: Beguiling Arrow
entries: Your enchantment magic causes this arrow to temporarily beguile its target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra {@damage 2d6} psychic damage, and choose one of your allies within 30 feet of the target. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it is {@condition charmed} by the chosen ally until the start of your next turn. This effect ends early if the chosen ally attacks the {@condition charmed} target, deals damage to it, or forces it to make a saving throw.
The psychic damage increases to {@damage 3d6} and {@damage 4d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Bursting Arrow
entries: You imbue your arrow with force energy drawn from the school of evocation. The energy detonates after your attack. Immediately after the arrow hits the creature, the target and all other creatures within 10 feet of it take {@damage 2d6} force damage each.
The force damage increases to {@damage 3d6} and {@damage 4d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Enfeebling Arrow
entries: You weave necromantic magic into your arrow. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage. The target must also succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or the damage dealt by its weapon attacks is halved until the start of your next turn.
The necrotic damage increases to {@damage 3d6} and {@damage 4d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Grasping Arrow
entries: When this arrow strikes its target, conjuration magic creates grasping, poisonous brambles, which wrap around the target. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra {@damage 2d6} poison damage, its speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it takes {@damage 2d6} slashing damage the first time on each turn it moves 1 foot or more without teleporting. The target or any creature that can reach it can use its action to remove the brambles with a successful Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against your Arcane Shot save DC. Otherwise, the brambles last for 1 minute or until you use this option again.
The poison damage and slashing damage both increase to {@damage 3d6} and {@damage 4d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Piercing Arrow
entries: You use transmutation magic to give your arrow an ethereal quality. When you use this option, you don't make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, the arrow shoots forward in a line, which is 1 foot wide and 30 feet long, before disappearing. The arrow passes harmlessly through objects, ignoring cover. Each creature in that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra {@damage 2d6} piercing damage. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage.
The piercing damage increases to {@damage 4d6} and {@damage 6d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Seeking Arrow
entries: Using divination magic, you grant your arrow the ability to seek out a target. When you use this option, you don't make an attack roll for the attack. Instead, choose one creature you have seen in the past minute. The arrow flies toward that creature, moving around corners if necessary and ignoring three-quarters cover and half cover. If the target is within the weapon's range and there is a path large enough for the arrow to travel to the target, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. Otherwise, the arrow disappears after traveling as far as it can. On a failed save, the target takes damage as if it were hit by the arrow, plus an extra {@damage 2d6} force damage, and you learn the target's current location. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage, and you don't learn its location.
The force damage increases to {@damage 3d6} and {@damage 4d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Shadow Arrow
entries: You weave illusion magic into your arrow, causing it to occlude your foe's vision with shadows. The creature hit by the arrow takes an extra {@damage 2d6} psychic damage, and a 5 ft dome of magical darkness appears at the creature's space until the start of your next turn.
The psychic damage increases to {@damage 3d6} and {@damage 4d6} when you reach 10th and 18th level in this class respectively.

optionalfeature.name: Careful Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the spell's full force. To do so, you spend 1 sorcery point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell, and it takes no damage if it would normally take half damage on a successful save.

optionalfeature.name: Esotoric Spell
entries: When you cast a spell with the Ritual tag, you can spend 1 sorcery point to cast the spell without expending the spell slot.

optionalfeature.name: Extended Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.
If the affected spell requires concentration, you have advantage on any saving throw you make to maintain that concentration.

optionalfeature.name: Heightened Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 2 sorcery points to give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Seeking Spell
entries: If you make an attack roll for a spell and miss, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll the {@dice d20}, and you must use the new roll.
You can use Seeking Spell even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Transmuted Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can spend 1 sorcery point to change that damage type to one of the other listed types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, thunder.
You can use Transmuted Spell even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Twinned Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range with the same spell (1 sorcery point if the spell is a cantrip).
If you twin a spell that requires concentration, the minimum DC for concentration saves is increased by an amount equal to the level of the spell (maximum of 5).

To be eligible, a spell must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the spell's current level. For example, {@spell magic missile} and {@spell scorching ray} aren't eligible, but {@spell ray of frost} and {@spell chromatic orb} are.

optionalfeature.name: Illuminating Mark (1)
entries: The marked creature cannot benefit from the {@condition invisible} or hidden condition against you.

optionalfeature.name: Pursuing Mark (1)
entries: You gain an additional 10 ft of movement speed when moving towards the marked creature.

optionalfeature.name: Strafing Mark (1)
entries: When the marked creature enters within 10 feet of you, you can immediately use your reaction to move up to half of your movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Blinding Mark (1)
entries: The marked creature has disadvantage on all checks that require sight.

optionalfeature.name: Leashing Mark (1)
entries: The marked creature's movement speed is reduced by 10 feet if it is more than 60 feet away from you.

optionalfeature.name: Elusive Mark (1)
entries: The marked creature has disadvantage on perception checks to detect you. Additionally, you can attempt to hide from the marked creature while behind half or three-fourths cover.

optionalfeature.name: Cardinal Mark (1)
entries: You know the direction of the creature as long as it is marked.

optionalfeature.name: Vengeful Mark (1)
entries: When the marked creature deals damage to you, it takes force damage equal to your mark die. This damage is only dealt once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Focused Mark (1)
entries: Your attacks ignore disadvantage when attacking a marked creature.

optionalfeature.name: Insightful Mark (1)
entries: You learn of any special senses (such as truesight or tremorsense) of the marked creature. Additionally, whenever the mark deals damage to the creature you learn whether it is resistant, vulnerable or immune to a single damage type or condition.

optionalfeature.name: Unveiling Mark (1)
entries: You learn of any magic affecting the marked creature. You also learn of any magical items in its possession, although you do not learn the nature or properties of these items. Any effect that would block divination magic (such as the {@spell nondetection} spell), will block this feature.

optionalfeature.name: Rejuvenating Mark (1)
entries: You regain hitpoints equal to the damage dealt by hunter's mark.

optionalfeature.name: Crippling Mark (1)
entries: The marked creature has disadvantage on all saving throws against you.

optionalfeature.name: Seismic Mark (1)
entries: The mark's damage is dealt in a 10 foot radius around the marked creature.

optionalfeature.name: Blurring Mark (1)
entries: The marked creature has disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

optionalfeature.name: Convergent Mark (2)
entries: Your hunter's mark die size improves by 1 (d4->d6, d6->d8). Whenever you hit a marked creature with an attack, you can choose to dissolve the mark, taking the maximum possible result for each damage die instead of rolling for the attacks damage.

optionalfeature.name: Ruthless Mark (2)
entries: All attacks made against the marked creature within 5 feet of it are made with advantage. If the creature is bloodied, then all attacks made within 30 feet of it are made with advantage

optionalfeature.name: Repressing Mark (2)
entries: You can choose to repress a single damage or condition resistance of the marked creature.

optionalfeature.name: Enfeebling Mark (2)
entries: When the marked creature deals damage, you can use your reaction to halve it for that instance.

optionalfeature.name: Apex Mark (2)
entries: You have advantage on all saving throws that the marked creature forces you to make.

optionalfeature.name: Frenzied Mark (2)
entries: Any creature that attacks the marked target deal the marks damage. Creatures other than you can only do so once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Divine Mark (2)
entries: You always know the exact position of the marked creature, and the marked creature cannot benefit from the {@condition invisible} condition. When you look at the creature, you do so as if you had truesight.

optionalfeature.name: Lethal Mark (2)
entries: All attacks against the marked creature is a critical hit on a roll of 18, 19 or 20.

optionalfeature.name: Draconic Mark (2)
entries: When you land an attack against the marked creature, your drake can immediately use its reaction to use it's breath towards the marked creature without expending a use of it. It can only do so once per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Feywild Mark (2)
entries: Any fey under your control can use their reaction to hit a creature within their range whenever you attack the marked creature.

optionalfeature.name: Slayer's Mark (2)
entries: When you hit the marked creature with an attack, you can choose to give it vulnerability to the next instance of damage dealt to it by a creature other than you. The vulnerability goes away if the marked creature deals damage to you.

optionalfeature.name: Befuddling Mark (3)
entries: When you hit a marked creature with an attack, you can force it to make a wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is under the effects of the {@spell confusion} spell until the start of your turn.

optionalfeature.name: Ethereal Mark (3)
entries: When you hit a marked creature with an attack, you can change your attack's damage type to force.

optionalfeature.name: Swarming Mark (2)
entries: All units under your control deal hunter's mark damage. Additionally, units under your control do not provoke opportunity attacks from the marked creature.

optionalfeature.name: Stalker's Mark (2)
entries: The marked creature cannot see you through any means other than truesight or aethersense.

optionalfeature.name: Taxing Mark (2)
entries: Each consecutive attack you land on the marked creature reduces its Armor class by 1. The effect goes away at the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Nimble I
entries: Your movement speed increases by 5 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Survivor
entries: You gain proficiency with the {@skill Survival} skill. If you already have proficiency, you gain expertise with the skill instead.

optionalfeature.name: Wilderness Expert
entries: You gain proficiency with the {@skill Nature} skill, the {@item poisoner's kit|phb} and the {@item herbalism kit|phb}. When you make an intelligence {@skill Nature} check, you can instead make a wisdom {@skill Nature} check.
you have advantage on checks made in order to identify plants, along with their medicinal or poisonous properties.

optionalfeature.name: Wildlife Expert I
entries: You gain proficiency with the {@skill Animal Handling} skill. Additionally, you gain advantage on checks made to identify or track a creature through their footsteps, scent, anatomy or other such natural indicators.

optionalfeature.name: Underdark Explorer
entries: You gain darkvision of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, it's range is increased by 30 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Alpine Adept
entries: You gain climbing speed equal to your walking speed. If you already have climbing speed, it's speed is increased by 10 feet.
When you take fall damage, you can reduce it by an amount equal to your ranger level + your constitution modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Aquatic Adept
entries: You gain swimming speed equal to your walking speed. If you already have swimming speed, it's speed is increased by 10 feet.
While you are underwater, you can hold your breath for a number of hours equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down).

optionalfeature.name: Craftsman
entries: You gain proficiency in an {@item artisan's tools|PHB} of your choice.
The time required to craft an item is reduced by a percentage equal to 10 time your proficiency bonus if you are using a tool that you are proficient with.

optionalfeature.name: Tenacious I
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to your armor class and saving throws if you are under half your hitpoints.

optionalfeature.name: Sturdy I
entries: When you roll a hit die to regain hitpoints, you can roll twice and choose either roll.

optionalfeature.name: Outdoorsman
entries: You can add your proficiency bonus on saving throws made in order to resist the environment.

optionalfeature.name: Strongbow
entries: You can use your strength modifier rather than your dexterity modifier for attack and damage rolls when using a hand-drawn bow (shortbow, longbow, etc).

optionalfeature.name: Tenacious II
entries: When you drop to 0 hitpoints, you can drop to 1 hitpoint instead. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Covert I
entries: You can use the {@action hide} action as a bonus action. Additionally, creatures have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks against you when you are surrounded by foliage.

optionalfeature.name: Covert II
entries: You draw on the powers of nature to hide yourself from view briefly. As a bonus action, you can magically become {@condition invisible}, along with any equipment you are wearing or carrying, until the start of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Covert III
entries: When you or a creature of your choice that you can see makes a dexterity {@skill Stealth} check while in natural terrain, they gain a bonus to that stealth check equal to your wisdom modifier.
Your critical hit range for attacks is reduced by 1 if you are hidden or invisible from the target.

optionalfeature.name: Covert IV
entries: You always have the {@spell greater invisibility} spell prepared, and you can cast it once per day without expending a spell slot. Additionally, when you cast this spell on yourself, you can forgo the need to concentrate on it.

optionalfeature.name: Sturdy II
entries: When you take damage, you can reduce that damage taken by an amount equal to your constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Nimble II
entries: Your speed increases by an additionaly 5 feet and you ignore non-magical difficult terrain. You also have advantage on athletics or acrobatics checks made to avoid or escape a grapple.

optionalfeature.name: Herbalist I
entries: You automatically succeed on {@skill Medicine} checks in order to stabilise a creature. Additionally, you can create two {@item healing potion} whenever you finish a long rest, provided you have a herbalism kit with you.
Healing potions created with this imbibement tree lose their potency when you finish your next long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Poisoner I
entries: You have advantage on checks made in order to identify toxins. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can create two vials of {@item basic poison}.
You can coat poison on your weapons and ammunition by using a bonus action, rather than an action.
Any poison created with this imbibement tree loses its potency when you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Desert Dweller
entries: You have resistance to fire damage.
You have advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Survival} checks when in a desert.

optionalfeature.name: Tundra Traveller
entries: You have resistance to cold damage.
You have advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Survival} checks when in the arctic.

optionalfeature.name: Jungle Junket
entries: You have resistance to poison damage.
You have advantage on checks made in order to assist in navigation through a forest or jungle.

optionalfeature.name: Abyssal Adventurer
entries: You have resistance to acid damage.
You have advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Survival} checks when underwater.

optionalfeature.name: Urban Wanderer
entries: You gain resistance to one of bludgeoning, slashing or piercing damage.
You have advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Survival} checks when in a town or a city.

optionalfeature.name: Armorsmith
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item smiths's tools|phb} and {@item leatherworker's tools|phb}.
you can spend one hour as part of a rest in order to maintain a set of armor. the maintained armor gains benefits for the next 24 hours depending on its type.

items: {@b Light:} The wearer gains an additional 5 feet of movement speed.
{@b Medium:} The wearer does not suffer from disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks and have advantage on saving throws made against going prone or being moved against your will.
{@b Heavy:} The wearer gains an additional +1 bonus to their armor class.

optionalfeature.name: Weaponsmith
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item smiths's tools|phb} and {@item leatherworker's tools|phb} and {@item woodcarver's tools|phb}.
you can spend one hour as part of a rest in order to maintain up to two weapons. the maintained weapons Gain a benefit for the next 24 hours depending on their property:

items: {@b Melee:} The weapon deals additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus when the wielder lands a critical hit.
{@b Reach:} Oppurtunity attacks with this weapon are made at advantage.
{@b Thrown:} You deal an additional {@damage 1d4} damage when you hit a creature with a thrown weapon attack.
{@b Ranged:} You ignore the loading property of the weapon and its short and long range increases by a number of feet equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Fletcher I
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item woodcarver's tools|phb}.
you can spend one hour as part of a rest in order to create 20 pieces of arrows, bolts or darts.

optionalfeature.name: Primal Power
entries: You can regain spell slots with a combined level equal to half your ranger level whenever you finish a short rest.

optionalfeature.name: Wildlife Expert II
entries: You can communicate with beasts as if you are permanently under the effects of the spell {@spell speak with animals}.
You always have the {@spell find familiar} spell prepared, and it counts as a ranger spell for you.

optionalfeature.name: Mental Fortitude I
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition frightened}, {@condition charmed}, or magically being put to sleep.

optionalfeature.name: Skillful
entries: When you make an ability check that you are proficient in, you can add a bonus to it equal to your hunter's mark die. You must do so before you know the result of the roll.
You can use this ability twice, regaining expended uses on a long rest. If you run out of uses, you can instead expend a use of ranger's quarry in order to use this feature again.

optionalfeature.name: Primal Warrior I
entries: You can form a magical bond with up to two weapons of your choice whenever you finish a long rest.
When you make an attack with a bonded weapon, you can use your wisdom attack and damage rolls, and can use the weapon as your spellcasting focus.

optionalfeature.name: Fletcher II
entries: When you create ammunition as part of a rest, you can create a number of special ammunition as well. The amount of special ammunition you can create is equal to your proficiency bonus.
you can create the following types of special ammunition:

items: {@item dried leech|BMT}
{@item adamantine ammunition|XGE}.
{@item Arrow of Faerie Fire|AspysGuidetoInfinitum}.
{@item Unbreakable arrow|XGE}.
{@item walloping arrow|DMG}
{@item Arrow of Roping|AspysGuidetoInfinitum}
{@item winged ammunition|BMT}
{@item +1 ammunition}.
{@item Arrow of Returning|AspysGuidetoInfinitum}

entries: Once you create special ammunition, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
Any special ammunition left unused after your next long rest loses its magic and turns mundane.

optionalfeature.name: Primal Warrior II
entries: You can use your spell save DC in place of your weapon mastery DC.
You gain a +2 bonus to saving throws and damage rolls as long as you are concentrating on a spell.

optionalfeature.name: Primal Warrior III
entries: You can add your strength or dexterity modifier to your damage rolls with your ranger spells.

optionalfeature.name: Spellblade I
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can expend one spell slot to deal acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison or thunder damage to the creature, along with the attacks damage. The extra damage is a number of {@damage d10}'s equal to the level of the spell slot expended.

optionalfeature.name: Spellblade II
entries: You can concentrate on two spells as long as one of the spells improve the effectiveness of your weapon attacks (eg: swift quiver, holy weapon, Haste, bless, etc). If you are concentrating on multiple spells, you have disadvantage on constitution saving throws made in order to maintain concentration.

optionalfeature.name: Primal Warrior IV
entries: If you use your action to make a weapon attack, you can use your bonus action to cast a spell with a casting time of one action.
Your concentration can no longer be broken by damage.

optionalfeature.name: Mental Fortitude II
entries: You gain resistance to psychic damage. Additionally, you gain immunity to the {@condition frightened} and {@condition charmed} conditions.

optionalfeature.name: Mental Fortitude III
entries: You gain proficiency in intelligence or charisma saving throws (your choice).

optionalfeature.name: Mental Fortitude IV
entries: You have advantage on all intelligence, wisdom and charisma saving throws.

optionalfeature.name: Wildlife Expert III
entries: When you create a familiar with the {@spell find familiar} spell, it can take the from of any beast of CR 1/2 or lower.
Beasts or fey under your control gain a number of temporary hitpoints equal to your wisdom modifier + your ranger level whenever they are summoned or conjured.

optionalfeature.name: Wildlife Expert IV
entries: You can summon an additional creature whenever you use a spell that summons a single friendly creature.
Beasts or fey under your control can make an additional attack when they take the attack action.

optionalfeature.name: Nimble III
entries: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

optionalfeature.name: Nimble IV
entries: You always have the {@spell freedom of movement} spell prepared, and you can cast it once per day without expending a spell slot. Additionally, if you cast this spell on yourself, you can do so as a bonus action, rather than an action.

optionalfeature.name: Sturdy III
entries: You always have the {@spell stoneskin} spell prepared, and you can cast it once per day without expending a spell slot. Additionally, when you cast the spell on yourself, you gain a bonus to your constitution saving throws and armor class equal to your wisdom modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Sturdy IV
entries: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

optionalfeature.name: Poisoner II
entries: When you apply poison on your weapon/ammunition, it stays potent for 10 minutes, rather than 1. You can create two vials of {@item serpent venom} in addition to your other poisons whenever you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Herbalist II
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against poisons and disease. You can create two {@item greater healing potions} in addition to your other healing potions whenever you finish a long rest.
When improving your skill in the herbalist profession, the time required to do so is reduced by a quarter.

optionalfeature.name: Tenacious III
entries: If a creature lands a critical hit on you, you can use your reaction to turn that attack into a normal hit. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a use of ranger's quarry to do so.

optionalfeature.name: Tenacious IV
entries: You gain advantage on all saving throws when under a quarter of your hitpoints. Additionally, any healing you recieve while under a quarter of your hitpoints is doubled.

optionalfeature.name: Tenacious V
entries: When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. You can use this feature once, regaining expended uses on a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Resilient
entries: When you fail a saving throw, you can use your reaction to add a bonus to it equal to your hunter's mark die. You can use this feature twice, regaining all expended uses on a long rest. If you run out of uses of this feature, you can expend a use of ranger's quarry to use this feature again.

optionalfeature.name: Warrior I
entries: You learn an additional fighting style available to the ranger class.

optionalfeature.name: Combatant
entries: If you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack while under the benefit of flanking, your critical hit range is improved by one.

optionalfeature.name: Duellist
entries: You can make an additional attack when you take the attack action as long as all of them are targeting the same creature.

optionalfeature.name: Defender
entries: You impose and benefit from flanking a creature if it is within your attack range.
Your critical hit range is reduced to 16-20 for reaction attacks made with a melee weapon.
If you land a critical hit on an opportunity attack with a melee weapon, you can use the highest possible result on the damage die, rather than rolling for damage.

optionalfeature.name: Marksman
entries: You no longer suffer from disadvantage when making ranged attacks within 5 feet of a hostile creature.
When you hold your action to attack, you can make as many attacks as you would have on your turn, rather than just one.

optionalfeature.name: Hurler
entries: The range of your thrown weapons are doubled if you move atleast 10 feet before making the attack.

You can choose to treat a thrown weapon attack as a melee weapon attack (if using strength) or a ranged weapon attack (if using dexterity) for the purpose of benefitting from class and subclass features. This benefit does not extend to other ranger imbibements.
You can choose to gain disadvantage on your attack in order to lob two thrown weapons as part of the same attack. You roll attack and damage rolls seperately for both weapons.

optionalfeature.name: Deadeye
entries: When you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack, you can cause your attack to damage a second creature in one of the following ways, the damage dealt through this feature is always half of the original attack's damage.

items: {@b Blowthrough:} You can make an attack roll against a creature directly behind your attack's point of entry within your attack's range.
{@b Ricochet:} You can make an attack roll against a creature within 15 feet of the original target.
These additional attacks only deal damage and do not inflict any conditions or additional effects.

optionalfeature.name: Primal Mark
entries: If you run out of uses of ranger's quarry, you can expend a spell slot as a bonus action in order to regain a number of ranger's quarry uses equal to the level of the spell slot expended.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Fletcher III
entries: The following options are added to the types of special ammunition that you can create.

items: {@item Arrow of Screaming|AspysGuidetoInfinitum}
{@item Bloodseeker Ammunition|BMT}
