row: You have talons that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

You have hooves that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.
Primary race with increased carry capacity

Your claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you can deal slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d4} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

You have a fanged maw that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with it, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

Your horns are natural melee weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

You can use your head and horns to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, you deal bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

You can use your claws to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.
You are proficient in the {@skill Stealth} skill. In addition, without squeezing, you can move through and stop in a space large enough for a Small creature.

If you replace a race with this lineage, you can keep the following elements of that race: any skill proficiencies you gained from it and any climbing, flying, or swimming speed you gained from it. If you don't keep any of those elements or you choose this lineage at character creation, you gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.
Dhampir, hexblood or reborn primary race; ask DM before picking this trait

When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, you can make the check with advantage. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

You can use your understanding of creative diplomacy or intimidation to guide a conversation in your favor. When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check, you can do so with advantage. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check or an ability check using {@item thieves' tools|PHB}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
When you make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) or Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
You have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) and Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks.

You have advantage on Strength-based ability checks and Strength saving throws. In addition, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.
When you make an Intelligence ({@skill History}) check or an ability check using {@item calligrapher's supplies|PHB}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

Whenever you make an Intelligence ({@skill History}) check related to magic items, alchemical objects, or technological devices, you can add twice your proficiency bonus, instead of any proficiency bonus you normally apply.
When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
You have proficiency in the {@skill Athletics} skill, and you count as one size larger when determining your carrying weight and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.
When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check or any ability check involving {@item navigator's tools|PHB}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check or an ability check using an {@item herbalism kit|phb}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check or an ability check involving {@item brewer's supplies|PHB} or {@item cook's utensils|PHB}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) or Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

When you make a Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) or an ability check involving {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check

When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check or any ability check to operate or maintain a {@filter land vehicle|items|source=phb;dmg|miscellaneous=mundane|type=vehicle (land)}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

Thanks to your supernaturally good memory, you have proficiency in two skills of your choice. Moreover, when you make an ability check using any skill in which you have proficiency, you can give yourself advantage on the check before rolling the {@dice d20}. You can give yourself advantage in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Thanks to your sensitive trunk, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}), Wisdom ({@skill Survival}), and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks that involve smell.
You always know which direction is north, and you have advantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check you make to navigate or track.

You temporarily remember glimpses of the past, perhaps faded memories from ages ago or a previous life. When you make an ability check that uses a skill, you can roll a {@dice d6} immediately after seeing the number on the {@dice d20} and add the number on the {@dice d6} to the check. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

You are proficient in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Performance}, or {@skill Sleight of Hand}. You are also proficient with one {@book tool|phb|5|tools} of your choice. Whenever you make an ability check with the chosen skill or tool, roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the check's total.

You gain proficiency in {@skill Stealth} checks. You can walk on two feet or four without impediment and can move through non-magical difficult terrain or any creature's space without penalty to your movement.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill persuasion} skill and  can roll the check with advantage once per short or long rest.
You are encased in thin metal or some other durable material. While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier

You have tough, scaly skin. When you aren't wearing armor, your base AC is 12 + Constitution modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

You have thick, leathery skin. When you aren't wearing armor, your base AC is 13 + Dexterity modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

shell provides you a base AC of 17 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can't wear light, medium, or heavy armor, but if you are using a shield, you can apply the shield's bonus as normal.
You have resistance to necrotic and radiant damage
You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition charmed} condition on yourself. and magic can't put you to sleep.
A primary race with fey ancestry

You have resistance to poison damage and immunity to disease, and you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition paralyzed} or {@condition poisoned}. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.

Starting at 5th level, as an action, you can channel your draconic energy to protect yourself. For 1 minute, you become immune to the damage type associated with your Chromatic Ancestry. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition charmed} or {@condition stunned} condition on yourself.
You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition poisoned} condition on yourself. You also have resistance to poison damage.
You gain resistance to necrotic damage.
You gain resistance to fire damage.
You gain resistance to acid damage.
You gain resistance to lightning damage.
You have advantage on saving throws involving poison damage and disease.
You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition frightened}.
You have resistance to psychic damage.

You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition frightened} condition on yourself. When you fail a saving throw to avoid or end the {@condition frightened} condition on yourself, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you succeed on a saving throw in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
Your blood has the strange property of being thicker. You are resistant to Poison Damage and Immune to Diseases.
You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.
You have advantage on saving throws against poison and disease, and you have resistance against poison damage. You can also eat rotten food without any ill effects.
You have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and you have resistance to cold damage.
You have advantage on checks and saving throws against being moved or knocked {@condition prone}.
As an action, you may change your size from medium to large or vice versa. Additionally, you have advantage against any spells or effects that would alter your form against your will.

As an action, you can touch a creature and roll a number of d4s equal to your proficiency bonus. The creature regains a number of hit points equal to the total rolled. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a long rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness.

If the {@spell mending} spell is cast on you, you can spend a Hit Die, roll it, and regain a number of hit points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). In addition, your creator designed you to benefit from several spells that preserve life but that normally don't affect Constructs: {@spell cure wounds}, {@spell healing word}, {@spell mass cure wounds}, {@spell mass healing word}, and {@spell spare the dying}.
When you take a long rest, you spend at least 6 hours in an inactive, motionless state, instead of sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but you remain conscious.
When you make a melee attack on your turn, your reach for it is 5 feet greater than usual
You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

If you move at least 30 feet straight toward a target and then hit it with a melee weapon attack on the same turn, you can immediately follow that attack with a bonus action, making one attack against the target with your hooves.

You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push or drag. In addition, any climb that requires hands and feet is especially difficult for you because of your equine legs. When you make such a climb, each foot of movement costs you 4 extra feet, instead of the normal 1 extra foot.
You have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. In addition, at 3rd level, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.

row.name: Vampiric Bite
entries: Your fanged bite is a natural weapon, which counts as a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient. You add your Constitution modifier, instead of your Strength modifier, to the attack and damage rolls when you attack with this bite. It deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage on a hit. While you are missing half or more of your hit points, you have advantage on attack rolls you make with this bite.
When you attack with this bite and hit a creature that isn't a Construct or an Undead, you can empower yourself in one of the following ways of your choice:

items: You regain hit points equal to the piercing damage dealt by the bite.
You gain a bonus to the next ability check or attack roll you make; the bonus equals the piercing damage dealt by the bite

entries: You can empower yourself with this bite a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

row.name: Draconic Ancestry
entries: You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

row: You can send telepathic messages to any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand these messages, but it must be able to understand at least one language to comprehend them.

When you take damage from a creature in range of a weapon you are wielding, you can use your reaction to make an attack with the weapon against that creature. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

As a bonus action, you gain {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} ith a range of 60 feet for 10 minutes. You must be on a stone surface or touching a stone surface to use this {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB}. The stone can be natural or worked. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Your hitpoint maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level.

Aquatic animals have an extraordinary affinity with your people. You can communicate simple ideas to any Beast that has a swimming speed. It can understand your words, though you have no special ability to understand it in return.
You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.

You have the ability to communicate in a limited manner with Beasts, Plants, and vegetation. They can understand the meaning of your words, though you have no special ability to understand them in return. You have advantage on all Charisma checks you make to influence them.
You can hold your breath indefinitely while you're not {@condition incapacitated}.
You can move across {@quickref difficult terrain||3} made of earth or stone without expending extra movement.

Your psychic connection to the Astral Plane enables you to mystically access a spark of divine power, which you can channel through your weapons. When you hit a target with a {@filter simple or martial weapon|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=martial weapon;simple weapon}, you can cause the target to take extra force damage equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, but you can use it no more than once per turn. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

row.name: Clockwork Toy
entries: This toy is a clockwork animal, monster, or person, such as a frog, mouse, bird, dragon, or soldier. When placed on the ground, the toy moves 5 feet across the ground on each of your turns in a random direction. It makes noises as appropriate to the creature it represents.

row.name: Fire Starter
entries: The device produces a miniature flame, which you can use to light a candle, torch, or campfire. Using the device requires your action.

row.name: Music Box
entries: When opened, this music box plays a single song at a moderate volume. The box stops playing when it reaches the song's end or when it is closed.

row: When you damage a creature with an attack or a spell and the creature's size is larger than yours, you can cause the attack or spell to deal extra damage to the creature. The extra damage equals your proficiency bonus. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest, and you can use it no more than once per turn.

Starting at character level 5, you can change your size to lrge as a bonus action if you're in a big enough space. This transformation lasts for 10 minutes or until you end it (no ction required). For tht duration, you have advantage on Strength checks, and your speed increases by 10 feet. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
As a bonus action, you can use your feet to manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, or pick up or set down a Tiny object.

When you fall at least 10 feet above the ground, you can use your reaction to extend your skin membranes to glide horizontally a number of feet equal to your walking speed, and you take 0 damage from the fall. You determine the direction of the glide.

The magic that runs in your veins heightens your natural defenses. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to roll a {@dice d6}. Add your proficiency bonus to the number rolled, and reduce the damage you take by an amount equal to that total (minimum of 0 damage). You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit.

You can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet of you. The creature understands you only if the two of you share a language. You can speak telepathically in this way to one creature at a time.
You can attempt to hide even when you are obscured only by a creature that is at least one size larger than you.
Ability checks made to track you have disadvantage, and you can move across {@quickref difficult terrain||3} made of nonmagical plants and undergrowth without expending extra movement.

When you fail a Dexterity saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll a {@dice d4} and add it to the save, potentially turning the failure into a success. You can't use this reaction if you're {@condition prone} or your speed is 0.

row.name: Eerie Token
entries: As a bonus action, you can harmlessly remove a lock of your hair, one of your nails, or one of your teeth. This token is imbued with magic until you finish a long rest. While the token is imbued in this way, you can take these actions:

items.name: Telepathic Message
items.entry: As an action, you can send a telepathic message to the creature holding or carrying the token, as long as you are within 10 miles of it. The message can contain up to twenty-five words.

items.name: Remote Viewing
items.entry: If you are within 10 miles of the token, you can enter a trance as an action. The trance lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or are {@condition incapacitated}. During this trance, you can see and hear from the token as if you were located where it is. While you are using your senses at the token's location, you are {@condition blinded} and {@condition deafened} in regard to your own surroundings. When the trance ends, the token is harmlessly destroyed.

entries: Once you create a token using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, at which point your missing part regrows.

row.name: Fey Gift
entries: You can use this trait to take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action, and you can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Starting at 3rd level, choose one of the options below each time you take the {@action Help} action with this trait:

items.name: Hospitality
items.entry: You and the creature you help each gain a number of temporary hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your proficiency bonus.

items.name: Passage
items.entry: You and the creature you help each increase your walking speeds by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Spite
items.entry: Until the start of your next turn, the first time the creature you help hits a target with an attack roll, that target has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes within the next minute.

row: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see, provided the creature is within a number of feet of you equal to 10 times your level. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic utterances, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language.When you're using this trait to speak telepathically to a creature, you can use your action to give that creature the ability to speak telepathically with you for 1 hour or until you end this effect as an action. To use this ability, the creature must be able to see you and must be within this trait's range. You can give this ability to only one creature at a time; giving it to a creature takes it away from another creature who has it.

Kalashtar sleep, but they don't connect to the plane of dreams as other creatures do. Instead, their minds draw from the memories of their otherworldly spirit while they sleep. As such, you are immune to spells and other magical effects that require you to dream, like {@spell dream}, but not to spells and other magical effects that put you to sleep, like {@spell sleep}.

You have an extraordinary ability to fluster creatures. As a bonus action, you can unleash a string of provoking words at a creature within 60 feet of yourself that can hear and understand you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn. The DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (choose when you select this race).You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
When you copy writing or craftwork produced by yourself or someone else, you have advantage on any ability checks you make to produce an exact duplicate.

You can accurately mimic sounds you have heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds you make can tell they are imitations only with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against a DC of 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

row.name: Kobold Legacy
entries: Kobold's connections to dragons can manifest in unpredictable ways in an individual kobold. Choose one of the following legacy options for your kobold.

items.name: Craftiness
items.entry: You have proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Sleight of Hand}, or {@skill Survival}.

items.name: Defiance
items.entry: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition frightened} condition on yourself.

row: As a bonus action, you can let out an especially menacing roar. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. The DC of the save equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
You can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes at a time.

You can throw yourself into a feeding frenzy. As a bonus action, you can make a special attack with your Bite. If the attack hits, it deals its normal damage, and you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

You can grasp things with your trunk, and you can use it as a snorkel. It has a reach of 5 feet, and it can lift a number of pounds equal to five times your Strength score. You can use it to do the following simple tasks: lift, drop, hold, push, or pull an object or a creature; open or close a door or a container; grapple someone; or make an unarmed strike. Your DM might allow other simple tasks to be added to that list of options. You can grasp things with your trunk, and you can use it as a snorkel. It has a reach of 5 feet, and it can lift a number of pounds equal to five times your Strength score. You can use it to do the following simple tasks: lift, drop, hold, push, or pull an object or a creature; open or close a door or a container; grapple someone; or make an unarmed strike. Your DM might allow other simple tasks to be added to that list of options.
Immediately after you use the {@action Dash} action on your turn and move at least 20 feet, you can make one melee attack with your horns as a bonus action.

You can take the {@action Dash} action as a bonus action. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. Whenever you use this trait, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

Whenever you make a long or high jump, you can roll a {@dice d8} and add the number rolled to the number of feet you cover, even when making a standing jump. This extra distance costs movement as normal.

Your reflexes and agility allow you to move with a burst of speed. When you move on your turn in combat, you can double your speed until the end of the turn. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you move 0 feet on one of your turns.

You can withdraw into your shell as an action. Until you emerge, you gain a +4 bonus to your AC, and you have advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws. While in your shell, you are {@condition prone}, your speed is 0 and can't increase, you have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws, you can't take reactions, and the only action you can take is a bonus action to emerge from your shell.
By absorbing oxygen through your skin, you can breathe underwater for up to 1 hour. Once you've reached that limit, you can't use this trait again until you finish a long rest.

The black blood that is a sign of your people's connection to That-Which-Endures boosts your natural healing. When you roll a 1 or 2 on any Hit Die you spend at the end of a short rest, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

You can telepathically speak to any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathy, but it must be able to understand at least one language. This process of communication is slow and limited, allowing you to transmit and receive only simple ideas and straightforward concepts.
You can walk on two feet or four without impediment and can move through any creature's space without penalty to your movement.
While you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, you do not take damage from falling and can move upto 2 feet for every 1 foot that you descend.

As a reaction to melee attack against you within 5 feet, you may impale the attacker on the needles on your back. The attacker takes damage equal to your Constitution modifier + half your level (rounded down).

When a creature attacks you, you can use a reaction to force the creature to make a Wisdom save (DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma Modifier). If the being is sentient, it may redirect the attack or make it against you with disadvanatage. You regain use of this feature after a short rest.

You have a platform built into your chassis. While large, a small creature can ride on the platform without squeezing. To make a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of you, they must use spears, a similar polearm or weapons with reach.

row.name: Integrated Protection
entries: Your body has built-in defensive layers, which can be enhanced with armor:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

You can don only armor with which you have proficiency. To don armor other than a shield, you must incorporate it into your body over the course of 1 hour, during which you remain in contact with the armor. To doff armor, you must spend 1 hour removing it. You can rest while donning or doffing armor in this way.
While you live, the armor incorporated into your body can't be removed against your will.

row: Your eyes briefly become pools of darkness, and ghostly, flightless wings sprout from your back temporarily. Creatures other than your allies within 10 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or become {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. Until the transformation ends, once on each of your turns, you can deal extra necrotic damage to one target when you deal damage to it with an attack or a spell. The extra damage equals your proficiency bonus.

Searing light temporarily radiates from your eyes and mouth. For the duration, you shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet, and at the end of each of your turns, each creature within 10 feet of you takes radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus. Until the transformation ends, once on each of your turns, you can deal extra radiant damage to one target when you deal damage to it with an attack or a spell. The extra damage equals your proficiency bonus.
Aasimar primary race; no other celestial revelation

Two luminous, spectral wings sprout from your back temporarily. Until the transformation ends, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed, and once on each of your turns, you can deal extra radiant damage to one target when you deal damage to it with an attack or a spell. The extra damage equals your proficiency bonus.
Aasimar primary race; no other celestial revelation

As a bonus action, you can magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

You can add a {@dice d4} to one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make, and you can do so after seeing the {@dice d20} roll but before the effects of the roll are resolved. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
If you hit a creature with an attack roll, the creature takes an extra {@damage 2d6}damage if it hasn't taken a turn yet in the current combat.

As an action, you can change your appearance and your voice. You determine the specifics of the changes, including your coloration, hair length, and sex. You can also adjust your height and weight, but not so much that your size changes. You can make yourself appear as a member of another race, though none of your game statistics change. You can't duplicate the appearance of a creature you've never seen, and you must adopt a form that has the same basic arrangement of limbs that you have. Your clothing and equipment aren't changed by this trait. You stay in the new form until you use an action to revert to your true form or until you die.
You gain one {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.
You have advantage on intelligence, wisdom and charisma saving throws against spells.

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of magical energy in a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide or a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d10} damage of the type associated with your Chromatic Ancestry. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. This damage increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d10}), 11th level ({@dice 3d10}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d10}).You can use your Breath Weapon a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Starting at 5th level, you can use a bonus action to manifest spectral wings on your body. These wings last for 1 minute. For the duration, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

row.name: Metallic Breath Weapon
entries: At 5th level, you gain a second breath weapon. When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation in a 15-foot cone. The save DC for this breath is 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. Whenever you use this trait, choose one:

items.name: Enervating Breath
entries: Each creature in the cone must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition incapacitated} until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Repulsion Breath
entries: Each creature in the cone must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 20 feet away from you and be knocked {@condition prone}.
Once you use your Metallic Breath Weapon, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

row.name: Fey Step
entries: As a bonus action, you can magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
When you reach 3rd level, your Fey Step gains an additional effect based on your season; if the effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier:
{@i Choose your eladrin's season: autumn, winter, spring, or summer. When finishing a long rest, you can change your season. See the "Info" tab for more information.}

items.name: Autumn
items.entry: Immediately after you use your Fey Step, up to two creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute, or until you or your companions deal any damage to it.

items.name: Winter
items.entry: When you use your Fey Step, one creature of your choice that you can see within 5 feet of you before you teleport must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Spring
items.entry: When you use your Fey Step, you can touch one willing creature within 5 feet of you. That creature then teleports instead of you, appearing in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you.

items.name: Summer
items.entry: Immediately after you use your Fey Step, each creature of your choice that you can see within 5 feet of you takes fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 damage).

row: As a bonus action, you can magically turn {@condition invisible} until the start of your next turn or until you attack, make a damage roll, or force someone to make a saving throw. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

You have a mystical connection to firearms that traces back to the gods of the giff, who delighted in such weapons. You have proficiency with all firearms and ignore the loading property of any firearm. In addition, attacking at long range with a firearm doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack roll.
You have advantage on intelligence, wisdom and charisma saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
You can take the {@action Disengage} or {@action Hide} action as a bonus action on each of your turns.
As a bonus action, you can magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can also deal {@damage 1d10} fire damage to that target.
Goliath primary race, no other giant's ancestry
When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can also deal {@damage 1d6} cold damage to that target and reduce its speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
Goliath primary race, no other giant's ancestry
When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can give that target the {@condition prone} condition.
Goliath primary race, no other giant's ancestry
When you take damage, you can take a reaction to roll {@dice 1d12}. Add your constitution modifier to the number rolled and reduce the damage by that total.
Goliath primary race, no other giant's ancestry
When you take damage from a creature within 60 feet of you, you can take a reaction to deal {@damage 1d8} thunder damage to that creature.
Goliath primary race, no other giant's ancestry
When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.
You can attune to 1 additional item as long as one of the items you’re attuned to is a tattoo.
Leberi or Half-leberi primary race; Homebrew, ask DM
You can add your proficiency bonus to your initiative rolls.

As a bonus action, you can jump a number of feet equal to five times your proficiency bonus, without provoking opportunity attacks. You can use this trait only if your speed is greater than 0. You can use it a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

If you miss with an attack roll or fail an ability check or a saving throw, you can draw on your bonds of reciprocity to gain a bonus to the roll equal to the number of allies you can see within 30 feet of you (maximum bonus of +3). You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
You have advantage on wisdom saving throws.

As a bonus action, you let out a cry at your enemies within 10 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, you and your allies have advantage on attack rolls against any of those enemies who could hear you. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Depending on the circumstance of your birth you may have lost one or more senses to gain a boon granted as an eldritch invocation. This invocation must not have any prerequisites. You may lose Smell and Taste, Sight or Hearing.
Leberi or Half-leberi primary race; Homebrew, ask DM

You can take the {@action Dash} action as a bonus action. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.Whenever you use this trait, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

row.name: Deathless Nature
entries: You have escaped death, a fact represented by the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against disease and being {@condition poisoned}, and you have resistance to poison damage.
You have advantage on death saving throws.
You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a long rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in an inactive, motionless state, during which you retain consciousness.

row: You have advantage on saving throws against spells.

As a bonus action, you can magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.Starting at 3rd level, you also gain resistance to all damage when you teleport using this trait. The resistance lasts until the start of your next turn. During that time, you appear ghostly and translucent.

As a bonus action, you can assume a more bestial appearance. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you die, or until you revert to your normal appearance as a bonus action. When you shift, you gain temporary hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} + your level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point), and have a +1 bonus to your armor class. You can shift a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

As a bonus action, you can assume a more bestial appearance. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you die, or until you revert to your normal appearance as a bonus action. When you shift, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point). While shifted, you can use your elongated fangs to make an unarmed strike. If you hit with your fangs, you can deal piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike. You can shift a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

As a bonus action, you can assume a more bestial appearance. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you die, or until you revert to your normal appearance as a bonus action. When you shift, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point), and your walking speed increases by 10 feet. Additionally, you can move up to 10 feet as a reaction when a creature ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This reactive movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. You can shift a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

As a bonus action, you can assume a more bestial appearance. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you die, or until you revert to your normal appearance as a bonus action. When you shift, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point), and you have advantage on Wisdom checks, and no creature within 30 feet of you can make an attack roll with advantage against you unless you're {@condition incapacitated}. You can shift a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
You have advantage on all intelligence, wisdom and charisma saving throws.
Your mind's connection to the world around you strengthens your will. You have advantage on all wisdom and charisma saving throws.
You gain proficiency with Greataxes and Battleaxes and the 'heavy' property of a greataxe doesn't give you disadvantage on attack rolls. In addition, you gain the benefit of the {@feat Slasher} feat.
You have advantage on attack rolls against another creature if at least one of your allies isn't {@condition incapacitated} and is within 5 feet of it.

table.name: Major Arcana
table.caption: Tarot Cards (Any effect that forces a saving throw uses your Spell save DC)
rows: When you finish a long rest, choose upto Wisdom modifier number of creatures within sight. For 8 hrs when they fail an Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw they can roll a {@dice 1d100} and on a 91-100 the result becomes exactly what they would need to succeed.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to roll a Charisma saving throw. On a failure it must roll a {@dice 1d6} and reduce it from the first Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw it makes on a turn for one minute. The creature can attempt the Charisma saving throw again at the end of each of it's turns(the penalty effect does not apply to this save).
On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For 10 minutes, the creature gains +2 to Concentration saving throws, Intelligence saving throws and Intelligence checks.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to roll an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, it has disadvantage on all attack rolls and it's Intelligence checks are reduced by 5 for one minute. The creature can make the save again at the end of each of it's turns.
On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For 10 minutes, the creature gains +2 to Wisdom checks and Wisdom saving throws. It also has advantage on Perception and Insight checks for the duration.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to roll a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, one of it's Senses is suppressed and it's Wisdom checks are reduced by 5 for one minute. The creature can make the save again at the end of each of it's turns.

On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For 10 minutes, the creature gains +2 to Charisma checks and Charisma saving throws. Additionally when the creature regains hitpoints, both the creature and all of it's minions/summons regain 3 extra hitpoints.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to roll a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it cannot regain hitpoints and instead takes {@dice 1d6} Necrotic damage when it attempts to do so for one minute. Additionally it's Charisma checks are reduced by 5 for the same duration and it can make the save again at the end of each of it's turns.

On your turn, choose a number of creatures within 30ft equal to your proficiency bonus. They gain temporary hitpoints equal to your Cleric level and a Blessing die. Immediately afterwards they can use their reaction to move upto their movement speed without provoking attack of opportunity.

When a creature within 60ft of you starts it's turn, you force it to roll a Wisdom saving throw and on a failure it considers one creature you choose that it can see as it's mortal enemy for one minute. It spends it's turns focusing only on killing it's mortal enemy. The creature can make the save again at the start of each of it's turns.
When you roll initiative, give yourself and Wisdom modifier amount of creatures, a +2 bonus to the initiative roll.

On your turn, choose 3 creatures within 60ft. You can swap positions among those creatures and an unwilling creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Spell save DC to resist the effect.
On your turn, choose 2 creatures within 30ft. For one hour they gain 10ft movement speed, and they additionally gain +2 to AC and Saving throws when they are within 30ft of each other.
When a creature within 60ft fails a saving throw, choose another creature within 30ft of it to make the same saving throw and be subject to the same effect on a failure.
At the end of any creature's turn, choose one creature within 30ft of you. It interrupts the turn order to take one action before the start of the next creature's turn.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to roll an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, whenever the creature tries to cast a spell it rolls a {@dice 1d6} and on a 1-3 the spell fizzles, wasting both the action and the spell slot. The creature can make the save again at the start of each of it's turns.
On your turn, choose 2 creatures within 60ft and dispel both the {@condition frightened} and {@condition charmed} conditions from them.

When a creature within 60ft succeeds on a saving throw against an Enchantment spell or magical effect, you force the creature to reroll the save with a {@dice 1d4} penalty and use the resulting total. This effect cannot be applied on saves succeeded using legendary resistance.

On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For one hour, it gains +5 bonus to it's Stealth and Survival checks. Additionally, when there are no creatures within 15ft of it, it is lightly obscured and has advantage on saving throws it makes to avoid being {@condition frightened} or {@condition charmed} or to end those conditions on itself.

When a creature within 60ft starts it's turn, you force it to roll a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature must take {@action Dash|XPHB} and use all it's movement on it's turn to move away from all other creatures. If it cannot move, it must take {@action Dodge|XPHB} instead. This effect ends if the creature takes damage.
When a creature within 30ft is about to roll an Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw, you make the creature roll thrice and keep the highest result.
When a creature within 30ft is about to roll an Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw, you make the creature roll thrice and keep the lowest result.

When a creature within 30ft heals another creature, it also receives the same amount of healing. Alternatively, when a creature within 60ft deals damage to another creature, it also receives the same amount of damage on a failed Dexterity saving throw or half as much on a success.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to roll a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, choose one damage type and the creature loses any resistance to it for one minute. Once per turn when the creature takes damage of the same type during this one minute, it takes additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For one minute, the creature gains resistance to all damage types until the end of it's next turn when it ends it's turn without making an attack, casting a spell or moving.

When a creature within 60ft starts it's turn, you force it to roll a Wisdom saving throw and on a failure it is {@condition restrained} in it's space by spectral chains for one minute. While it is {@condition restrained}, it cannot be moved by any means. The creature can make the save again at the end of each of it's turns.
When a creature within 30ft drops to 0 hitpoints, it is immediately healed for half it's maximum hitpoints and end the {@condition prone} condition on it.
When a creature within 60ft takes damage, it takes additional {@dice 4d8} damage of the same type as the triggering damage.
On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For ten minutes, the creature can use their reaction to treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

When a creature within 60ft rolls damage, you force it to roll a {@dice 1d6}. On a 1 all the damage dice become the lowest value it can roll and on a 6 all the damage die become the highest value it can roll.

On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft and force it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is {@condition Restrained} by unbreakable red ropes and enters a delirious state for 10 minutes. While it is delirious it mumbles about it's deepest, darkest desires and requests for affection from other creatures, giving them advantage on all Charisma checks when interacting with it.
On your turn, choose 2 creatures within 30ft. The {@condition Restrained} and {@condition Paralyzed} conditions end on them, and they gain 10ft extra movement speed until the end of their next turn.

When you roll initiative, choose upto 2 creatures that you can see and force them to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they cannot move, take actions or reactions on their first turn of combat.

When a creature within 60ft takes damage that would put it at 25% of it's maximum hitpoints or less, the creature can instead drop to 1 hitpoint and gains temporary hitpoints equal to half it's maximum hitpoints. Additionally until the end of it's next turn it has advantage on all Attack rolls, Ability checks and Saving throws.

On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. It emits dim light upto 30ft away for one minute. It's allies that are in the dim light can reroll any healing die once and add +2 to each die's total. It's enemies that are in the dim light have disadvantage on Stealth checks.

When a creature within 60ft starts it's turn, you force it to roll a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is {@condition Incapacitated} for one minute as despair fills it's mind. The creature can make the save again at the start of each of it's turns.

On your turn, choose 2 creatures within 60ft and force them to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they are put under a psychedelic trip for one minute. For the duration they are {@condition dazed} and their movement speed is halved. Each creature can make the save again at the start of it's turn.
On your turn, you emit bright moonlight that reaches upto 60ft from yourself and dispel all illusions in the area. The {@condition invisible} condition also ends on all creatures within the area.

On your turn, you blast sunlight that reaches upto 60ft from yourself and banish magical darkness in the area. Creatures you choose that were hit by the sunlight regain hitpoints equal to your Cleric level.

When a creature within 60ft takes damage, you can force it to roll a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it is cursed for one minute. The first time it takes damage on a turn, it takes an extra {@dice 1d8} Necrotic damage and heals the creature dealing that damage for the same amount.

On your turn, choose a creature within 30ft. For one minute, when it fails an Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw it gains advantage on the next Attack roll, Ability check or Saving throw it makes. Additionally, when it rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20}, it can spend 2 of it's hitdie to roll again and take the new result.
When a creature within 60ft rolls a critical hit, it is judged for it's actions and it has vulnerability to all of the damage from the next attack that hits it within a minute.

When you finish a short rest, choose 3 creatures that you can see. These creatures can regain one spell slot whose level can be as high as your (proficiency bonus - 1), or they can regain one use of a class/subclass feature that recharges on a long rest.

On your turn, choose a creature within 60ft and force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure for one minute, anytime it rolls a 20 on the {@dice d20} it is turned into a 19 and anytime it rolls 1-4 on the {@dice d20} it is turned into a 5. The creature can make the save again at the end of it's turn.

action.name: Hasted Action
entries: Certain features grant you an additional action that you may use on your turn known as a Hasted Action. This action can be used only to take the {@action Attack} (one weapon attack each only), {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, {@action Hide}, or {@action Use an Object} action.

items: A dazed creature can move or take one action on your turn, not both. You also can't take a Bonus action or a Reaction.
A silenced creature cannot speak, including performing the verbal component of a spell.

object.name: Eldritch Cannon, Shock Mortar

hp.special: equal to five times your artificer level

entries: {@note Created by the {@subclassFeature Eldritch Cannon|Artificer|TCE|Cannoneer|tct|3} subclass feature.}

actionEntries.name: Shock Mortar
entries: Choose a point within 30 feet. Creatures 10 feet around that point must make a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d8} Thunder damage.

object.name: Eldritch Cannon, Beacon Lenser

hp.special: equal to five times your artificer level

entries: {@note Created by the {@subclassFeature Eldritch Cannon|Artificer|DRK|Cannoneer|tct|3} subclass feature.}

actionEntries.name: Shock Mortar
entries: The cannon projects a beacon 20 feet long, creatures in its path must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 2d8} radiant damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

race.name: Warforged

entries.name: Age
entries: A typical warforged is between two and thirty years old. The maximum warforged lifespan remains a mystery; so far, warforged have shown no signs of deterioration due to age. You are immune to magical aging effects.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Most warforged take comfort in order and discipline, tending toward law and neutrality. But some have absorbed the morality, or lack thereof, of the beings with which they served.

entries.name: Size
entries: Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Constructed Resilience
entries: You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition poisoned}, and you have resistance to poison damage.
You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
You are immune to disease.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

entries.name: Sentry's Rest
entries: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn't render you {@condition unconscious}, and you can see and hear as normal.

entries.name: Integrated Protection
entries: Your body has built-in defensive layers, which can be enhanced with armour:

items: You can don only armour with which you have proficiency. To don armour other than a shield, you must incorporate it into your body over the course of 1 hour, during which you remain in contact with the armour. To doff armour, you must spend 1 hour removing it. You can rest while donning or doffing armour in this way.
While you live, the armour incorporated into your body can't be removed against your will.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice.
In addition to these features, a warforged can support an additional feature in the form of an upgrade.

entries.name: Adaptive Plating
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.

entries.name: Battle Platform (Juggernaut only)
entries: You have a platform built into your chassis. While large, a small creature can ride on the platform without squeezing. To make a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of you, they must use spears, a similar polearm or weapons with reach.

entries.name: Nightvision
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Steadfast
entries: You have advantage on checks and saving throws made against being moved or knocked {@condition prone}.

entries.name: Specialized Design
entries: You gain one skill proficiency and one tool proficiency of your choice.

entries.name: Age
entries: A typical Vermkin reaches adulthood at age 16 and lives up to 100 years.

entries.name: Size
entries: Your size is Small.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You speak common and one other language.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You discern colors in that darkness as shades of gray.

entries.name: Scurry
entries: You can walk on two feet or four without impediment and can move through any creature's space without penalty to your movement.

entries.name: Age
entries: A Leberi grows to be a teen at around the same age as humans though they age slower afterwards, living to be around 130 years old though some live upto 150 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: A Leberi’s concerns tend to start and end with themselves and those of close relation when in Leberi Society, Staying neutral most of the time. When taken out of their element though, they may align extremely in any direction.

entries.name: Size
entries: Leberi Tend to be a little taller than humans on average and weigh a little less. Your size is Medium

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Pungent Blood
entries: Your blood has the strange property of being thicker. You are resistant to Poison Damage and Immune to Diseases.

entries.name: Natural Escaladers
entries: Your long, warped and rubbery fingers allow for a firmer grip granting you a climbing speed of 20 feet

entries.name: Sensory Sacrifice
entries: Depending on the circumstance of your birth you may have lost one or more senses to gain a boon granted as an eldritch invocation. This invocation must not have any prerequisites. You may lose Smell and Taste, Sight or Hearing.

entries.name: Language
entries: You speak Liberian and 1 language of your choice.

entries.name: Leberi (Gelas'Bat)
entries: Leberi Mainlanders found deep within the jungles of Liberia. Despite looking humanoid, they display many features found in reptiles, fish or even frogs.
Gelas'Bat refers to the ####

entries.name: Age
entries: Half-Leberi grow into their teens the same time humans do and possess some facet of their Leberi Longevity living to be around 110 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Fiercely argumentative, the Leberi tend to sit anywhere in terms of alignment except on the fence.

entries.name: Size
entries: Half Leberi are aren't too dissimilar from humans in body proportion, though they tend to be more lean. Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Sour Blood
entries: You have advantage against saving throws involving poison damage and Disease.

entries.name: Seabound
entries: Swimming comes naturally to you. You gain a swim speed of 30 feet and while swimming, you may {@action dash} with a bonus action.

entries.name: Skilled Artisan
entries: You become proficient in any one skill and either one set of tools or one weapon.

entries.name: Otherworldly Trace
entries: You can attune to 1 additional item as long as one of the items you’re attuned to is a tattoo.

entries.name: Language
entries: Common, Leberi and one other language.

entries.name: Half-Leberi
entries: The discovery of the Half-Leberi coincides with the discovery of the Liberian Isles in the Year 1139 of the 11th Era, when the Biltian explorer Pensacura Menastorn made landfall on the isle of Cetu. They were found to be in tribes located on many of Liberian Isles as well as the coast on the mainland. They were noted to be a convival, lively and free spirited folk with the elders being generally a lax but jovial people while the young are ebullient and adventurous. This picture of leberi life was sadly a brief one, with colonization efforts by the three empires reducing the people to mainly a life of servitude.

Half-Leberi became the term of use after the Leberi were discovered on the mainland of Liberia. Half-Leberi were theorized to be either the result of ancient human interaction with the mainland or an adaptation to life away from it on the isles. They are Human-like in appearance with the exception of saggy skin, round beady eyes, better height and scale like patches on parts of their body.

race.name: Custom Ancestry
entries: Instead of choosing one of the game's races for your character at 1st level, you can choose different traits depending on your own unique history, giving you full control over how your character's origin shaped them:
You can build your race through this link: {@link https://infinitum-wiki.netlify.app/custom_ancest.html}
You pick one of the races of which you have chosen a feature from as your primary race for the purposes of feat and feature prerequisites. You can only have one primary race.

items.name: Variable Trait; Darkvision
entries: You gain {@sense darkvision} with a range of 60 feet.

items.name: Variable Trait; Skill Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

entries.name: Super Specialization
entries: You gain one tool proficiency of your choice and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses those tools.

entries.name: Artifex
entries: Despite a warforged's prowess in combat, its role in combat is that of support. The frontlines were still largely manned by non-automatons. And when they begin to deplete they are replaced by the bakers, doctors and factory workers. It is in those dire times that the resistance to a warforged in the factory place was the least. Especially after the war, when some of the combat varieties could be more better put to use rebuilding the economy.

images.title: A Warforged Artifex sealing a Pyteli Box

entries.name: Propelled Gait
entries: Your walking speed improves by 5 feet.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries: A benefit to warforged design was its precision and reduced mass without the sacrifice to general capability. As such This design was made to handle more precise equipment like rifles and artillery with subroutines for close-quarters combat as well.

images.title: A Warforged Skirmisher charging into combat, Unkown theatre and time.

entries.name: Spell Databank
entries: You know one {@filter cantrip of your choice from the wizard spell list|spells|level=0|class=Wizard}. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it. In addition, Whenever you reach a level in a class which grants you the spellcasting feature, you may choose to know one additional spell from the spell list offered. After you choose this spell, you may not use this feature to learn another.

entries.name: Incatator
entries: Although much rarer due to the high production cost and rarity of resources to build it, A variety was produced to provide magical support for minor engagements. Equipped with a special mechanism that imparts its creators intelligence, it is able to manipulate the weave using it.

images.title: A Warforged Incatator simultaneously watching and incribing results of an experiment.

entries.name: Transformation Subroutine
entries: As an action, you may change your size from medium to large or vice versa. Additionally, you have advantage against any spells or effects that would alter your form against your will.

entries.name: Combat Patterns
entries: You are proficient in one martial melee weapon of your choice.

entries.name: Juggernaut
entries: The first role granted to warforged remained its most common role; as shock troops. This amounts to its simple design, cheaper parts and sheer tenacity. It became an integral part of many armies with many tactical maneuvres reliant on their functioning.

images.title: A Warforged Juggernaut rearming at The Battle of Eilonwie. 11E Year 877.

entries.name: Bright-eyed and Bushy-tailed
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill and can roll the check with advantage once per short or long rest.

entries.name: Keen Linguist
entries: You know common and two other languages of your choice. After hearing and seeing a minute of conversation in an unknown language, a softfur gains a small grasp of the spoken language can infer basic meanings.

entries.name: Button-Eyed
entries: When a creature attacks you, you can use a reaction to force the creature to make a Wisdom save (DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma Modifier). If the being is sentient, it may redirect the attack or make it against you with disadvanatage. You regain use of this feature after a short rest.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Softfurs are gregarious by nature, maybe even more so with those outside their communities. They tend to be good or neutral as a result.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries: You have advantage on attack rolls against another creature if at least one of your allies isn't {@condition incapacitated} and is within 5 feet of it.

entries.name: Vengeful Prick
entries: As a reaction to melee attack against you within 5 feet, you may impale the attacker on the needles on your back. The attacker takes damage equal to your Constitution modifier + half your level (rounded down).

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Pricklebacks live a belligerent life, equal parts working with or against each other depending on the tribe. Tending to chaotic as a result.

entries.name: Iron Gut
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against poison and disease, and you have resistance against poison damage. You can also eat rotten food without any ill effects.

entries.name: Nose for Trouble
entries: You have advantage on {@skill perception} checks made to hear or smell.

entries.name: Sneaky Scurry
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Stealth} checks. You can walk on two feet or four without impediment and can move through non-magical difficult terrain or any creature's space without penalty to your movement.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: A Longsnout's loyalty typically lies with himself and his immediate pack. Most are neutral, though a streak of them fall on the chaotic side.

entries.name: River Born
entries: You have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and you have resistance to cold damage.

entries.name: Masters of the Axe
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item greataxe|tct|Greataxes} and {@item Battleaxes|tct|Battleaxes} and the 'heavy' property of a greataxe doesn't give you disadvantage on attack rolls. In addition, you gain the benefit of the {@feat Slasher|tce} feat.

entries.name: Housecarving
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item woodcarver's tools|phb} or {@item carpenter's tools|phb}.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Dykentail society is structured and hierarchical, usually revolving around the river they were born near. They usually want what's best for their Damhaven, leaning them towards lawful and good.

entries.name: Swift Climbers
entries: You have a walking speed of 35 feet and a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

entries.name: Free Gliders
entries: While you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, you do not take damage from falling and can move upto 2 feet for every 1 foot that you descend.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Dreyfolk's chaotic nature lead them to live very independent lives, though few would wish harm upon others.

images.title: An illustration of a Dreyfolk bandit

The current resting place of the Circlet of Barbed Vision is unknown, but rumor has it that a spectral assassin known as {@creature Jourrael, the Caedogeist|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|the Inevitable End} seeks this relic.

It resonates with nearby musical tones. In the modern era, it is best known as the personal weapon of famed bard {@creature Scanlan Shorthalt|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}.

Legend holds that it was worn by Duana, High Priest of the {@deity The Dawnfather|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, when she was martyred in the Battle of Ghor Dranas in the final days of the {@book Calamity|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Calamity}. In more recent times, it was worn by {@creature Pike Trickfoot|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, a legendary cleric of the {@deity The Everlight|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, while fighting against {@book the Chroma Conclave|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Chroma Conclave} and {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}.

itemGroup.name: Pyremaul
entries: Forged from deep red iron, this massive hammer is set with a brilliant fire opal that shimmers with eternal flame. It is rumored to be currently wielded by {@book Grand Legate Phaestor, the fire giant ruler of Vulkanon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|6|fire giants}, somewhere beneath the {@book Cliffkeep Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Cliffkeep Mountains}.

itemGroup.name: Spire of Conflux
entries: A powerful relic passed down from generation to generation of Ashari leaders, the Spire of Conflux was lost over three centuries ago when Joran the Sea-Speaker, a respected leader of {@book the Water Ashari|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|The Ashari}, was devoured by a demon of the Abyss. It was rediscovered by the legendary druid {@creature Keyleth, Voice of the Tempest|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Keyleth of Zephrah, Voice of the Tempest}. However, rumors swirl that she is seeking another hero to wield it—one who can travel the land and do good in small ways as she once did.

itemGroup.name: Star Razor
entries: The thick, grooved blade of this shining silver {@item longsword|phb} is lined with etched runes that sparkle blue in the light. Star Razor—known also as Dwueth'var—was thought to have been destroyed or lost after the {@book Calamity|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Calamity}, but new rumors suggest that it might be wielded by a half-orc somewhere in {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount}.

Star Razor (Awakened)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn
Star Razor (Exalted)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn

itemGroup.name: Suude
entries: Exandria's most infamous drug, {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} is a glittering powder made from {@book residuum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|An Enchanting Export}. It was first developed by power-hungry archmages in the {@book Age of Arcanum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|Age of Arcanum} as an incense burned to enhance focus during ritual spellcasting. The secret to its refinement has been lost and rediscovered a variety of times since the {@book Calamity|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Calamity}, and many different types of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} have been developed by arcanists in search of ever-greater power. It has terrible addictive and mentally degenerative properties, even when used sparingly.

After burning {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} within a vessel and inhaling its fumes as an action, you take 22 ({@damage 4d10}) psychic damage and must make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you become {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour and fall {@condition unconscious} for 1 minute, or until you are shaken awake as an action. During this time, the world seems to move in slow motion, and your vision is twisted in kaleidoscopic colors—yet your focus is never distorted. If one dose of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, or more, is used within 1 hour of another, the DC of the Constitution saving throw is increased by 5 per additional dose. If you fail this save by 10 or more, you instantly drop to 0 hit points.

On a success, you gain the ability to use one of the following Metamagic options as a sorcerer for the next minute, requiring no sorcery points. The type of Metamagic you gain access to depends on the type of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, and once you use it, you can't use it again until you inhale {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} again.

{@item Suude (Brown)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Brown suude} allows you to use the {@optfeature Extended Spell|PHB} Metamagic option, {@item Suude (blue)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|blue suude} allows you to use {@optfeature Twinned Spell|PHB}, and {@item Suude (Brown)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|red suude} grants {@optfeature Distant Spell|PHB}.

Suude (Blue)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn
Suude (Red)|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn
